How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (775 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Adira" is an Arabic slang term used in Levantine queer culture to describe someone with a strong presence — someone powerful and accomplished.
  • It is also the name of a Berlin-based collective that curates events and club nights celebrating the diversity of queer Arab* culture.
  • Among the collective's events is the ADIRA Drag Festival, which celebrated its third edition in Berlin in late October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Adira" is an Arabic slang term used in Levantine queer culture to describe someone with a strong presence — someone powerful and accomplished.

It is also the name of a Berlin-based collective that curates events and club nights celebrating the diversity of queer Arab* culture. The asterisk signals the inclusion of non-Arab ethnic minorities and people with diverse identities and roots in Southwest Asia and North Africa.

Among the collective's events is the ADIRA Drag Festival, which celebrated its third edition in Berlin in late October.

This year's theme, "Who's Your Diva?!," brought together drag performers paying tribute to legendary figures from across the Eastern Mediterranean who have become queer icons — from Egyptian music legend Umm Kulthum to Turkish star Bülent Ersoy and Lebanese pop icon Haifa Wehbe.

Hassandra, co-founder of ADIRA and the ADIRA Drag Festival, was among the performers, taking on the persona of Lebanese pop star Elissa.

"It is very important for me to bring my Lebanese Arab identity and culture into what I do, because I think it's a very beautiful culture. And there's a lot of campy, glamorous, beautiful divas," Hassandra said.

According to recent reports, elissa's "whole discography is very romantic, raw, soft, kind of like very Adele vibes," Hassandra told DW ahead of the October 30 show. "However, her personality is known to be the extreme opposite. She's very feisty. Very blunt, very unfiltered. Not soft at all as a person.".

The star is also known for speaking out on political concerns in Lebanon. She has publicly voiced support for LGBTQ+ communities in the Middle East, while also frequently sparking controversy across the Arab world with her outspoken positions on other political issues.

Hassandra's ADIRA Drag Festival performance addresses this complexity, ultimately "tapping into her sort of controversial political opinions," the drag artist explained.

It has been revealed that this reflects one of the ideas Hassandra hopes to promote with the theme of this year's festival. "As queer people, we tend to idealize a lot of pop divas. But these pop divas are very imperfect in their nature," Hassandra noted. The show provides an opportunity to critically revisit these divas' legacy through a more critical lens.

"And this sort of critical lens can be taken into the outside world, as in: never follow anyone in life blindly. No one should follow any politician, any political party, any pop diva, any activist blindly.".

In a recent development, born in Beirut in 1994, Hassandra studied theater and stage acting at the Lebanese University before moving to Berlin in 2017. "I would say it was it was just a very sort of impulsive decision at the age of 22. I mean, there's no doubt that the economic situation was really bad in Lebanon and continued to become even worse," the artist remarked.

According to recent reports, in Berlin, Hassandra became increasingly involved in the city's independent art scene and queer nightlife. Drag emerged as another form of self-expression for the actor.

Through performances that combine theatrical intensity, political humor, grotesque aesthetics and moments of tenderness, Hassandra challenges conventional understandings of gender and identity.

Their work explores themes of home, nostalgia, displacement and queer Arab culture. These ideas are also central to ADIRA, which Hassandra founded in 2023 with Syrian-German DJ and cultural producer Zuher Jazmati, also known as xanax_attax.

Through panel discussions, performances and music events, ADIRA fosters collective participation and community-building.

As Islamophobia and homophobia rise alongside the far right, spaces like ADIRA offer a sense of belonging and support for Arab queer communities.

That sense of community has become even more vital following the deadly Islamist terrorist attack during Berlin's Christopher Street Day pride parade in July.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that in the aftermath, Hassandra felt caught between their different identities. As an Arab queer person, "you fall in this position where then you start receiving a lot of racism," they noted.

"And I think this is why it's important, for us queer Arabs, to say we are sad over what happened, but that we also reject any of the racism that comes from that," Hassandra said. "I think we [the Arab community] are being used in a lot of ways as a punching bag for a lot of things that are happening.".

Rather than allowing the attack to fuel hatred and racism, Hassandra said, "we should make Germany a safer place for everyone to live in."  "There's place for everyone. It's a huge country," they added.

The interview with Hassandra was conducted by Gönna Ketels.

In a recent development, ‘I don’t know. We still have a few hours before the match, and we’re still trying to get all the players fit.,’ Arteta noted.

Asked if Raya could still play, Arteta added: ‘Yes.’.

Kepa filled in for his countryman on Tuesday against Dortmund and will be ready to step in again on Sunday if called upon.

Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

Renee Slegers has left Arsenal by mutual consent after the club’s poor start to the Women’s Super League season.

The Gunners sit sixth in the table and are already 12 points off the pace set by Chelsea, having drawn all six of their league matches on home soil.

A goalless draw with West Ham last weekend has proved to be Slegers’ final match in charge.

Slegers took charge as interim head coach in October 2024 and was then given the permanent job three months later.

Recent findings suggest that that season ended in glory for Arsenal, who won their second Champions League title in May 2025. Earlier this year, the club won the inaugural FIFA Women’s Champions Cup.

However, results have dipped significantly this season and Arsenal have used the international break to make the change in head coach, with Slegers’ assistant Aaron D’Antino also leaving the club.

“It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renee, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here,” noted director of women’s football Clare Wheatley.

“In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural FIFA Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron.

Arsenal XI vs Man City: Confirmed team news and predicted lineup.

Arteta reveals Raya injury hope as Arsenal face crunch Man City clash.

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style.

“After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary.”.

Arsenal have won just three of their 11 matches in the WSL this season. Only two teams in the league have scored fewer goals.

A draw with Barcelona at the Nou Camp in the Women’s Champions League earlier this month was a positive result for Arsenal, who sit eighth of 18 teams in the competition.

Domestic results have not been good enough, though, and the search for a replacement will now begin.

“Renee is a wonderful person who has made a significant contribution to Arsenal, playing an integral role in some of the most historic achievements in the club’s history, including our Champions League and FIFA Champions Cup successes,” Arsenal CEO Richard Garlick remarked.

“Aaron also deserves special recognition for his service to Arsenal over many years, during which time he has helped us to win several titles.”.

Manchester United midfielder Carlos Baleba will not play again this year with Mauricio Pochettino revealing the full extent of his injury blow.

Asked for an enhancement on the Cameroon international, Pochettino revealed he would be sidelined for 10-12 weeks, dating back to when the injury first occurred.

That timescale rules him out of the entire festive period and possibly until the end of January.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

John Terry believes that Arsenal star David Raya is ‘100 per cent’ the best goalkeeper in world football at present.

Raya joined Arsenal on an initial loan deal from Brentford in August 2023 before his move was made permanent for £27 million the following year.

The 31-year-old was an integral part in Arsenal’s success last season, in which the team won the Premier League and reached the Champions League final, where they were beaten on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain.

Raya has continued that form this season to help Arsenal open up a six-point lead at the top of the table after 11 games, and Terry believes the Spaniard is without doubt the world’s best shotstopper.

‘You look at Raya, who they brought in, who knew he was that good?’ Terry noted in an interview with Rory Jennings.

It has been revealed that ‘He’s the best keeper in the world, 100 per cent. Catches crosses, dominates his box. Unbelievable with both feet. Really good.’.

Terry was also keen to praise the rest of Arsenal’s defence, and believes their current backline could go down as one of the best in Premier League history.

‘I think they’re annoyingly good, and I think if they get to the levels that I think they will and win back-to-back-to-back [titles], I think they have to be in the debate,’ he added.

‘Now, you can argue individually who’s better, this one or that one, but I think if they’ve got titles underneath them, then I think they have to be in the conversation as a collective and individually as well.’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Arsenal will look to showcase their defensive prowess against Manchester City on Sunday to put more distance between themselves and one of their main title rivals.

The aforementioned Raya was absent in midweek against Borussia Dortmund after sustaining a shoulder injury in the 2-2 draw with Newcastle United last weekend, but Arteta did not rule the Spaniard returning to face City.

‘We still have a few hours before the match, and we’re still trying to get all the players fit,’ Arteta remarked.

Asked if Raya could still play, Arteta added: ‘Yes.’.

By Jonathan O'Shea | 27 Nov 2026 10:50.

Two Serie A strugglers will meet in this week's Sunday lunchtime kickoff, as Udinese and Fiorentina vie for three precious points.

That tally separates the sides after 12 matchdays, with the hosts trailing behind their Viola visitors.

Having sacked Kosta Runjaic after an awful run of seven defeats from eight games, Udinese are still waiting to see an upturn since Paolo Zanetti took charge.

Zanetti started with a loss to relegation rivals Venezia before the international break, then saw his side fight scrap out a 1-1 draw with Bologna when they returned to action last week.

Against one of Serie A's form teams, that was a good result in isolation, but the Friulani still have just one league win so far - against newly promoted Monza, way back at the end of August.

Since then, their season has unravelled completely, and picking up two points from 10 matches has left them stuck inside the drop zone.

Now heading back to Udine, the Bianconeri have already equalled their worst home record at this stage of a top-flight campaign, and they are at the moment on a run of five straight defeats at Bluenergy Stadium.

Perhaps the only positive omens are that they comfortably won this equivalent fixture last season, and that Fiorentina are also in freefall.

It was a tale of two substantial home wins when the pair met last term, with the Friuli club responding to a 5-1 loss in Florence by winning 3-0 a few weeks later.

This time, Fiorentina will head north in a similar state of distress to Udinese, having lost once again on Monday night.

Failing to build on a promising draw against Juventus, the Viola sunk to a 3-0 defeat in Monza, leaving them 16th in the Serie A table and just one point above the drop zone.

Making their worst start since 2001, they have now lost seven of their first 12 fixtures and are yet to keep a clean sheet.

In fact, Fiorentina have conceded at least twice in all of the last seven, as Paolo Vanoli struggles to pull off the same salvage job he managed last term.

Vanoli was rehired earlier this season, but after recently sandwiching an away win over Sassuolo with a pair of home draws, Monday's meltdown has sent Fiorentina fans even deeper into despair.

Udinese boss Zanetti is still missing Nicolo Bertola, who recently joined Idrissa Gueye on the sidelines, while last season's top scorer Keinan Davis is a doubt.

The latter has been struggling with an adductor problem, and the Friulani's forwards have only contributed three league goals so far.

Sources indicate that at least Nicolo Zaniolo seems to be finding some form, with two in his last three appearances - as many as across the previous 28. Zaniolo once spent a fruitless loan spell at Fiorentina, but he has previously scored twice against the Viola in Serie A.

Meanwhile, the away side have two players on four goals - Argentine pair Mateo Pellegrino and Franco Mastantuono.

They should both feature in the final third, possibly alongside Alieu Njie, who overcame a minor thigh injury to appear from the bench against Monza.

However, Vanoli is still without Fabiano Parisi and Marin Pongracic, while Brazilian defender Viery has just been ruled out for the next month.

Udinese possible starting lineup:.

Okoye; Abankwah, Palma, Solet; Vojvoda, Karlstrom, Piotrowski, Kamara; Lovric, Ekkelenkamp; Zaniolo.

Fiorentina possible starting lineup:.

De Gea; Jimenez, Dragusin, Ranieri, Mario; Ndour, Fagioli, Oulai; Mastantuono, Pellegrino, Njie.

Despite changing coaches, neither side can keep the back door shut, as only Sassuolo have conceded more goals in Serie A.

So, they should both find the net in a tense, scrappy match, which Fiorentina will win thanks to their stronger attack.

#164903. From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated

📅 26 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1055 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1055 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.
  • But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?
  • It has been revealed that the smell of rotten food can make us recoil.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.

But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

It has been revealed that the smell of rotten food can make us recoil. Certain sexual practices can provoke a similar reaction. And in today's polarized political climate, even political opponents can become objects of disgust.

Recent findings suggest that psychologists have long investigated whether sensitivity to disgust helps explain political beliefs. A review of 24 studies found that people who reported being more easily disgusted tended to hold more socially conservative views.

One explanation begins with evolution.

"We think that it evolved in part to reduce exposure to things that could make you sick," psychologist Yoel Inbar, of the University of British Columbia in Canada, told DW.

But disgust is not a single emotion. The Three-Domain Disgust Scale, developed in 2009, distinguishes three types:.

One theory is that people who are especially wary of germs and disease may also prefer traditional social rules.

Inbar explains that avoiding potential sources of infection can also mean missing out on newly introduced experiences.

"Some people are more on the cautious conservative side, and some people are more on the exploring risk-taking side when it comes to pathogen exposure," he remarked.

Industry observers note that indeed, the language of contamination also appears in political rhetoric. During his 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump repeatedly described immigrants as "poisoning the blood of our country." Trump has also described himself as a "germaphobe.".

Inbar acknowledges that the evidence linking sensitivity to disgust with conservative political beliefs remains uncertain.

"We have hypotheses. I don't know that we have as strong of evidence as I would like," Inbar stated.

Disgust is not exclusively conservative. And what people find revolting can depend on their values.

A 2020 study titled "Is Disgust a "Conservative" Emotion?" found that liberals and conservatives were disgusted by different things.

Conservatives, generally aligned with the Republicans in US politics, reported greater disgust at examples involving sexual behaviors and drug use, while liberals, generally aligned with the Democrats, reported greater disgust at animal abuse and environmental pollution.

However, when asked how easily disgusted they were in general, there was no clear difference across the political spectrum.

Some early studies suggested conservatives demonstrated stronger physical reactions to frightening or disgusting images, measured partly through changes in sweating.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But subsequent research, including a 2020 study by political psychologist Bert Bakker at the University of Amsterdam, struggled to reproduce those findings.

Studies based on questionnaires, however, have generally found that people with more conservative attitudes report being more easily disgusted.

"If bodily reactions don't differ across political groups, why do feelings?" Manos Tsakiris, of Royal Holloway and the Centre for the Politics of Feelings at the University of London, told DW.

Tsakiris and colleague Mariana von Mohr wondered whether the answer might lie in how people perceive and interpret signals from their bodies.

Scientists call the perception of internal sensations, such as hunger, breathing or a racing heart, "interoception." It's sometimes called our eighth sense, alongside the familiar five, plus our senses of balance and body position.

"A bodily signal doesn't arrive with a label attached," Tsakiris told DW. "We have to notice it and make sense of it.".

The researchers surveyed 632 US adults, asking how much they noticed and trusted signals from their bodies — a measure known as "interoceptive sensibility.".

They found that people who were more easily disgusted by sexual behavior tended to be more conservative, regardless of how aware they felt of their bodies.

But for moral disgust, the link to conservatism was found only among people who reported lower bodily awareness.

What particularly surprised Tsakiris was that perceived bodily awareness alone had no link to political views.

"People who are highly attuned to their bodies were neither more liberal nor more conservative," he said.

Inbar questions whether all forms of disgust are equally useful for studying political attitudes.

He and Joshua Tybur, one of the creators of the Three-Domain Disgust Scale, generally prefer measuring pathogen disgust — reactions to potential sources of disease — rather than sexual disgust.

Questions about sexual disgust may already reflect conservative beliefs about sex.

"It's almost asking people the same thing twice," Inbar stated.

The fresh study found no significant link between pathogen disgust and conservative views.

Inbar wants the findings on bodily awareness and disgust tested again, with predictions set out in advance. For now, he considers them "suggestive at best.".

Tsakiris suggests that people who struggle to understand their bodily feelings may be more vulnerable to political messages telling them what those feelings mean.

Industry observers note that "I know what you're feeling. You're feeling angry or you're feeling disgusted about this thing," he remarked, illustrating how someone might put an emotional label on another person's unease.

Such labels could influence political behavior, he argues, although the study did not directly test this.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"This is how disgust can do political work: it can turn moral judgments about individuals into judgments about whole groups," he said.

It has been revealed that the research cannot establish whether disgust shapes political beliefs or existing beliefs shape what people find disgusting. Bakker notes that political beliefs can influence how people describe their own personalities, suggesting the relationship could work both ways.

"Voting behavior is very complex and citizens make up their mind about politics in a complex way," he told DW.

According to recent reports, inbar also cautions against exaggerating disgust's importance. "The thing to emphasize in your story is that the relationship, while it's consistent, is quite small," he said.

"It's one of the many influences on people's politics.".

Tsakiris advocates what he calls "critical feeling": questioning our emotional responses to provocative material, including social media posts, just as we question the information itself.

He also emphasizes discussing our feelings with others and listening to different perspectives, even when we disagree.

"Life and politics and democracy is a contact sport," he stated. Edited by: Rosalie Delaney.

Arsenal have been told they will need to pay in excess of €100 million (£83.5m) to sign Antonio Nusa from RB Leipzig in the January transfer window, according to reports in Germany.

Arsenal are in the market to strengthen Mikel Arteta’s attacking options and Nusa is one of the options on their shortlist.

The 21-year-old, who joined RB Leipzig in a €21m (£17.8m) deal from Club Brugge two years ago, has been one of the German club’s standout performers this season with nine goals and eight assists in 17 games so far.

At international level, Nusa has established himself as a key part of Norway’s attack, scoring 10 goals in 36 appearances.

Arsenal have been monitoring Nusa’s performances in the Bundesliga and the Champions League ahead of the upcoming transfer window.

But according to Sky Germany, RB Leipzig will only consider selling Nusa if they receive an ‘astronomical offer’, which would be bids over €100m (£83.5m).

RB Leipzig, who sit fourth in the Bundesliga and remain in contention to secure a play-off place in the Champions League league phase, are noted to want to keep Nusa for the remainder of the season.

Earlier this year, RB Leipzig held off selling Yan Diomande in the January window and ended up agreeing a deal worth up to £120m with Real Madrid in the summer.

  • Chelsea are allegedly yet to determine whether they will consider ending Alejandro Garnacho's loan stint at Aston Villa.
  • On Tuesday evening, the Argentine was left out of the squad for the Champions League fixture at Galatasaray, despite Unai Emery naming two goalkeepers and having one spare spot on the substitutes' bench.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 27 Nov 2026 11:08.

Chelsea are allegedly yet to determine whether they will consider ending Alejandro Garnacho's loan stint at Aston Villa.

On Tuesday evening, the Argentine was left out of the squad for the Champions League fixture at Galatasaray, despite Unai Emery naming two goalkeepers and having one spare spot on the substitutes' bench.

Emery suggested after the game that he only selected players who he felt were capable of making an impact in that particular match, essentially delivering a clear message to Garnacho.

Garnacho has been restricted to just seven substitute appearances totalling fewer than 100 minutes since making the loan switch to Villa, who can activate a permanent £43m transfer if the winger plays a set number of matches.

However, like in the case of Liverpool's Harvey Elliott in 2025-26, it has become apparent that Emery has given up on a loan player who Villa could sign for big money if they make in the region of eight to 10 appearances.

As per several reports, Villa do not have the option of ending Garnacho's loan during the winter transfer window, nor do Chelsea have a recall clause.

These were the same terms that Villa and Liverpool agreed for Elliott, and subsequently failed to agree over a compromise for the second half of the last campaign.

According to The Athletic, Villa will need to hope that a foreign club expresses an interest in signing Garnacho at the turn of the year.

Garnacho is stated to have wanted to leave the Premier League for a European club prior to Emery expressing an interest in his services.

At this point in time, though, it is unclear whether Chelsea would give the green light to a change of clubs for Garnacho.

If it is not beneficial from a financial perspective, they may choose to take no action.

According to recent reports, the exact reason why Emery wanted to sign Garnacho is unclear. The fact that the former Manchester United attacker has not made a single start is either reflective of his efforts in training or Emery not having any serious interest in a permanent deal.

Either way, it is clear that Garnacho needs to rebuild his career in Europe, most likely La Liga where he has previously spent time at Atletico Madrid as a youngster.

Sources indicate that how that may come about remains to be seen. Any club would likely have to take the bulk of Garnacho's wages and pay a substantial loan fee for it to be worthwhile to Chelsea.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United had the January transfer window in mind when triggering Bruno Fernandes’ contract extension.

Standard Sport understands that Man Utd have activated their option to extend their captain’s deal by one year.

Fernandes’ current terms were due to expire at the end of the current season, but now run until the summer of 2028.

Fernandes confirmed last week that he had put contract negotiations with United on hold due to the club’s ongoing struggles on the pitch, having already rejected two offers of new terms.

Man Utd head into the Premier League weekend sitting in 19th place in the Premier League, and welcome sixth-placed Brentford to Old Trafford on Saturday in what is new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first home game in charge.

Fernandes has struggled to reproduce the form that earned him a host of individual awards last season, and Standard Sport understands that both parties believe it is sensible to return to negotiations at a later date.

Pochettino hints at Fernandes injury in shock blow to Man Utd plans.

Man Utd confirm Bruno Fernandes absence ahead of Brentford clash.

Man Utd XI vs Brentford: Confirmed team news and predicted lineup.

Make 2026 the year of working smarter.

But that left Fernandes open to approaches for foreign teams with pre-contract offers ahead of the summer.

And that’s why Man Utd have acted.

To prevent any further distractions, Fernandes has been tied up for a further 12 months and will return to the negotiation table once the club are on more assured footing form-wise.

But an exit this summer can not yet be ruled out.

Fernandes may not be able to help his team-mates on Saturday, though, having been struck down by an illness which prevented him from training on Friday morning.

Recent findings suggest that confirming the issue later on Friday, Pochettino remarked of Fernandes: "He's affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and, today, he cannot be part of the training session.

"We'll see. We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we'll see. We're not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don't feel [you can]. We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing.".

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

Industry observers note that it was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he said with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

The giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

Recent findings suggest that if you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had mentioned he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

Bradley Barcola's first ever senior hat-trick ⚽️ He's been unplayable 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/UMhUDmGPo9.

“I’m really happy for Bradley, because you were asking me yesterday about him, not making the numbers,” Iraola smiled. “Also Florian [Wirtz], and I think both of them played really, really well. They made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat-trick I thought he was a threat.

“He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”.

Barcola should have had the stage to himself on an evening when Liverpool were so obviously better than LASK in Linz but it will have frustrated Iraola immensely that his team scoring six times was tarnished by three daft goals being given up in the final 25 minutes.

We can look at the late switch off in due course but the only place to begin is with Barcola, who looked ready for business as early as the eighth minute when his first touch was a cushioned back heel, taking possession by crossing one leg behind the other, and how he seized his moment.

Liverpool had already taken the lead when Ronald Araújo rose powerfully to head in a Kostas Tsimikas corner but, two minutes after, the Barcola show began, a confident right-footed shot being swept past Lukas Jungwirth from 10 yards after some good build-up play from Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas.

Recent findings suggest that as Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”.

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

It has been revealed that they travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Recent findings suggest that tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 27 Nov 2026 11:24, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 11:44.
  • The stuttering champions and the challengers-in-crisis face off in Sunday's Premier League main event, which sees Arsenal and Manchester City draw swords at the Emirates Stadium.
  • The Gunners hold a six-point advantage over Enzo Maresca's men at the summit of the Premier League table, leading some to deduce that another success for the holders could already expel the Sky Blues from the title race.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 27 Nov 2026 11:24, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 11:44.

The stuttering champions and the challengers-in-crisis face off in Sunday's Premier League main event, which sees Arsenal and Manchester City draw swords at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners hold a six-point advantage over Enzo Maresca's men at the summit of the Premier League table, leading some to deduce that another success for the holders could already expel the Sky Blues from the title race.

Out of sight in first place, boasting the best defence in the top flight and taking 16 points from the last 18 on offer in the Premier League, Arsenal have lived up to their early-season expectations as the overwhelming favourites to retain their crown.

Yet, the Emirates faithful cannot shake the feeling that there is still something missing in Mikel Arteta's ranks, after Arsenal's second-half shortcomings were exposed in back-to-back draws with Newcastle United and Borussia Dortmund.

Both stalemates saw the Gunners fail to hold onto and build on one-goal advantages in the first half, before their foes came out all guns blazing after the restart and capitalised on Arsenal's alarming lack of a ruthless attacking touch.

Only four of Arsenal's 30 shots on goal in the Champions League were on target, as their 12-game winning run in home league phase/group stage fixtures came to an end, and their 17 Premier League goals scored so far ranks as the worst among all top-six teams.

However, the holders are five from five at the Emirates Stadium in the top flight - scoring 10 times and conceding just twice in the process - and they are yet to draw a blank at home in any tournament this term.

Interestingly, Arsenal's 10 home goals matches Man City's 10 away strikes in the 2026-27 Premier League season, while only Brighton & Hove Albion (26) can better the visitors' overall total of 22.

Such statistics will come as little consolation to travelling fans amid the Sky Blues' sorry slump, though, as Enzo Maresca's men have collected just one point from the last 12 on offer in the top flight after a perfect seven from seven to start the campaign.

The Citizens at least managed to snap their three-game losing sequence in last week's 1-1 draw at home to Fulham - not that such a feat was worth celebrating, though - before they also had to settle for a point in their midweek Champions League clash with Napoli.

Maresca and former Man City players have disagreed over whether the club's guilty verdict and appeal uncertainty over their 115 charges is impacting on-field performances, but the manager himself now finds himself under fire for questionable tactical calls and team selections over the autumnal period.

There is no suggestion that the former Chelsea boss is under any immediate sack pressure, though, despite presiding over a 122-year worst; City are just the second team in English Football League history to win their first seven matches of a season but fail to triumph in any of their next four, after the 1904-05 Sheffield Wednesday crop.

Furthermore, the Sky Blues were swatted aside in August's 3-0 Community Shield defeat to Arsenal, who have only lost two of their last nine head-to-heads against Man City and are unbeaten in their last three meetings on Emirates soil.

Arsenal form (all competitions):.

Manchester City Premier League form:.

Manchester City form (all competitions):.

Fears of a serious shoulder injury to Arsenal number one David Raya have been allayed by Arteta, and at the time of writing, the Spain international has not been officially ruled out of the visit of Man City.

Arsenal will also welcome teenage wonderkid Max Dowman back from a three-game domestic suspension, but Martin Zubimendi (hamstring) and Bukayo Saka (quad) will not be back until just before Christmas at the earliest.

After Christos Tzolis's underwhelming midweek display, expect Eberechi Eze to return to the forward line, where Arteta has a critical choice to make between Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz after the former's thunderous finish in midweek.

Meanwhile, captain Martin Odegaard has another Premier League record in his sights; if he sets up two goals here, he will equal the record for the most assists by a Norwegian player in the competition - his 38 is marginally inferior to Morten Gamst Pedersen's 40.

Meanwhile, Man City are expected to head south with a fully-fit squad barring former Arsenal transfer target Antoine Semenyo, who is a few weeks away from returning from a knee injury.

Snubbed from the starting XI against Fulham before saving City's skin against Napoli, Rayan Cherki has surely done enough to hold his spot at the Emirates, while Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye also have cases to come back in after providing assists off the bench last time out.

Goalless in his last three Premier League matches, Erling Haaland could equal his own personal worst for an English top-flight goal drought, having never gone longer than four Premier League games without finding the back of the net.

Arsenal possible starting lineup:.

Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Rice; Madueke, Odegaard, Eze; Havertz.

Manchester City possible starting lineup:.

Donnarumma; Nunes, Guehi, Dias, O'Reilly; Anderson, Fernandez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland.

The defensive numbers make for dreadful reading for Man City, who have let in seven goals across their last three away games and are without a clean sheet in 10 fixtures in total.

A profligate Arsenal side may not be the best-placed to capitalise, as only one of their last five wins has been by more than a one-goal margin, but the champions should still demonstrate why they are champions and deal another blow to Man City's already-fading title hopes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes is a doubt for Manchester United as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to welcome Brentford to Old Trafford on Saturday.

The club captain was unable to train on Friday morning due to a virus, which has thrown into doubt his involvement in Pochettino’s first home match in charge.

Pochettino is still figuring out how best to set up his fresh team, and this is a potentially huge spanner to throw into the works.

Fernandes’s absence could see Matheus Cunha move into the No10 role, supported by Amad Diallo and Patrick Dorgu, with Bryan Mbeumo leading the line.

Industry observers note that elsewhere, the new manager also has a decision to make in defence. Having opted for a back three in the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield last weekend, Pochettino switched to a four-man defence for the chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting on Wednesday, in which Fernandes scored both goals.

Although Brentford will fancy their chances of victory based on the respective league positions of the two clubs - Man Utd 19th, the Bees in sixth - United will be urged by their fans to attack. As such, a more timid back three seems unlikely.

Industry observers note that it will be a case of balancing fitness levels with only two days of rest between games. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens has come under fire in recent weeks for his performances, but back-up Karl Darlow has struggled with injury since arriving in the summer.

Sources indicate that pochettino’s defensive options are fairly limited. Leny Yoro is available after his early red card against Liverpool was overturned, while Harry Maguire was restored to the starting XI for the Sporting game.

Brentford’s pace in behind may necessitate a quicker backline, meaning Maguire could make way again here, having also reportedly complained of an injury after the midweek match.

Lisandro Martinez has been at left-back, but Dorgu’s attacking qualities will likely be required on Saturday and Luke Shaw is also now back in training. By moving Martinez back to centre-half alongside Yoro, Pochettino can find the pace required. Diogo Dalot may get the nod ahead of Noussair Mazraoui at right-back.

Should Fernandes be passed fit, the attack continues to pick itself - if not their exact positions.

Fernandes was deployed on the left behind Cunha in the defeat by Liverpool, while Mbeumo was briefly used as the lone forward under Michael Carrick.

Here, we’re predicting Cunha to lead the line after his midweek rest due to suspension, with Fernandes in behind as the No10 and Mbeumo on the left wing.

If Amad is fit enough to start after being forced off in the draw with Sporting, expect the Ivorian on the right flank. If not, youngster Shea Lacey could be a candidate to start.

Recent findings suggest that marcus Rashford and Benjamin Sesko remain injured, as do midfielders Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte. Pochettino revealed that Baleba would be out for 10 to 12 weeks from when he sustained his hamstring problem against Roma in early November.

Injured: Rashford, Baleba, Ugarte, Sesko.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to James Pearce of The Athletic, both Federico Chiesa and Wataru Endo are expected to leave Liverpool by the end of next summer’s transfer window. Neither the Italian winger nor the Japanese midfielder have a place in the long-term aims of head coach Andoni Iraola, and the former Bournemouth boss has already informed them about that.

Chiesa missed the first five Premier League games this season through a back injury, and then he made a two-minute appearance in Liverpool’s home defeat to Manchester City. Endo, meanwhile, hasn’t played at all in any competition, and neither of them is a part of the Champions League squad.

Chiesa is likely to be sold, perhaps in January already, having 18 months left on his contract, while Endo is expected to leave Anfield as a free agent when his deal expires at the end of the season.

It has been revealed that captain Virgil van Dijk, goalkeeper Alisson Becker, left-back Kostas Tsimikas and versatile defender Joe Gomez, are all out of contract in the summer as well. Van Dijk and Alisson are likely to get sign newly introduced deals as they both wish to stay put and remain extremely vital for Liverpool.

#164894. Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2135 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2. Achieving high molecular weight, controlled stereochemistry and sequence precision simultaneously has been elusive using conventional chemical methods that rely on protecting-group manipulations. Here we propose enzymatic living polymerization, which enables the precision preparation of natural polysaccharides with molecular weights up to 660 kg mol−1 but polydispersity from low to less than 1.05. Such a living behaviour originates from the initiator weakly binding with the polymerase, realizing fast equilibrium of the active (bound) and dormant (unbound) species, as demonstrated by mechanistic and computational studies. Our approach is generalizable to diverse polysaccharide types, including sequence-controlled block copolymers, and provides a modular route to explore molecular-weight-dependent biological functions of natural polysaccharides.

Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Janosch, the pen name of German author and illustrator Horst Eckert, won hearts around the world with his warm and simple sense of humor. He charmed children and adults alike with his iconic Tiger, Bear, Tiger-Duck and other animals.

Janosch created more than 150 books, which have been translated into over 30 languages.

His best-selling children's book, "Oh, wie schön ist Panama," translated into English as "The Trip to Panama," was so lucrative that Janosch was able to settle down on the Canary Island of Tenerife in 1980, where he lived together with his wife Ines. The writer and illustrator died peacefully at the age of 95, his publisher Bernhard Feil announced on Wednesday.

Recent findings suggest that janosch was born as Horst Eckert on March 11, 1931, in Hindenburg (now Zabrze, Poland) in what was then Upper Silesia. After World War II, his family had to flee to Germany.

According to recent reports, in 1953, Janosch started studying at the Academy of Art in Munich, thinking that it would be easy to become an artist. He was however dismissed after just a few terms for "lack of talent.".

Recent findings suggest that but luckily for his later readers, Janosch did not give up. He continued to work as a freelance artist, soon discovering his second great gift, namely writing.

His first children's book about a horse named Valek was published in 1960.

Although Janosch became famous primarily for his children's books, he also wrote books for adults that focused on his own childhood.

Even though he wrote cheerful books for children, Janosch hardly had any positive memories of his own childhood, as his father was an alcoholic. He was beaten not only by him but also by his mother and grandmother. Raised in a strictly Catholic environment, he was continuously threatened to be punished by God.

Later on, Janosch tried to overcome the burden of his childhood memories by turning to alcohol as well.

Recent findings suggest that he always expressed a great deal of understanding for children, trying to encourage them to stand up for their rights. As a result of his childhood experiences, Janosch did not want to have children himself, and his attitude towards the Catholic Church always remained divided. "As I am a sinner and a heretic, God will let me live a long life so that I can return to the Church," he told his biographer Angela Bajorek.

Janosch's animal figures are endearing but not always well-behaved. They love all kinds of nonsense. But even if they lie to each other or put their own interests first, the true winner at the end of stories is always friendship and solidarity.

According to recent reports, janosch achieved his major breakthrough with "The Trip to Panama," a story about two friends, a little tiger and a bear, who set out to find their paradise in Panama. After touring around in circles, they finally end up where they started out; they realize that their journey was the destination. Janosch received the German Youth Book Prize in 1979 for the work.

Janosch's protagonists have become familiar to generations of children all over the world. They come up over and over again in the various stories carefully illustrated with water colors.

There is the honest lion Hans from the toy chest who fails to catch a nutcracker with his lies. There is Schnuddel and a ridiculous bragger Günter the Box-Frog. And then there is a tiger that collects mushrooms while looking out for his devoted friend, a bear, who always stands up for him even when the tiger temporarily leaves him because of a little pig in one of the stories.

The "Tigerente," literally "Tiger-Duck," a wooden duck on wheels with yellow-brown stripes, appears on numerous pictures by the illustrator. At times, the animal has been tossed into a corner, at times it is hanging from the ceiling, or the Box-Frog pulls it across the drawing.

His iconic figures, especially the Tiger-Duck, have served as motifs on various items, from cups to stamps to jewelry, and even on airplanes. Film adaptations and TV series based on his stories were produced in German and English.

Guests who visited Janosch in Tenerife were impressed by his very modest lifestyle. He always said that hanging around in his hammock doing nothing was what he enjoyed most. And yet Janosch remained very active until the end of his life.

It has been revealed that from 2013 to 2019, he wrote a column for the German weekly Die Zeit, taking on the role of Mr. Wondrak, who commented on world affairs. Shortly before his 90th birthday in 2021, the complete collection of his Mr. Wondrak columns were published as a book in German.

It has been revealed that like the protagonists in his stories, Janosch always tried to content himself with few things. As he wrote in one of his books: "He who needs almost nothing, has everything.".

This article was originally written in German.

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is believed to be in with a chance of facing Manchester City in Sunday's Premier League blockbuster at the Emirates Stadium.

The Spain international sustained a serious-looking shoulder injury in last weekend's 2-2 draw with Newcastle United, but his issue is nowhere near as severe as first believed.

Mikel Arteta is yet to rule Raya out of the visit of Man City, and if the Gunners' number one is declared fit enough to participate, he will undoubtedly steal the gloves off of Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Whoever starts in goal for Arsenal should be shielded by the central pairing of Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhaes, as William Saliba is slowly re-integrated, and the full-back duo of Jurrien Timber and Riccardo Calafiori, displacing Ben White and Piero Hincapie after the 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League in midweek.

Myles Lewis-Skelly should also make way for Bruno Guimaraes in the double pivot, while the underwhelming Christos Tzolis can expect to lose out to Eberechi Eze on the left flank.

Noni Madueke and Martin Odegaard are safe, though, as the latter chases Morten Gamst Pedersen's record of 40 Premier League assists from a Norwegian player; the Arsenal skipper sits on 38.

Viktor Gyokeres's thunderbolt in midweek has given Arteta a major decision to make up top, but Premier League regular Kai Havertz - who has scored three goals and set up another in his last four matches against Man City - should come back in.

Arsenal possible starting lineup:.

Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Rice; Madueke, Odegaard, Eze; Havertz.

Manchester City head to Arsenal this weekend in desperate need of a morale-boosting victory.

Enzo Maresca’s side have picked up just one point from the last 12 available in the Premier League, with a disappointing home draw with Fulham following successive defeats at the hands of Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

Sitting third and already six points behind leaders Arsenal after only 11 games, many pundits predict that City’s title chances will effectively be over if they lose again in north London on Sunday.

City are also still waiting for their appeal to be heard against the guilty verdict returned by an independent panel back in September on their charges of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules across a nine-season period between 2009/10 and 2017/18. They deny any wrongdoing.

Maresca has to find the right team to beat an Arsenal side that have lost just twice at home across all competitions in 2026.

Gianluigi Donnarumma will start in goal as usual, with the back four in front of him likely consisting of Matheus Nunes, Ruben Dias, Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol.

Dias was rested for the home draw with Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday night, with the City captain set to be restored to the starting XI here.

Nico O’Reilly has emerged as the first-choice option at left-back in recent weeks, but the defensive ability of Gvardiol could be key in a potentially cagey match.

Maresca has experimented with the construction of his midfield in the last few games. Enzo Fernandez was deployed as a No10 against Napoli, but a return to the preferred paring of the Argentine and Elliot Anderson at the base of City’s midfield feels likely at Arsenal.

Sources indicate that similarly, Iliman Ndiaye has impressed on the right wing in recent weeks. Rayan Cherki was deployed out wide against Napoli, but has been most effective as a No10.

Jeremy Doku has become trusted on the left, while Erling Haaland cannot be left out - even if he is enduring a goalscoring drought by his usual lofty standards.

Maresca revealed at his pre-match press conference on Friday that Antoine Semenyo was close to returning from a knee injury sustained against Ipswich last month, though the trip to Arsenal will come too soon for his comeback.

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 14:56 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 15:01 EST, 25 November 2026.

Premier League officials are 'shocked and furious' after the FA overturned Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's red card at Liverpool - despite the competition's own independent panel unanimously backing the dismissal.

It has been revealed that daily Mail Sport understands that the Premier League's Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel has returned a 5-0 verdict in support of referee Sam Barrott's decision to send off Yoro. The panel also backed VAR's decision not to intervene. Their findings will be released next Wednesday.

But an extraordinary row has now erupted, with United celebrating a successful appeal while the Premier League and refereeing body Pro Ref stand by the original decision.

United appealed against the red card following Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Anfield - Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge - and an independent FA regulatory commission, consisting of three former players, rescinded Yoro's one-match ban on Tuesday.

The Frenchman was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he ran clear on goal in the eighth minute. United disputed the referee's view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, having taken a heavy touch.

The FA panel appeared to agree, on the basis Yoro did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity, meaning the Frenchman is free to play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Referee Sam Barrott revealed Manchester United defender Leny Yoro a red card vs Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off for this foul on Alexander Isak - but his red card was overturned on Tuesday.

Barrott and his on-field officiating team from Sunday are believed to be angry at the overturn.

However, top-flight officials are now understood to be demanding answers as to how this has happened, with Pro Ref chief Howard Webb backing his referees.

Recent findings suggest that 'That (the red card) was the referee's call, made on the field,' said Webb. 'Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect - and formed the opinion it wasn't.

Sources indicate that 'I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving swiftly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.'.

According to recent reports, united sources have branded this interpretation as 'totally wrong' and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott's decision.

United dispute that it was a subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

The Premier League and Pro Ref did not comment.

By Ben Knapton | 27 Nov 2026 11:43.

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca could be tempted into three changes for Sunday's Premier League battle with champions Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

The Sky Blues are seeking to snap a four-game winless run in the top flight, but they had to come from behind twice to salvage a 2-2 draw with Napoli in the Champions League in midweek.

Rayan Cherki scored City's second goal at the Etihad and is now poised for a return to the Premier League starting lineup behind Erling Haaland, who risks matching a personal worst.

Having failed to score in his last three Premier League games, the Golden Boot winner could equal his longest drought in the English top flight, a four-game sequence between February and April earlier this year.

However, Haaland has found the net in each of his last four Premier League games against Arsenal and could receive additional support from Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku, both of whom provided assists off the bench against Napoli.

Ndiaye and Doku returning to the XI may force Enzo Fernandez into a deeper role alongside Elliot Anderson, as Maresca favours experience over the youthful exuberance of Ayyoub Bouaddi against the holders.

Ruben Dias for Josko Gvardiol may be the sole defensive alteration that the visiting manager makes, as his City side aim to end an appalling run of 10 straight games without a clean sheet.

Manchester City possible starting lineup:.

Donnarumma; Nunes, Guehi, Dias, O'Reilly; Anderson, Fernandez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland.

Manchester United midfielder Carlos Baleba will not play again this year after Mauricio Pochettino revealed the extent of his hamstring injury.

Baleba was injured during United’s Champions League clash against Roma on November 3, pulling up as he made a run into the penalty area before being forced off in tears.

The Cameroon international has not played since, with former manager Michael Carrick initially confirming he would be sidelined for several weeks.

Pochettino has now confirmed Baleba faces up to three months out, with the timeframe dating back to the injury against Roma. The setback is expected to rule him out throughout the festive period and potentially until the end of January.

“Baleba, the moment was Roma, [when he got] injured, and the medical staff were talking about 10 to 12 weeks,” Pochettino told a press conference on Friday.

Baleba is set to miss United’s upcoming fixtures against Brentford, Newcastle, Coventry and RB Leipzig, as well as league matches against Crystal Palace, Arsenal, Nottingham Forest, Sunderland and Brighton.

Nashville SC defender Jack Maher revealed he is "so confident" his team-mates can defeat FC Cincinnati in their MLS Cup playoff tie.

Nashville won the 2026 Supporters' Shield in stunning fashion, setting a newly introduced single-season points record (77), but made a losing start to the postseason.

BJ Callaghan's side lost Game 1 in Round One at home 1-0 after an early own goal from Patrick Yazbek, marking their first defeat at GEODIS Park in MLS play this season.

Nashville must now defeat Cincinnati in Game 2 on Saturday to keep the series alive, and Maher is optimistic they can get the job done at TQL Stadium.

"First loss at home in MLS play for the whole entire year, and I think that that's something that clearly is frustrating," said Maher.

"The mood around the locker room was that this hasn't really happened before this year. But we're optimistic about the next game, and we're going to give it clearly everything we got.

"It's a hungry group in that locker room, and I think that if [Cincinnati] want to go on, they got to beat us twice.

"I'm so confident that we have the guys in this locker room to be able to go up to Cincinnati, get a great result, come back home, and finish the job.".

Nashville boss Callaghan added: "This team's battle-tested, and the group will be ready to respond.

"You can feel that there's a bit of a hunger. This team has continually revealed that we have the experience from early in the season in playing knockout-type games, and the group will be prepared to respond.".

Antoine Semenyo is close to returning for Manchester City, Enzo Maresca has confirmed.

The Ghana international has not featured for Man City since sustaining a knee injury in the 3-2 victory over Ipswich on October 17, missing the last eight games across all competitions as a result.

During this period, City have not won a Premier League game and head to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday to face leaders and reigning champions Arsenal.

Semenyo is not expected to be available for the trip to north London, though he could return against either Leeds or Brentford within the next week following a positive update from Maresca.

“We have good news, Antoine is quite close,” Maresca said in Friday’s pre-match press conference. “It’s good news for us. He is already on the pitch - he is very close, hopefully it can be next week, we hope so.

“I was laughing with him yesterday or two days ago. I told him in the Premier League the last game we won was with him on the pitch, so I noted we need him back soon to win games.

“Antoine is an important player but we have more players in his position that are doing well like Iliman in this moment. But he needs time to recover.”.

Semenyo had been enjoying a decent start to his first full season as a Man City player before being struck down by injury, scoring twice and weighing in with three assists in seven appearances.

The winger also started City’s significant away wins over Manchester United and Liverpool, two results that has boosted Maresca’s belief that his side can end their recent slump with victory at Arsenal.

He added: “I think we already indicated this season we are able to win vital games, to win away. So I don’t see any reason why we are not able to win there.

“We have shown this season we can win important games away. Old Trafford and Anfield are two important away games and Sunday we have another one.

“We highlighted already and we can win again.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 12:15.

Naby Keita has been out of action for several weeks and is going through a difficult period. The Guinean midfielder, presently at Ferencvaros, has asked the Hungarian club to let him step back so that he can recover mentally, a request accepted by his manager Balazs Borbely.

Sources indicate that the former Liverpool player, who has made only four league appearances this season, is expected to resume training with the group in January. In an interview with Flashscore, Borbely explained the difficulties faced by his player, including recurring injuries and a complicated sporting context.

According to recent reports, the situation eventually took a mental toll on the player. 'For the moment, however, he does not feel mentally ready to help the team. He has therefore asked the club to give him a little time to put his mental state in order' - Borbely revealed.

In a recent development, the manager clarified that Ferencvaros had accepted his request and that both parties should resume working together in January. Keita had already endured a difficult previous season, marked by several injuries and a complicated relationship with his former manager, the Irishman Robbie Keane.

In a recent development, having arrived at the Hungarian club in January 2025, initially on loan before signing permanently, the Guinean has failed to regain a regular place in the team. His last start was on 20 September. Since then, he has been a substitute on two occasions, but has mainly been absent from the squad.

Keita's absence comes as Ferencvaros make an excellent start to their Europa League campaign, with four wins in as many matches, including a convincing 2-0 victory over AC Milan.

Above all, Keita's current difficulties are nothing newly introduced.

Recurring injuries had already disrupted his time at Liverpool (2018-2023), where he never managed to establish himself as an undisputed starter despite the expectations placed on him after his successful spell at RB Leipzig.

His stay at Werder Bremen then failed to relaunch his career. Physical problems continued to disrupt his consistency, before his relationship with the German club deteriorated. Having arrived at Ferencvaros in January 2025 on loan, then signing permanently a few months later, the Guinean hoped to rediscover continuity in Hungary. But once again, he has not been able to play more than 10 league matches per season so far.

It is to be hoped that this break will allow one of Guinea's greatest talents of the past decade to recharge, professionally and above all personally.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that on November 4, 2001, London's Leicester Square became a world of witches and wizards. The occasion was the world premiere of "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" (released in the US and India as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone").

"Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.

Daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle. The BBC quoted him as saying, "It is so cool. I have never heard my name shouted so much in an hour.".

The crowds highlighted just how far Harry Potter fever had spread in only four years.

The first Harry Potter book was published by Britain's Bloomsbury in June 1997, with an initial print run of just 500 hardcover copies.

About 5,000 paperback copies were also released around the same time.

Sources indicate that today, first editions are prized collectors' items, with hardcover copies commanding high prices at auction. In mid-October, one sold for $400,000 through US auction house Heritage Auctions.

Industry observers note that at first, the book's popularity grew largely by word of mouth among schoolchildren. Media attention followed when it won the prestigious Nestle Smarties Book Prize later that year.

With an estimated 120 million-plus copies sold worldwide, it is the best-selling book in the series and ranks among the best-selling novels of all time.

For years, J.K. Rowling's public image was defined by her extraordinary rise from a single mother on welfare to a billionaire.

But in recent years, debate over her views on gender and transgender identity has increasingly overshadowed that success. It's an problem Rowling herself frequently weighs in on.

According to recent reports, in an essay published on her website on October 21, 2026, Rowling reiterated her opposition to what she calls the "current, dominant strain of trans activism." She argues that this movement "holds that a man who declares himself a woman is, literally, a woman, and is therefore entitled to be treated as a woman in all contexts." Rowling argues that allowing trans women into single-sex spaces poses a risk. She describes biological sex as an indisputable biological fact.

Such statements have led critics to accuse Rowling of transphobia, while others regard her stance as a defense of women's rights and safety.

The controversy has also divided her fans. Some stand by Rowling, while others try to draw a distinction between the books and their author.

Others have left Harry Potter behind altogether. One former fan is German YouTuber Coldmirror, known for her Harry Potter parodies. The media artist from the Bremen area, whose real name is Kathrin Fricke, told the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper: "I don't have any love left for Harry. I'm still somewhat interested, but I can no longer watch it in good conscience." She cited Rowling's campaigning against transgender people as the reason.

The "Harry Potter" film cast is divided as well. The three main stars — Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint — have publicly spoken out in support of transgender people. Meanwhile, Ralph Fiennes, who played Lord Voldemort, and Helena Bonham Carter, who portrayed Bellatrix Lestrange, have defended Rowling's right to express her views.

It has been revealed that despite the controversy surrounding Rowling, Warner Bros., which holds the Harry Potter film rights, is bringing the books back to the screen — this time as a series for HBO. The premiere is scheduled for December 25.

The eight-episode first season is an an adaption of the first book. Even though the episode lengths haven't been announced, the scope of a TV series gives each book much more room than the original films did. That means more time to explore subplots, character development and everyday life at Hogwarts. While many fans are looking forward to a more detailed adaptation, others remain skeptical. They find it hard to imagine the familiar characters being played by anyone else.

The new trio consists of Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley.

Sources indicate that J.K. Rowling is an executive producer on the show. HBO says, however, that her views on gender identity won't be reflected in the storyline. Several people involved in the latest production have publicly distanced themselves from her views. Paapa Essiedu, who has been cast as Severus Snape, signed an open letter supporting transgender people. Rowling subsequently remarked she had neither the power nor the desire to have him removed from the show because of it. John Lithgow, who plays Dumbledore, and Nick Frost, who portrays Hagrid, have also spoken out against Rowling's views.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, the Harry Potter merchandising machine is still going strong. On November 4, Britain's largest Harry Potter store to date is set to open in London. According to Warner Bros., the two-story shop covers more than 1,950 square meters.

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

Recent findings suggest that city will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

Industry observers note that the data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of fresh signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 15:52 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 18:32 EST, 25 November 2026.
  • Celtic have announced a long-term partnership with a company the club believe will transform their recruitment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 15:52 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 18:32 EST, 25 November 2026.

Celtic have announced a long-term partnership with a company the club believe will transform their recruitment.

London-based Pluto Data Analytics use predictive analytics and AI to help football clubs with player identification. The initial deal lasts three years, with scope for extension.

Celtic believe the deal will ‘support the club’s continuing commitment to innovation and excellence in football operations by enhancing recruitment analysis, talent identification, squad planning and broader football decision-making processes.’.

The Parkhead club’s recruitment strategy has been heavily criticised by supporters in recent seasons amid their struggles in Europe and increased domestic competition from Rangers and Hearts.

A statement explaining the arrangement added: ‘The partnership forms part of Celtic’s ongoing investment in modern football infrastructure and its commitment to ensuring that football decisions are informed by the best available intelligence and expertise.

‘By working with Pluto Data Analytics, Celtic will gain access to enhanced analytical tools and insights to support its existing recruitment and football operations functions.

The Parkhead club are hoping that upcoming deal will improve their recruitment process.

‘The objective is clear: to improve decision-making, identify emerging opportunities and support the club’s long-term football strategy.’.

The move comes following long-standing criticism that the Scottish champions’ means of scouting undervalued talents had become outdated, with their failure to act swiftly and efficiently in the transfer market leading to repeated failures in the European qualification rounds.

Rival clubs such as Hearts have benefited from the use of data thanks to the access they have had to Jamestown Analytics.

‘We are always looking for ways to strengthen our football operation and ensure that we continue to evolve in an increasingly competitive environment,’ said Celtic chief executive Michael Nicholson.

‘We have been reviewing the options in this area in order to select the optimum model for our club.

‘Our partnership with Pluto Data Analytics, an organisation with real quality and pedigree within this field, reflects our commitment to innovation and continuous improvement.

O'Neill says he hopes partnership 'will help us deliver the success we are all striving for'.

It has been revealed that ‘Recruitment remains one of the most important areas of any football club. Our aim is to identify talent as effectively as possible, reduce uncertainty where we can and support our football staff with the best available information.

‘We believe this partnership will strengthen our ability to support the club’s ambitions both domestically and in European competition.’.

Manager Martin O’Neill added: ‘I am very pleased that Celtic and Pluto are joining together to give the club an extra level of insight and analysis which is becoming more prominent in football.

‘While football is not an exact science, if the club can access and utilise fresh tools and new details, ultimately, we hope that such data will help us deliver the success we are all striving for.

Celtic chief executive Michael Nicholson claims Pluto deal is 'optimum model' for the club.

In a recent development, ‘Our recruitment and wider football operations teams have already engaged with Pluto. Our prepares in the short, medium and longer term are being developed and we are confident that our relationship will deliver real tangible benefit to the club over the next few years.’.

Jon Godfrey, CEO of Pluto Data Analytics, mentioned: ‘Today is a substantial day for Pluto and we are incredibly excited to be working with Celtic, one of the biggest clubs in world football.

‘We believe that predictive data modelling combined with the allure and resources of such a famous institution will allow us to achieve great things in this partnership.
