Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith.

It has been revealed that I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Burkina Faso teenager Mohamed Zongo has signed for Chelsea and is set to move to Stamford Bridge when he turns 18 next year.

Owners BlueCo reached an agreement to sign Zongo, then 16, in December 2025 and he was originally expected to join the Blues’ French sister club Strasbourg.

But Zongo has now been fast-tracked and signed a pre-agreement contract with Chelsea at their Cobham training ground after turning 17 on Thursday.

Zongo’s current club, Sporting des Tannounyan in Burkina Faso, said that the Chelsea hierarchy decided to change their plans after he impressed during Chelsea trials.

Zongo made his senior international debut for Burkina Faso aged just 16 last month, when he came off the bench to play in the second half of a 7-0 friendly defeat by Argentina in Buenos Aires.

The teenager previously impressed when he starred for Burkina Faso on their run to the quarter-finals of the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar last autumn. The midfielder scored the winner as his nation stunned Germany in the round of 16.

Scouts from a number of top European clubs were in attendance at games across the tournament and many took note of the performances produced by Zongo, who was 15 at the time.

Zongo had previously been linked with several other suitors, including LaLiga outfit Villarreal.

  • Separated by eight places in the Premier League table, 18th-placed Sunderland welcome mid-table Tottenham Hotspur to the Stadium of Light in matchweek 12.
  • The Black Cats have found greater defensive balance in recent weeks to sit inside the bottom three on goal difference alone, offering encouragement ahead of facing Roberto De Zerbi's men, who have won four of their last five matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 12:19, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 20:45.

Separated by eight places in the Premier League table, 18th-placed Sunderland welcome mid-table Tottenham Hotspur to the Stadium of Light in matchweek 12.

The Black Cats have found greater defensive balance in recent weeks to sit inside the bottom three on goal difference alone, offering encouragement ahead of facing Roberto De Zerbi's men, who have won four of their last five matches.

Sunderland continue to struggle for victories this season, but the Wearside outfit's recent results suggest that Regis Le Bris intends to address their underwhelming start by strengthening their defensive foundations.

Le Bris's men collected four points at the start of the campaign before suffering four consecutive defeats, during which the Mackems conceded at least twice against Arsenal, Manchester City, Brighton & Hove Albion and Bournemouth.

Having failed to score in three of those four defeats, the Black Cats' problems at both ends of the pitch were laid bare.

Shutting out Leeds United, however, began a sequence in which Sunderland have kept three clean sheets in four matches, although their only Premier League victory during that period remains the 1-0 success over Chelsea at the start of the month.

Nonetheless, those shutouts suggest that Le Bris intends to repair his leaky defence before turning his attention to a misfiring attack.

That approach could prove useful when Spurs visit Wearside this weekend, with De Zerbi's men occasionally struggling against opponents content to surrender possession and frustrate them.

Sunderland's counter-attacking approach troubled Chelsea three weeks ago, and De Zerbi's men will hope to avoid the pitfalls that befell the Blues in that early-November encounter.

The North Londoners arrive buoyed by four victories in their last five matches, including three clean sheets, while the absence of European commitments has given them a full week to prepare.

That should benefit the 10th-placed visitors, although the joint-lowest scorers in the top half must deliver a strong away performance to climb the standings, with the capital club just three points behind fifth-placed Bournemouth.

Spurs could finish the weekend in the Europa League position currently occupied by the Cherries, although that would require Marco Rose's men to slip up and Brentford, Leeds, Chelsea and Everton all to fail to win.

Sunderland Premier League form:.

Sunderland form (all competitions):.

Tottenham Hotspur Premier League form:.

Sunderland have several absentees this weekend: loanee Kevin Danso is ineligible to face his parent club, while Romaine Mundle (knee), Daniel Ballard (thigh), Habib Diarra (thigh), Granit Xhaka (calf) and Brian Brobbey (thigh) are sidelined; however, Dayann Methalie (illness) and Omar Alderete (knock) face late assessments.

Without joint-leading scorer Brobbey, the Black Cats will look to Enzo Le Fee to add to his three goals or another player to provide a match-winning contribution.

Although only Dominic Solanke and Jan Paul van Hecke have scored more than once for Spurs, the visitors can call upon Mohammed Kudus's creativity and ability to score from unlikely positions at the Stadium of Light.

Youngster Luca Jamie Williams-Barnett excelled on his full debut for the club, scoring and setting up Solanke's second-half strike against Ipswich Town to stake a strong claim for another start.

On the injury front, Xavi Simons (knee) and Wilson Odobert (knee) remain long-term absentees, while Mathys Tel (Achilles), Mykhailo Mudryk (ankle) and Savio (thigh) are unavailable in the short term; Tosin Adarabioyo (calf) faces fitness tests before Sunday, although Sandro Tonali is understood to have recovered from the illness that kept him out of last weekend's victory over Ipswich.

Sunderland possible starting lineup:.

Roefs; Meunier, O'Nien, Mukiele, Reinildo; Sadiki, Ahoka; Hume, Le Fee, Talbi; Isidor.

Tottenham Hotspur possible starting lineup:.

Kinsky; Porro, Van Hecke, Senesi, Udogie; Tonali, Fernandes; Kudus, Maddison, Williams-Barnett; Solanke.

Sunderland's three clean sheets in four matches suggest that Spurs will need patience, particularly against opponents whose counter-attacking approach has already frustrated Chelsea.

However, Brobbey's absence limits the hosts' attacking options, and the visitors' four victories in five mean we back them to edge a low-scoring contest.

Manchester United have reportedly activated their option to extend Bruno Fernandes’ contract.

The influential Red Devils captain was previously set to see his deal at Old Trafford expire in the summer, with speculation that he could depart after previous strong links to Saudi Arabia.

But United always possessed the option to trigger an automatic one-year extension, which they have now done.

Fernandes’ contract is now valid until June 2028, but The Athletic’s David Ornstein reports that such an extension will not necessarily prevent the Portugal playmaker from leaving next summer.

It means that if he does go, then United will at least receive a transfer fee.

Manchester United have a potential ace up their sleeve in transfer talks over Nico Paz.

Argentine star Paz is enjoying a burgeoning reputation across Europe after a remarkable start to the season with Como, which has seen him score six goals from attacking midfield - including two against Man Utd in the Champions League last month.

Paz joined Como in 2024 from Real Madrid in a deal worth around £5million, and it had long been expected that the player would return to the Spanish giants, who hold an €80m (£67m) buy-back clause for Paz.

But The Athletic report that Paz does not presently favour a return to Spain, where he will not be a key player, and is noted to be attracted by the prospect of joining Man Utd who need a long-term replacement for captain Bruno Fernandes.

The race for Paz is set to be fierce, but Man Utd will hope they have an advantage over rivals in the form of fresh manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Luka Vuskovic has revealed he chose to leave Tottenham for career stability, admitting that not a single Spurs manager spoke to him during the three years he was on the club’s books.

Spurs wanted Vuskovic to go out on loan again, with De Zerbi unable to offer him a place in the starting lineup, but the youngster was not keen on another season of upheaval and made it clear he wanted a permanent home.

“That (a loan) was their idea, but it was never an option from my side,” Vuskovic said in an interview with the Times. “Because already I have been on three loans and for me, my family, my girlfriend, it’s too much to move, with all the languages, and it gets too much for the person, you know?

“Before they signed everybody, they mentioned they don’t see me at the moment as a starting player.

According to recent reports, “Tottenham said they don’t want me at the minute, so I said, ‘OK, I have no problem with that, you gave me a loan already when I was 16, I just want to play somewhere where the club wants me. You can earn from me, so I think it’s fair for both of us.’ ”.

Chelsea are being linked with a shock reunion with Antonio Rudiger in January.

The German defender previously spent five years at Stamford Bridge before leaving for Real Madrid in 2022.

According to Football Insider, Chelsea could make a cut-price swoop to bring Rudiger back to west London before his current contract at the Bernabeu expires next summer.

He is struggling for game time under Jose Mourinho, while Xabi Alonso needs to quickly improve a defence that is leaking goals.

It looks like Arsenal will face a major fight from Manchester United over Nico Paz.

As mentioned already this morning, the Gunners are believed to be closely monitoring Como’s rising superstar, along with the likes of Liverpool and Tottenham.

But The Athletic’s David Ornstein now claims that Manchester United will pursue Paz if captain Bruno Fernandes leaves the club this summer, with a switch to Old Trafford said to hold some appeal for the Argentine.

It looks like Paz does not want to return to Real Madrid as things stand right now, despite their €80m buy-back clause.

Manchester United look to have been handed a major boost in their pursuit of Maxi Araujo.

The Uruguay and Sporting defender has emerged as a potential candidate to become Mauricio Pochettino’s first Old Trafford signing during the January transfer window as the new manager seeks to improve his options at left-back.

According to Sport Witness, Araujo’s camp are open to the move, which could apparently cost around €50m-€60m despite the €80m release clause in his contract at the Estadio Jose Alvalade.

Arsenal are interested in a blockbuster deal for Nico Paz, reports claim.

The Argentine playmaker has been central to the stunning rise of Serie A side Como under ex-Gunners star Cesc Fabregas, having left Real Madrid for Italy in 2024.

Los Blancos have a buy-back option for Paz next summer said to be valued at around €80m, though he is also attracting plenty of interest from elsewhere.

CaughtOffside cite reports claiming that Arsenal are closely tracking the 22-year-old, along with Liverpool and Tottenham, with a return to Madrid looking unlikely as things stand.

Richarlison is open to moving to Saudi Arabia to end his Tottenham exile.

The striker has been frozen out at Spurs by manager Roberto De Zerbi after failing to agree a summer exit.

Everton, Vasco da Gama and Trabzonspor were all noted to have explored deals for Richarlison, who ended up staying put at Spurs despite being left out of De Zerbi's Premier League squad.

Manchester United fans will be dismayed by reports that Mauricio Pochettino will have just £50million to improve his squad during the January transfer window.

A leaky defence has led to calls from ex-players such as Gary Neville for significant investment, but it appears Man Utd will try to do their business on a tight budget in January.

Augmenting reality with integrated photonics

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, augmented-reality (AR) glasses promise to transform how we interact with the world by seamlessly blending digital content with our physical surroundings.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, augmented-reality (AR) glasses promise to transform how we interact with the world by seamlessly blending digital content with our physical surroundings. Yet making them viable for comfortable, all-day use remains deeply challenging, constrained by hard trade-offs of size, power and display performance. This calls for fundamentally latest ways to generate and control light with high precision in an ultracompact form factor. Here we examine how integrated photonics can help bridge the technology gap in AR hardware. We review the basics of AR displays and recent advances in integrated photonics for new AR display components and architectures, then turn to key challenges and future directions, from component development to system innovation and scalable manufacturing, and highlight broader opportunities for synergy with fields such as quantum computing, bioimaging and optical sensing.

New England Revolution head coach Marko Mitrovic believes winger Peyton Miller is "converting from being potential to being a performer".

Miller made a decisive impact in the Revs' first-round, Game 1 victory over the Philadelphia Union in the MLS Cup playoff.

After forcing an own goal from Nathan Harriel, the 19-year-old scored in the second half to secure a 2-0 success at home.

Miller has scored eight goals and provided nine assists in MLS play this season, and Mitrovic praised the teenager's shift in mentality this term.

"He's converting from being potential to being a performer, and that's what a performer does," Mitrovic mentioned of Miller.

In a recent development, "If I have to track 90 yards or 90 metres back and protect my goal, I have to do it. And if I have to attack, I have to do it.

"I think that level of maturity is actually the biggest progression that we've seen from Peyton this year.".

Ahead of their must-win game at Subaru Park, Philadelphia will be hoping to rely on a youngster of their own in Cavan Sullivan.

Sullivan was named 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year, and Union interim head coach Ryan Richter was delighted for the 17-year-old.

"All the good things that come to him are a reflection of the hard work and the mentality that he has," Richter stated of Sullivan's award.

"The one thing that you know with him is that he has major ambitions and he has big dreams of what he wants to do in his career.

Recent findings suggest that "This is a great honour for him, but I know he's not going to take it and get complacent. He's onto the next thing. He's driven to take another step after this.".

Philadelphia Union – Bruno Damiani.

Since the beginning of September, Damiani has scored 10 goals, tied for the most in MLS with Orlando City's Antoine Griezmann.

Meanwhile, his six goals in home matches in that span are tied for most in MLS with five players, including teammate Milan Iloski.

New England Revolution – Peyton Miller.

Miller (19 years, 13 days) became the first teenager to score a playoff goal for New England last weekend.

Prior to Miller, the youngest Revs goalscorer in the MLS Cup playoffs was Tajon Buchanan (21 years, 290 days) in 2020, also against the Union.

MATCH PREDICTION: PHILADELPHIA UNION WIN.

Philadelphia have lost just once at home against an MLS team since the start of April (W8 D5), but the loss came versus New England on October 24.

The Revs have won consecutive road matches against the Union once, winning both their away games in this fixture in 2015.

The Union have been shut out in three of their last four games, after not being held scoreless in any of their previous 20 matches against MLS foes.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In Brazil, Fluminense's youth academy is considered one of the best because of the number of players it has produced this century.
  • It has been revealed that all born in 2001, Joao Pedro (Chelsea), Luiz Henrique (Zenit), Andre (Wolverhampton Wanderers) and Matheus Martinelli (still at Fluminense) shared what was called the 'Golden Generation' of Xerem.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 12:28.

In Brazil, Fluminense's youth academy is considered one of the best because of the number of players it has produced this century. And Xerem's greatest achievement was simultaneously having a generation of young players who reached the highest levels of world football.

It has been revealed that all born in 2001, Joao Pedro (Chelsea), Luiz Henrique (Zenit), Andre (Wolverhampton Wanderers) and Matheus Martinelli (still at Fluminense) shared what was called the 'Golden Generation' of Xerem. Evanilson (Bournemouth), who is older and was born in 1999, was also in the team with them at some point in the youth system.

Three players who play or have played in the Premier League. One who was at the last World Cup. And another who won the Copa Libertadores with Fluminense and is still a starter for the team. A very rare feat that, for Gustavo Leal, who coached this generation for four years, was no coincidence.

The coach, recently runner-up in the Canadian Premier League with Atletico Ottawa, spoke with Trivela last week and explained the secrets to such a decisive generation.

Leal progressed from the Under-13s to the Under-20s in Fluminense's youth system and led this special group for four years. From the privileged position he held in this process, he understands that it was no coincidence and that the club, through its training methodology, plays a significant role in the development of these athletes.

Recent findings suggest that 'I strongly believe in the process and I do not think it is a coincidence that so many good players are in the same generation. It was a combination of the individual quality of the athletes and the good professionals they worked with. Xerem has many good people in goalkeeper training, in the physical area and in psychology' - he said.

The 40-year-old coach highlighted that several coaches had led them, such as Leonardo Ramos in the Under-13s (now in the Under-20s at Internacional), Thiago Macedo (who was Gustavo Leal's assistant in jobs in Mexico and Chile) and Marcelo Veiga, who currently coordinates the Xerem youth academy.

'This generation went through many good coaches. And this, combined with the quality that these players already had, allowed us to have such a large number of top-level players in the same generation' - he added.

When asked by reporters who surprised him most in this golden generation, Leal immediately chose Joao Pedro.

He then pointed out that it was not necessarily a surprise, but that what the striker has achieved is impressive. The 25-year-old was voted Chelsea's best player by fans last season and is maintaining that form this season.

Recent findings suggest that 'We always saw that Joao Pedro had a different kind of quality. Ever since he arrived in the Under-13s, we could already tell he was a special player. I think that, however optimistic we are and however much we work with the players to help them reach their full potential, perhaps we cannot imagine that this potential will be realised so swiftly and at such a high level' - he commented.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jarrod Bowen has admitted that talks over his West Ham future will take place if a return to the Premier League is not secured this season.

The West Ham captain, who played his 300th game for the club this week, was the subject of Premier League interest at the end of last season following the club’s relegation to the second division for the first time in 14 years, but never considered leaving.

Bowen instead committed his immediate future to West Ham by signing a newly introduced contract, which included revised terms to help the club in their bid for promotion.

The 29-year-old says it was an easy decision to stay, but conversations will need to be had if West Ham are resigned to a second season in the second tier.

You don't want to be stuck, you want to bounce back and be in the Premier League straight away.

The Hammers have endured a tricky start to life in the Championship, and currently sit outside the play-off places and winless in four games under new manager Scott Parker.

“I never wanted to leave after being relegated,” Bowen tells Standard Sport.

“I always wanted to give it an opportunity, to go we can get this club back into the Premier League. I wanted to be the spearhead of that.

Gavin And Stacey props go to auction in aid of Cancer Research Wales.

West Ham fans ‘prepare for relegation’ as pressure mounts on newly introduced manager Parker.

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean.

Industry observers note that “I think it's wrong to look too far ahead into the future because I think your energy has to be into this season. But if it doesn't happen, then we will sit down and have a conversation at the end of the season.

“But I think for now, we have to put all our energy into this season because there's something special that we can achieve.”.

West Ham have struggled to adapt to the Championship, winning six of their opening 17 games, but Bowen claims this came as no surprise to him and believes promotion expert Parker can turn things around.

“He's been brilliant,” Bowen states of former Hammers midfielder Parker, who has earned promotion from the Championship on three seperate occasions. “Someone who understands the club, played so many years here, captained here at this club as well. He's been a breath of fresh air since he's been here.

According to recent reports, “We've only worked together a few weeks. Obviously, the results haven't been the way that we wanted. Some of the performances that we've had, we probably deserve more from some of the games.

“We feel we're in a weirdly good place, and we're looking forward to what we've got coming up.”.

An edgy 1-0 victory at Swansea last month felt at the time like the making of West Ham as promotion candidates, but they are yet to taste victory since Parker replaced Nuno Espirito Santo in the dugout last month.

The 1-0 defeat to Portsmouth this week prompted Parker to warn that West Ham risk getting stuck in the Championship if they do not adapt to the physical demands of the league.

And Bowen insists promotion back to the top flight is not as easy as some make out.

“Of course you don't want to be stuck,” he continued. “You want to bounce back and be in the Premier League straight away, of course you do.

“But like I noted, it's not as easy as what people think or just to expect. Just because you've come down, it'll be easy for you to get back promoted because that's not the case, and we're finding that out right now.”.

Bowen was speaking to Standard Sport at the EFL’s Power of 72 event at the London Stadium, promoting West Ham’s Thrive employability programme, which concentrates on providing support to Neet (not in education, employment or training) and underemployed young people in Newham and east London.

EFL Power of 72 celebrates the positive impact EFL Clubs have on their communities and the bond between clubs and local people, with one million people participating in EFL club charity programmes every season.

“It's so notable to me because it's something that I've been involved in for a few years now since I've been here,” Bowen said of the Thrive employability programme.

“We have people with different backgrounds, different upbringings, that all have limited opportunities to go out and showcase that. So, the work we're doing is giving them the opportunity to go and showcase what they want to do, giving them the work experience to go on and achieve what they set out to do.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • European shares fell sharply in early trading on Friday as a global sell-off fueled by concerns over artificial intelligence stocks spread from Wall Street to Asia and Europe.
  • Fears of curbs on AI data-center spending have added to investors' concerns after Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress.
  • The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 1.6% in early trading, wiping out its gains for the week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European shares fell sharply in early trading on Friday as a global sell-off fueled by concerns over artificial intelligence stocks spread from Wall Street to Asia and Europe.

Fears of curbs on AI data-center spending have added to investors' concerns after Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 1.6% in early trading, wiping out its gains for the week. Most major European markets fell more than 1%, with media, healthcare and retail stocks leading the declines.

European markets had previously weathered the week's turbulence better than their Asian and US counterparts because of their more limited exposure to AI stocks.

Earlier, Japanese and South Korean shares tumbled after a massive selloff in tech stocks on Wall Street the previous day.

Sources indicate that tokyo's benchmark Nikkei 225 index fell 5.5% in early trade, while Seoul's tech-heavy Kospi index slid as much as 8.8%, triggering a circuit breaker which suspended trading for 20 minutes. Taiwan's benchmark TAIEX index was also down more than 8%.

Asian tech giants including Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) have borne the brunt of the artificial intelligence-related selloff.

Samsung plunged nearly 10% while SK Hynix slid over 11%.

Chip-related shares in Japan also took a beating, with Tokyo Electron stock trading down around 9% and Kioxia shedding 13%.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US markets were hammered on Thursday by a sharp retreat in tech stocks, particularly those involved in the buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure like data centers.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 5.52% and shed as much as $2.5 trillion (roughly €2.23 trillion) in market value, while the broader S&P 500 index plunged 4.4%.

The rout occurred as investors grow increasingly anxious about the colossal AI spending plans and whether they will eventually produce commensurate profits.

The results of the US midterm elections, which saw Democrats seize control of both houses of US Congress, added to the concerns.

A number of Democratic governors-elect campaigned on slowing artificial intelligence development and promised to stop or pause the construction of data centers amid growing public opposition to such projects.

"It's pretty clear there's been a real shift ​in sentiment," Michael McCarthy, chief executive for Australia and Upcoming Zealand at online brokerage Moomoo, told the Reuters news agency.

"Market turning points are often accompanied by strong disagreement, and that shows up in the market ​by huge swings in either direction," he said. "That's what we appear to have had — and last night's emphatic sell-down suggests that is the direction that we're now headed in.".

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 17:09 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 18:48 EST, 25 November 2026.

Andoni Iraola tried to stifle a smirk on Tuesday when it was put to him that he had a fair chance of completing a perfect week by thrashing Manchester United, winning away in Europe and then winning his first-ever Merseyside Derby.

The usual responses came back of remaining level-headed and not getting carried away, of course – but Iraola has ticked off two of those three tasks and now goes to Everton with his much-criticised, substantial-money signings in the form of their Liverpool careers.

That is Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, of course, who both scored here to further quash any narratives over them being expensive flops, a debate which had followed them for much of their first year or so on Merseyside.

Isak scored a brace to take his season tally to double-figures and make it six away games in a row where he has struck, while Wirtz followed up his best performance of the season against United with a fine strike from distance.

Wirtz especially has never been far away from criticism during his time at the club but is silencing his doubters every week and said this week that Iraola had helped him rediscover the player Liverpool thought they were buying for £116million two summers ago.

It has been revealed that the sentiment spreads beyond Wirtz. After a season of strife, Iraola has brought the feel-good factor back at Anfield and supporters are enjoying watching their team again after a year in which it felt like a chore to do so some weeks.

Alexander Isak scored twice as Liverpool beat Club Brugge 3-0 in the Champions League.

That made it three wins in a row for the Reds as they start to really click under Andoni Iraola.

CLUB BRUGGE (4-3-3): Sommer 4; Sabbe 5 (Siquet 84), Spileers 5, Mechele 6, Seys 6; Vetlesen 6 (Vermant 75), Potts 7 (Tsawa 84), Vanaken 6; Forbs 7, Tresoldi 6, Lemarechal 7 (Diakhon 75).

Subs not used: Jackers, Vanden Driessche, Han-beom Lee, Virgili, Dams, Robberechts, Audoor, Vasovic.

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 7; Frimpong 6 (Van Dijk 73, 6), Araujo 6, Jacquet 7, Kerkez 6; Nyoni 7 (Mac Allister 73, 6), Szoboszlai 7; Munoz 6 (Ngumoha 42, 6), Wirtz 7, Barcola 6 (Chambers 86); ISAK 8 (Koumas 86).

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Tsimikas, McConnell, Danns.

Scorers: Isak 13, 82, Wirtz 79.

Referee: Alejandro Hernandez (Esp) 6.

It is making the Liverpool fans fall for Iraola a little bit more each week. How that feeling would be turbocharged with Derby delight at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday.

Sources indicate that ‘I was very pleased with the result and the performance overall,’ mentioned Iraola. ‘At 3-0, you can think it was an easy game and I don’t think it was. We were facing a really good team.’.

As the 1,000 or so travelling Kop enjoyed their strong Belgian beers and chocolate waffles in this quaint, picturesque city, they were still laughing about poor old Manchester United and Sunday’s 4-0 demolition job.

This was a much tougher test against an opposition that had started well in the Champions League with three wins from four, so Liverpool’s performance was never going to be as convincing – but the victory was still vital.

It helped them take a step closer to cementing a top eight place in this long-winded league phase. That would ease the pressure on a congested calendar by seeing them not only be able to rest players in the latter games of the league stage but also skip a play-off round.

It has been revealed that club Brugge are no mugs and they indicated that, with energetic winger Carlos Forbs the pick of the bunch. The former Manchester City academy starlet has inherited a certain Cristiano Ronaldo’s No 7 shirt at Portugal and gave Milos Kerkez a testing night here.

It has been revealed that the Belgian side, like Liverpool, had won three of their first four European games including victory away to Inter. They had won five of the last seven league titles with a brave playing style that Iraola admitted was a pleasure to analyse – which he added was not always the case.

Their bold approach was their undoing here, though, with possession tossed away far too easily for Liverpool’s opener after 13 minutes. Yann Sommer, in the winter of his career at 37, passed straight to Bradley Barcola who, via stand-in skipper Dominik Szoboszlai, found Isak.

It has been revealed that the Swede needed no second invitation to fire home his ninth goal of the season. Isak had been rested for most of Liverpool’s early European outings but was the difference here and loves playing away: he has now netted on his last six games away from Anfield.

Liverpool have 12 points from five games and will almost certainly be in the knockout stages.

Florian Wirtz continued his fine form as he curled in a delightful effort to put Liverpool 2-0 up.

Iraola will hope to make it the perfect week with victory in Sunday's Merseyside Derby.

In a recent development, only Mohamed Salah has done so in seven or more in recent history for Liverpool. Everton would be a fine place to match that record.

Despite the scoreline flattering Liverpool, things were far from easy after Isak’s opener. Alisson was needed to deny Felix Lemarechal both sides at half-time and Virgil van Dijk – rested from the start – was called on as a second-half substitute to steady the ship.

Sources indicate that winger Victor Munoz limped off in agony after going down before half-time holding his knee. Iraola feared the worst when a stretcher was called but the Spaniard walked off and was feeling ‘optimistic’ after the match, according to the boss.

Szoboszlai should have put the game to bed after a sublime team move led to the Hungarian being thwarted by Sommer at point-blank range, while Barcola was also guilty of wastefulness after getting his feet tangled up when in a dangerous position.

But Wirtz, in the best form of his Liverpool career, made it three goals in his last three with a fine strike from distance that clipped in off the post.

Sources indicate that then Isak raced through on goal and dinked a shot over Sommer for goal No 10 of the season for him. It completed a memorable night for Iraola and his big-money boys. Now to make it a perfect week at Everton on Sunday.

Liverpool are looking up as the hectic period of the campaign approaches.

Andoni Iraola's side have bounced back from successive defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce prior to the November international break, and go into the Everton game seeking a fourth straight win across all competitions.

While Sunday’s showdown at the Hill Dickinson Stadium will represent Iraola’s first taste of a Merseyside derby, history largely favours the Reds having lost just one of the last 10 meetings.

It remains to be seen if Victor Munoz is able to shake off a knock and prove his fitness, but two key Liverpool players will have to be careful if selected due to the looming threat of a ban.

With that in mind, here’s a look at the Liverpool players at risk of suspension.

As every club have already been made fully aware of this season, players who pick up five yellow cards in the first 19 matches of the Premier League season are hit with a one-match ban.

Liverpool's cut-off point in which suspensions will be handed out for a fifth yellow card is the home game against Coventry on January 2, 2027. From there, players who are booked 10 times in the first 32 matches of the campaign are suspended for two games.

Alexis Mac Allister and summer signing Bradley Barcola are the significant suspensions concern for Liverpool at present.

The Argentina international was booked in the win over Crystal Palace so had to watch his step in the 4-0 thrashing of Manchester United, but Barcola is a upcoming suspension risk after being cautioned in the second half last weekend.

As such, if the Frenchman and/or Mac Allister are shown a yellow card in the Merseyside derby, a one-match ban must be served in the very next fixture - at home to Sunderland on December 2.

Ultimately, the pair are walking the disciplinary tightrope for upcoming games against Everton, Sunderland, Chelsea, Leeds, Tottenham, Hull, Aston Villa and Coventry.

Furthermore, with Liverpool taking on Chelsea next weekend, Barcola and/or Mac Allister would be suspended for the trip to Stamford Bridge if either are booked against the Black Cats.

Ronald Araujo, Milos Kerkez and Virgil van Dijk are on three yellow cards, while Jeremy Jacquet and Munoz are among a host of Liverpool players still in danger of being suspended.

Latest Update: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1023 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.
  • The question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care.
  • Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.

The question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care. In the US, that shift is reaching hospital standards. From January 2027, breast cancer centers must screen patients' physical function and recommend exercise or physical therapy where needed.

Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.

Recent findings suggest that the 2025 trial, called CHALLENGE, was led by the Canadian Cancer Trials Group. It began enrolling patients in 2009 and published its results in 2025.

The trial's 889 participants came from six countries, most from Canada and Australia. All had finished surgery and chemotherapy for stage 2 or 3 colon cancer, which had not spread to distant organs.

Recent findings suggest that half received only health education materials on exercise and healthy eating. The other half additionally met a physical activity consultant for three years.

In the exercise group, the target was similar to adding 45 to 60 minutes of brisk walking, three to four times a week. The amount and type of activity varied from person to person, stated Tormod Skogstad Nilsen, a cancer exercise researcher in Norway. But he said participants achieved lasting increases in their physical activity.

Sources indicate that exercise helped. People in the exercise group were less likely to see their cancer come back, to develop a new cancer or to die. In all, 93 had at least one of these setbacks, compared with 131 in the health education group.

Industry observers note that in cancer research, living longer usually means a larger share of people is still alive at a given point. It does not promise anyone a set number of extra years.

Eight years after joining CHALLENGE, about 90 of every 100 people in the exercise group were alive, compared with about 83 of every 100 in the health education group. That is about 7% more people alive in the group who had guided exercise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, for people without cancer, the evidence comes from studies that follow people's habits and health over many years. These can show a link, but not prove cause and effect. Active people may also eat better or smoke less.

In another 2025 study, more than 85,000 adults in the United Kingdom wore a wrist tracker for a week. Over about six years, those who moved most had a 26% lower risk of 13 cancers, including breast and colorectal cancer, than those who moved least.

Sources indicate that even light activity, such as household chores, was linked to lower risk. The link held after researchers accounted for lifestyle, weight and other health conditions.

Sources indicate that earlier research, based on people's self-reporting, has led to similar conclusions. A 2016 analysis of 1.44 million adults in the US and Europe linked free-time activity to a lower risk of many cancers, largely regardless of weight or smoking.

A trial to prove prevention is unlikely: Many cancers take years to develop, so it would need huge numbers of people followed for a long time.

Sources indicate that CHALLENGE included only people with colon cancer. But how it picked participants offers a clue: Before joining, they had to pass a fitness test.

Anna Campbell, a professor of clinical exercise science at Edinburgh Napier University in Scotland, sees that as a guide.

"I think patients with any other cancer stage II and III who have a reasonable baseline level of fitness and no major comorbidities that would prevent them from undertaking moderate to vigorous activity could be considered for similar interventions," she mentioned. Comorbidities are other health conditions.

Nilsen noted some people decline to join exercise trials because they feel too unwell or tired, or do not want to exercise. "Hence, study populations are typically younger, 'healthier', and most times slightly more motivated compared to a clinical population," he said.

The coaching aimed to make activity a lasting habit, and Campbell stated that is where the trial's value lies.

"The main success of the study is that it enabled the participants to become independent exercisers staying active in a safe and effective and individualized way," she mentioned.

Nilsen agreed. Helping people become more active "in their own environment," without depending on a well-equipped training center, "would likely lead to more sustainable activity behavioral changes," he said.

He is wary of fixed targets, however. "Exercise should be tailored to each individual and the challenges they face, rather than striving to reach a given minimum of exercise required," though health care resources may not always allow it, he added.

According to recent reports, in a 2024 survey of 549 people with cancer, only one in 10 had been referred to an exercise service. Yet almost three in four thought their oncologist should raise the subject.

According to recent reports, "There are some excellent examples of effective pathways but these are few and far between," said Campbell. Good services bring everyone on board, from surgeons to community fitness instructors.

"Ideally, one person in the clinical setting needs to champion the program to link all the team together.".

Sources indicate that campbell expects CHALLENGE's regular coaching will be cut back in everyday care. Apps and live online group sessions could still work, she remarked, if run by properly trained staff.

One recent study of live online exercise engaged patients from poorer backgrounds, in rural areas and with advanced cancer. "It answered some of the barriers, such as cost, travel and lack of confidence," she mentioned.

Patients can ask their care team what exercise is safe for them and what support exists.

Recent findings suggest that according to Nilsen, a training session can bring structure and company. "You made it here, despite your feeling unwell or fatigued this morning, so you feel mastery based on that," he said.

Unai Emery's side make the trip to Portman Road sitting in the bottom half of the Premier League table.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.

“At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play,” noted Sage, speaking to PalaceTV.

It has been revealed that “I think we didn’t play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

“When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half.”.

Sage’s side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that victory, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his team, but on Thursday night was left ruing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season’s Conference League winners.

Sources indicate that sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month spell with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner’s, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

He told Uefa: “It’s a very disappointing return because we lost. I can’t take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn’t there.

“The scoreline may have been close, but there was a substantial difference in the way the two teams played.

“We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.

“I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half.”.

The veteran captain noted: “It has been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it so we’re very happy with the performance.”.

When asked about Evanilson’s header, which Smith supplied the assist for, he replied: “It wasn’t my best cross but I put it in an area, what a finish from him and I think we deserved that little bit of luck.

“From there on we went on to win the game but in the second half we got a little bit tired but the quality that came off the bench is great and we look forward to Sunday now.

“It’s a great header, he deserved it because he has worked very hard this season and many more to come from him.”.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Thursday night’s European football with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in Europa League action, and Brighton hosting Kauno Zalgiris in the Uefa Conference League.

Palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

In a recent development, palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

Bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Sunderland travel to Portuguese side Torreense, while Sturm Graz are the opposition for Bournemouth’s first ever European game at the Vitality Stadium (or Dean Court if you prefer). Bournemouth continue to be without Justin Kluivert, Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott because of injury.

Brighton are favourites to win the Conference League and play their first game in the competition against Lithuanian club Kauno Zalgiris. Lifting the trophy in Istanbul at the end of the season would assure Brighton of a place in next season’s Europa League, though given their Premier League form and Manchester City’s predicament, Champions League qualification could be a realistic aspiration. Brighton won with 10 men at Sunderland on Saturday, and were successful in their appeal against Pascal Struijk’s red card.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United will have Leny Yoro available for selection against Brentford this weekend, though a fellow defender remains at risk of a Premier League suspension.
  • Yoro was dismissed after just eight minutes in Man United’s defeat to Liverpool last Sunday, as Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge after succeeding Michael Carrick as head coach swiftly turned into a nightmare.
  • The Frenchman was given his marching orders for bringing down Alexander Isak just outside the box, with the Premier League revealing the red card was shown to the United defender “for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO)”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United will have Leny Yoro available for selection against Brentford this weekend, though a fellow defender remains at risk of a Premier League suspension.

Yoro was dismissed after just eight minutes in Man United’s defeat to Liverpool last Sunday, as Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge after succeeding Michael Carrick as head coach swiftly turned into a nightmare.

The Frenchman was given his marching orders for bringing down Alexander Isak just outside the box, with the Premier League revealing the red card was shown to the United defender “for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO)”.

However, Man Utd appealed the decision and it has proven successful with Yoro cleared to face Brentford on Saturday.

A statement from the FA read: “Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a claim of wrongful dismissal.

“The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.”.

Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a claim of wrongful dismissal.

According to recent reports, united have had to deal with their fair share of suspensions already this season. Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Matheus Cunha and, more recently, Youri Tielemans, have all been sent-off at some point to raise concerns over a disciplinary concern within the squad.

A further suspension concern is in the form of central defender Harry Maguire, who is presently on four Premier League yellow cards.

As per the rules, players who pick up five yellow cards in the first 19 matches of the Premier League season are hit with a one-match ban.

Man United's cut-off point in which suspensions will be handed out for a fifth yellow card is the away game against Brighton on January 2, 2027. From there, players who are booked 10 times in the first 32 matches of the campaign are suspended for two games.

Maguire’s Premier League yellow cards this season have come against Everton, Manchester City, Bournemouth and Chelsea.

As such, if the central defender is booked against Brentford, he will have to serve a one-match ban against Newcastle at St James’ Park on December 2.

Even if Maguire avoids a yellow card, he will still be walking the disciplinary tightrope in upcoming games against Newcastle, Coventry, Crystal Palace, Arsenal, Nottingham Forest, Sunderland and Brighton.

The other Man United players in danger of a Premier League ban are Bruno Fernandes, Diogo Dalot, Ayden Heaven, Bryan Mbeumo, Andrey Santos and Luke Shaw, all on two yellow cards.

A club statement remarked: "Alessandro Bastoni underwent clinical and diagnostic tests this morning at the Humanitas Institute in Rozzano.

"The tests revealed a strain to his left quadriceps.".

Inter did not offer a timeline for Bastoni's recovery, but with widespread reports indicating he could miss at least three weeks, he may not return until the newly introduced year.

Senne Lammens' two errors cost Man United victory at Sporting.

Man United have received five red cards and conceded five penalties in just 17 games across all competitions this season.

Hearts welcome Scottish Premiership leaders Celtic to Tynecastle Park for a matchday 15 showdown on Sunday.

The hosts are fourth in the Scottish Premiership table with 23 points from 13 games, while the visitors are top of the standings with 34 points after 14 matches.

Hearts head into Sunday's match off the back of a disappointing run of results, having recorded just one win and suffered four defeats in their last five matches.

The sole victory came in their last Scottish Premiership outing, with the Jambos sensationally defeating Dundee 8-0, a result that continued a trend of high-scoring fixtures for Hearts this term.

Hearts have been one of the most entertaining teams to follow in the Scottish Premiership this season, scoring 34 goals - the most in the division - and conceding a significant 22 times.

The Jambos have been involved in several blockbuster encounters, including the 8-0 win against Dundee and a 5-0 triumph over St Mirren, although they have also been on the wrong end of such scorelines.

Wouter Vrancken's side have lost 5-2 to Falkirk and suffered a humiliating 7-1 defeat against upcoming opponents Celtic on matchday nine, leaving the Jambos eager to exact their revenge on Sunday.

Celtic, meanwhile, are among the highest scorers in the Scottish Premiership, with 32 goals scored, but also boast the best defensive record in the division, conceding only 11 times.

The Bhoys head into the weekend placed at the top of the table with 34 points from 14 league matches, although second-placed Rangers may have moved top of the table by the time of Sunday's kick-off.

Celtic, regardless of Rangers' result, will be eager to maintain or extend their lead at the top of the standings, leaving Martin O'Neill aiming for a 12th win in 15 league games.

The league leaders will travel to Tynecastle confident of claiming all three points, especially after their 7-1 victory earlier in the campaign and their recent return to winning ways after a challenging period between mid-September and early November.

Celtic managed just three wins, one draw and suffered six defeats during that time, but they have since bounced back with four straight victories ahead of this encounter with the Jambos.

Arsenal take on Manchester City in the standout Premier League fixture this weekend, though it will be played in the backdrop of uncertainty.

While it is first against third and a showdown between last season’s top two, the outcome at the Emirates Stadium may not have too much of an impact on this year’s title race.

This is because Man City head to north London on the back of being handed an enhancement on their appeal against the Premier League's financial charges.

Back in October, City were in October found guilty of 114 breaches of the league's financial rules, with an independent commission concluding the club had used "sham" commercial contracts to disguise more than £830million in funding between 2009 and 2018.

City, however, have consistently denied wrongdoing, and an appeal was immediately released with a result expected in early 2027.

Speculation over possible punishments, should Man City’s appeal prove unsuccessful, range from a fine to various points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.

Meanwhile, senior figures at some Premier League clubs have told BBC Sport that Man City’s owners must be forced to sell up as punishment for its breaking financial rules.

Below is a breakdown of what sanctions Man City could potentially face if their appeal is unsuccessful.

Expulsion from the Premier League: The most severe sanction could see Man City removed from the Premier League and relegated to the Championship, with any decision subject to the relevant league rules and the outcome of any appeal.

Suspension from Premier League matches: Another potential sanction would be a suspension. The club could potentially be suspended from participating in Premier League fixtures for a specified period.

More London travel chaos as weekend Tube and rail closures follow end of strike.

Man Utd defender at risk of suspension after Leny Yoro red card appeal.

Liverpool handed latest suspension risk ahead of Chelsea clash.

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean.

Points deduction: A significant deduction in points could be imposed, either during the current season or in a future campaign.

The size and timing of any deduction would be determined as part of the sanctions process.

Stripping of titles and trophies: Retrospective sporting penalties could also potentially affect honours that were won during the period covered by the charges.

In this scenario, Arsenal would not be awarded a single retrospective Premier League title. This is because the seasons in which they finished runners-up to Man City has not been under investigation. The Gunners would, though get a League Cup after being demolished 3-0 by City in the 2017-18 final at Wembley.

However, no decision has been made to strip City of any titles or trophies.

Transfer restrictions: The club could potentially face restrictions on registering or signing players for one or more transfer windows.

Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (746 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.
  • About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.
  • It is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.

About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.

It is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK). And it's been up and running for more than two decades.

Recent findings suggest that the first LÜKEX in 2004 dealt with the scenario of an extreme winter with a major power outage. Lessons from that exercise proved valuable in 2005 when the Münsterland region of North Rhine-Westphalia — Germany's most populous state — experienced the worst power outage in the country's postwar history. When heavy snowfall caused power lines to collapse, leaving 250,000 people without electricity for days, there was a better understanding of who to contact and where the bottlenecks were.

Since it first started, LÜKEX has trained for scenarios involving terror attacks, an influenza pandemic, biological health threats, storm floods in northern Germany and gas shortages in southern Germany. The most recent exercise in 2023 simulated a cyberattack targeting government operations.

With the help of other ministries, the German Weather Service and the Federal Institute of Hydrology, the BBK developed a drought risk analysis to serve as the scenario.

Participants, which include aid organizations Malteser and the German Red Cross, didn't know the specifics of the challenges they would be facing until the exercise kicked off on Wednesday.

Industry observers note that at that point, they were told it was July 20, 2027. In that simulated future, they find themselves in a Germany that has been struggling with extreme heat for weeks; water levels in rivers are falling, food supplies are becoming scarce and emergency services are under growing pressure.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that patrick Pöhler, spokesperson for Malteser, said additional details include supermarkets having run out of water, collapsed supply chains and skyrocketing prices to enter a swimming pool. He said the scenario also goes into how the situation is impacting sections of society.

"Emergency services and elderly care are areas that require particular attention," Pöhler mentioned. "The increasingly extreme summers of recent years have shown how severely heat can affect staffing levels and operational capacity.".

In its scenario, the northern port city of Hamburg is tasked with managing the disruption of key transport routes that are impacting access to food and drinking water, as well as handling disinformation attacks that are fueling public fear.

According to recent reports, "We have not conducted an exercise of this magnitude since the end of the Cold War. Yet such preparations are essential to strengthen our resilience and crisis-response capabilities," said Hamburg's minister for the interior, Andy Grote.

LÜKEX is designed to test and strengthen the country's ability to manage major crises at a strategic level. No matter the specific scenario, they all help test internal structures, workflows and decision-making processes.

"The lessons learned are continuously incorporated into improving preparedness, planning and cooperation in civil protection," said BBK spokesperson Katharina Böcker.

Recent findings suggest that this year's topic was decided a long time ago, well before recent summers in which Germany experienced extreme heat, she added. Thousands of people died from heat-related causes during the hot months of this year.

"Crises such as extreme heat waves and prolonged droughts can affect large parts of the population and challenge the operational capabilities of our critical structures over an extended period," said Christian Reuter, secretary general of the German Red Cross, another organization taking part.

Observers take note of how organizations react in the crisis scenario to find out what went well and where things didn't run smoothly.

"We are explicitly encouraged to make mistakes," mentioned Malteser's Pöhler, because that is how weaknesses can be identified and addressed.

A first internal debrief is scheduled for Friday, he added.

A preliminary report with the main findings and respective recommendations is due to be published in the first quarter of next year. A full evaluation report will then be released later in the third quarter of 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla owner Elon Musk said on Friday that the manufacturer would scale down production of the Cybertruck at its Austin factory in the coming year.

  • "Tesla will be winding down production of the cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk mentioned on his X social media site.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla owner Elon Musk said on Friday that the manufacturer would scale down production of the Cybertruck at its Austin factory in the coming year.

The South African entrepreneur remarked Tesla would be scaling back production of his futuristic but often-mocked pickup truck and amping up production of what he hopes will soon become a fleet of fully automated taxis.

"Tesla will be winding down production of the cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk mentioned on his X social media site.

The announcement follows a bruising week for Musk amid the US midterm elections, where Republicans struggled despite his major donations, with his companies losing billions in value by market capitalization as investors sought to ditch stock.

Musk later responded to a complimentary user online who hailed the Cybertruck as the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made," and calling it an "end of an era" by saying: "True.".

For years he had poured much of his enthusiastic marketing zeal into promoting the Cybertruck, saying during the 2023 launch "finally, the future will look like the future.".

However the oversized body, straight lines and stainless steel and the post-apocalpytic vibe these created also met with widespread criticism and even mockery.

The electric powertrain was probably a barrier to sales in the US, by far the biggest pickup truck market, where Musk had hoped to take on some of the country's top-selling gas-guzzling vehicles like the Ford F150 or the Chevrolet Silverado and the Dodge Ram.

Meanwhile, the car's striking shape, weight and size made it impossible for Tesla to try to crack Europe, where electric vehicles are gaining a much larger market share.

In a recent development, unlike in the US, EU safety regulations place considerable emphasis not just on people in cars in accidents, but also on the dangers posed to pedestrians who might be hit by a vehicle. That meant it was not possible for Tesla to register and sell the Cybertruck for road use in Europe.

Beyond this, the vehicle's size would likely have rendered it impractical and unpopular on many European roads, where space tends to be at more of a premium.

Depending how quick the wind-down proves to be, the Cybertruck's production run could prove shorter than its five-year R&D phase.

Given its longstanding concerns meeting Musk's very public sales and production predictions, Tesla does not publish sales figures broken down by model.

But according to the automotive data platform Kelley Blue Book, the manufacturer sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, down from 38,965 in 2024.

At launch in 2023, Musk had predicted unit sales nearer a quarter of a million.

Industry observers note that for orientation, Ford sold more than 800,000 F-Series pickups in the US last year, a slight boost on 2024's numbers. These vehicles start at less than half the list price of a Cybertruck in the US.

The IPO for SpaceX this year revealed that Musk's second-largest company was comfortably the biggest buyer of Cybertrucks in 2025. It bought vehicles worth $131 million and did not even enjoy a bulk-buy or friends-rate discount, paying list prices for the fleet.

The Cybercab is a vehicular element in Musk's bid to transform Tesla towards a company focused more on AI and robotics than automobilies.

Rather than just featuring the self-drive or driving assistance programs that Musk has been championing for years, the Cybercab has no steering wheels, pedals or mirrors at all and is designed never to have a human in control.

Musk say the model will be the tech giant's main autonomous model and will supply a global network of Robotaxis.

According to recent reports, starting in the past few months, around 300 such vehicles have been registered and have started operating, on approved roads in the Austin area near Tesla's Gigafactory Texas. They're being added to the existing fleet of autonomous Model Y Teslas being used for the purpose, serving in an area known as a geofence of around 680 square kilometers (264 square miles).

Cancer-associated mutations in PIK3CA underlie congenital overgrowth disorders that frequently involve the vasculature1,2. Among the affected tissues, the endothelium commonly exhibits aberrant expansion, leading to vascular malformations3. Notably, these lesions arise predominantly in veins and capillaries, whereas arteries are largely spared, for reasons that remain unclear. Here, using genetic lineage tracing, we show that endothelial expression of PIK3CAH1047R drives profound clonal expansion of capillary and venous endothelial cells, whereas mature arterial endothelial cells are refractory to pathological PI3K activation. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features, providing a mechanistic explanation for the paucity of arterial lesions after PIK3CA genetic perturbation. Mechanistically, these effects are mediated by two complementary downstream branches of PI3K signalling: increased proliferation, which drives vascular overgrowth, and upregulation of the venous-specifying transcription factor NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), which suppresses arterial differentiation. Together, our findings reveal that pathogenic responses to PIK3CAH1047R are dictated by endothelial differentiation state and fate trajectory, and demonstrate that arterial endothelium is intrinsically resistant to oncogenic PI3K signalling. Arteries are therefore shielded from PIK3CA mutations, explaining the rarity of arterial malformations in PIK3CA-driven disease.

It has been revealed that somatic and germline pathogenic variants in cancer-associated genes cause diverse congenital disorders1,2 and are also found in phenotypically normal tissue4,5. Germline mutations may be inherited or arise de novo, whereas somatic mutations, acquired during embryonic development, generate mosaicism and a broad spectrum of phenotypes1. Understanding how identical mutations produce distinct outcomes across tissues is crucial for defining cellular susceptibility to disease and explaining the phenotypic heterogeneity.

In a recent development, PIK3CA encodes p110α, the catalytic subunit of phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3Kα), which regulates cell growth, proliferation, migration and metabolism6 through AKT and downstream effectors, including mTOR and forkhead box O (FOXO) transcription factors7,8. PIK3CA is an oncogene that is frequently mutated in both mosaic congenital disorders9 and phenotypically normal tissue4. Activating mutations occur throughout the coding sequence, with recurrent hotspots including E545K, E542K, H1047R and H1047L3. Mesoderm-derived tissues, including the endothelium, are commonly affected in PIK3CA-related congenital disorders, which manifest as aberrant tissue overgrowth and vascular malformations10,11,12,13. Although PIK3CA mutations have been extensively studied in adult epithelial tissues14,15,16,17, their effects on cellular heterogeneity, differentiation and clonal dynamics in mesoderm-derived lineages remain poorly understood.

Vascular malformations are congenital vascular anomalies classified as slow-flow lesions, affecting capillaries, veins and lymphatic vessels or fast-flow lesions, often involving arteries18. Somatic activating PIK3CA mutations occur in the endothelium of all major slow-flow vascular malformations, where lesion expansion requires mitogenic signals, even though the mutation alone is insufficient to confer a proliferative advantage19,20,21,22. By contrast, no evidence presently implicates PIK3CA mutations in fast-flow arterial malformations3. Whether arterial endothelial cells have these mutations but resist their effects, or mutant clones are negatively selected or eliminated in arterial vessels remains unclear.

According to recent reports, here we demonstrate that endothelial responses to oncogenic PIK3CAH1047R are governed by cellular identity and developmental trajectory. Combining mosaic genetics, lineage tracing and single-cell analyses, we identify a differentiation-stage-specific window of susceptibility to pathological PI3K signalling, while fully differentiated arterial endothelial cells are resistant. These findings provide a framework for the tissue and vessel-type specificity of PIK3CA-driven vascular malformations.

In a recent development, postnatal expression of Pik3caH1047R (Pik3catm1.1Waph/+) from the endogenous locus in mouse retinal endothelial cells using Pdgfb-creERT2 results in venous and capillary malformations, whereas arteries remain unaffected19 (Extended Data Fig. 1a–e). To correlate these phenotypes with the distribution of mutant cells, we introduced the R26-mTmG reporter allele into the Pik3caH1047RPdgfb-creERT2 mice (pan-endothelial (pEC)-GFP-Pik3caH1047R; Fig. 1a). Tamoxifen-mediated Cre activation induced recombination of the endogenous Pik3caH1047R allele and the reporter, resulting in membrane-bound GFP expression that marks recombined cells and therefore approximates Pik3caH1047R-expressing endothelial cells. Pdgfb-creERT2R26-mTmG mice were used as controls (pEC-GFP). After low-dose administration of 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OHT) at postnatal day 1 (P1), retinas were analysed at P6 (Extended Data Fig. 1c). Mosaic recombination was observed throughout the vascular plexus in both genotypes (Fig. 1b). Although GFP+ mutant cells were present in all vessel types, vascular malformations occurred exclusively in capillaries and veins (Fig. 1c,d). In these vessels, mutant GFP+ endothelial cells underwent marked clonal expansion, generating enlarged vascular tubes (Fig. 1d,e and Extended Data Fig. 1f), accompanied by increased endothelial cell proliferation during early lesion formation (Extended Data Fig. 1g–i). By contrast, Pik3caH1047R GFP+ cells in arteries neither expanded nor altered vessel width (Fig. 1d,e and Extended Data Fig. 1f). Consistent with these phenotypes, capillary and venous mutant GFP+ cells displayed increased PI3K pathway activation, as assessed by staining of phosphorylated S6 (p-S6), whereas arterial mutant cells highlighted no detectable increase relative to wild-type (WT) cells (Fig. 1d,f). These data show that Pik3caH1047R endothelial cells selectively expand in capillaries and veins, while arteries remain structurally and molecularly normal despite containing mutant cells.

Recent findings suggest that the apparent resistance of arterial endothelial cells to Pik3caH1047R prompted us to directly investigate the behaviour of mutant cells in arteries. To this end, we used the Bmx(PAC)-creERT2 mouse line, which specifically targets arterial endothelial cells in retinal vessels. WT and Pik3caH1047R arterial endothelial cells (aEC) were traced by combining Bmx(PAC)-creERT2 and R26-mTmG with or without the Pik3caH1047R allele (aEC-GFP and aEC-GFP-Pik3caH1047R; Fig. 1g). Bmx(PAC)-creERT2-mediated tracing revealed robust arterial recombination after 4-OHT administration at P4 or P7, whereas induction at P1 did not label arterial endothelial cells (Extended Data Fig. 2a,b). Thus, recombination was induced at P4 or P7 for subsequent experiments. In both settings, the proportion of GFP+ cells and arterial vessel width were comparable between the mutant and control retinas (Fig. 1h–j and Extended Data Fig. 2c–f). Arteries also displayed similar smooth-muscle-cell coverage and maintained expression of arterial markers UNC5B and CX37 (Extended Data Fig. 2g–j). Moreover, GFP+ arterial endothelial cells of both genotypes lacked expression of NR2F2, a key transcription factor that suppresses arterial identity23,24,25,26 (Extended Data Fig. 2k,l). Consistent with earlier observations, mutant GFP+ cells showed low PI3K pathway activation, with no increase relative to controls (Fig. 1i,k and Extended Data Fig. 2m,n). To assess the long-term effects, we analysed retinas at P21. No differences were detected in the GFP+ cell distribution, arterial morphology or NR2F2 expression between WT and Pik3caH1047R cells in main arteries and arteriolar branches (Extended Data Fig. 2o–q). These findings show that mutant cells persist in arteries or arteriolar branches without detectable changes in arterial identity, morphology or PI3K activation, supporting the resistance of differentiated arterial endothelial cells to Pik3caH1047R.

To investigate why arterial endothelial cells are protected against Pik3caH1047R, we pharmacologically disrupted key arterial features in aEC-GFP and aEC-GFP-Pik3caH1047R pups. As arterial endothelial cells experience higher shear stress, we first reduced systemic blood pressure with the angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor captopril27. Although captopril reduced KLF4 expression and induced dilation of the vascular plexus28, it did not alter the proportion of GFP+ cells or arterial width. Furthermore, endothelial proliferation was not increased in mutant arteries (Extended Data Fig. 3a–d). We next inhibited Notch signalling, a key regulator of arterial differentiation and maintenance, using N-[N-(3,5-difluorophenacetyl)-l-alanyl]-S-phenylglycine t-butyl ester (DAPT). Despite a pronounced response in sprouting capillaries, DAPT likewise did not elicit any response in arteries to Pik3caH1047R expression (Extended Data Fig. 3a,e,f). Collectively, these results indicate that inhibition of major arterial identity programmes alone is insufficient to overcome arterial resistance to Pik3caH1047R.

To test whether resistance to Pik3caH1047R emerges during arterial differentiation, we traced tip endothelial cells—a pre-arterial population that contributes to arterial growth29,30. We used the Esm1(BAC)-creERT2 mouse line, which specifically marks tip cells, crossed with R26-mTmG (tEC-GFP) alone or in combination with Pik3caH1047R (tEC-GFP-Pik3caH1047R; Fig. 2a). 4-OHT was administered at P1, and Esm1-GFP+ progeny were analysed at different timepoints (Fig. 2b and Extended Data Fig. 4a). Then, 24 h after induction, GFP+ cells were predominantly localized at the sprouting front (Fig. 2b). By P6, GFP+ cells contributed extensively to arteries in tEC-GFP retinas, and the GFP+ arterial area further increased by P8 (Fig. 2b). Consistent with previous reports30, a subset of Esm1-traced cells also contributed to the capillary plexus (Fig. 2b). Pik3caH1047R expression markedly reduced the GFP+ area within arteries (Fig. 2b–f and Extended Data Fig. 4b,c). Instead, most mutant GFP+ cells were retained in the capillary bed, where they expanded (Fig. 2d,f and Extended Data Fig. 4b–f) and formed multiple vascular malformations (Fig. 2b,c). Moreover, mutant, but not control, GFP+ cells were frequently detected in veins (Fig. 2b–f and Extended Data Fig. 4b,c). The few Pik3caH1047R GFP+ cells that reached arteries did not induce pathology (Fig. 2c). Consistent with lesion formation, Pik3caH1047R GFP+ cells displayed increased p-S6 levels in capillaries, but not in arteries (Fig. 2e,g and Extended Data Fig. 4g,h). By P21, Pik3caH1047R GFP+ clones persisted in capillaries and veins, although they did not further expand (Extended Data Fig. 4i–l). These data indicate that Pik3caH1047R expression impairs mobilization of arterial precursors to arteries, resulting in their retention within capillaries and the diversion of a subset towards veins, where they expand and form vascular malformations.
