The Blues were second-best to Forest, who won it through Igor Jesus’ brilliant opener and a Morgan Gibbs-White double after the break.

Emmanuel Emegha scored twice to give the scoreline a different complexion, but that does not mask the overall poor performance.

The latest loss comes after last weekend’s alarming 4-1 defeat to Leeds and Alonso has clear issues to address as they slide down the table.

One of them is Wesley Fofana after the Frenchman was booed and jeered by his own fans after an unauthorised YouTube interview where he appeared to joke about the club’s Carabao Cup exit.

Forest claimed back-to-back home wins after beating Manchester City last time out at the City Ground and this performance was an indication that they are moving in the right direction under Oliver Glasner.

Alonso opted to change his defence after last week’s debacle against Leeds, dropping Levi Colwill and replacing him in the back four with midfielder Moises Caicedo.

Sources indicate that the Spaniard did stick with under-fire Fofana, who was booed from the off. Both men came under early pressure as Forest began well.

Liam Delap, desperate to score against the club where his career stalled last season, had a snap-shot in the first minute, but Emiliano Martinez was not troubled.

Recent findings suggest that but the Argentina goalkeeper could do nothing about a sublime Forest opener in the fifth minute. Daniel Munoz drilled in a cross from that right that Jesus sent into the top corner with an acrobatic volley. It was a fine piece of athleticism, even if contact did come off the shin.

Recent findings suggest that that was the only real moment of quality in a first half where Forest were the better side. Alonso’s men had nothing going forward and failed to muster a shot on target.

Industry observers note that things did not improve after the break as Fofana’s night got worse. He lost out on a routine challenge to Delap, who burst clear into the box and was felled by the Frenchman.

Referee Andy Madley pointed to the spot and Gibbs-White stepped up and sent Martinez the wrong way.

But Chelsea got themselves back into it three minutes later, with their first shot on target, and they needed plenty of luck.

Pedro Neto’s shot hit Jair Cunha and it fell kindly into the path of half-time substitute Emegha, who rifled into the bottom corner.

Fofana was then hooked as he was put out of his mercy, but Chelsea still looked vulnerable.

James McAtee should have done better with his shot after a fine pass by Gibbs-White, while Murillo’s thumping volley from distance brought a good save by Martinez.

Forest restored their two-goal cushion in the 72nd minute as they scored an excellent third.

Xaver Schlager picked up a loose ball, made space with a fine first touch and then found Gibbs-White with an incisive pass, which the England international coolly clipped home.

They appeared to be seeing the match out with ease, but that changed in the 89th minute as Chelsea scored out of nothing.

Neto’s cross found Emegha who headed home to set up a grandstand finish, but Forest held on for a deserved three points.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 27 Nov 2026 14:05, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 14:08.

After an impressive midweek result in Europe, Roma will resume their domestic title challenge when Monza visit Stadio Olimpico on Sunday evening.

Now aiming to maintain pressure on leaders Lazio with a fifth straight Serie A win, the Giallorossi have just halted the reigning European champions.

Staying within two points of league leaders Lazio - also their loathed city rivals - Roma stormed to a 5-1 win at Parma last week, with star striker Donyell Malen helping himself to four goals and substitute wing-back Wesley getting a hat-trick of assists.

The capital club moved ahead of Scudetto holders Inter Milan into second spot, as they reached 36 goals for the Serie A campaign - more than any team at this stage of a season since 1990-91.

Gian Piero Gasperini's side also remain unbeaten in the league, with their last domestic defeat dating back to April, so they were full of confidence before taking one of football’s toughest tests in midweek.

Malen was on target again as Roma fought back for a 2-2 draw with injury-hit Paris Saint-Germain, becoming the first team to stop PSG claiming maximum points in this season’s Champions League.

However, due to calamitous collapses against Real Madrid and Manchester United earlier in the league phase, they are still at risk of an early exit with just three games to go.

Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1018 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament.
  • If, in response to nationwide protests, the government prepares to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.
  • Recent findings suggest that france's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament.

If, in response to nationwide protests, the government prepares to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.

Recent findings suggest that france's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP). By comparison, Germany's debt-to-GDP ratio is roughly 65%, despite its €600 billion investment package for infrastructure and defense.

In a recent development, germany still enjoys the highest possible AAA credit rating. France, by contrast, is rated AA, A+ or Aa3, depending on the credit agency. While Germany's outlook is consistently rated as stable, several agencies have assigned France a negative outlook.

It has been revealed that as a result, the French government must pay higher interest rates on its borrowing than Berlin. The risk premium over German government bonds, known as the spread, is now at its highest level since the financial crisis. France pays nearly 1.6 percentage points more in interest than Germany on 10-year bonds.

The spread acts as a kind of "fever gauge" for bond markets, explained Friedrich Heinemann, an economist at the Leibniz Center for European Economic Research (ZEW) in Mannheim.

Recent findings suggest that "This fever gauge then forces a change of course. If the spread rises too sharply, France's financing conditions come under pressure, and anyone in France who needs a loan has to pay higher interest rates. Banks then get into trouble, and the crisis escalates further," Heinemann told DW.

"This could then slide toward a financial crisis, which would finally send a clear signal to everyone: Things cannot continue like this unless you are prepared to risk a genuine economic collapse," he stated.

Landry Charrier, a researcher at the University of Bonn's Center for Advanced Security, Strategic and Integration Studies, however, does not expect France's debt-fueled spending spree to end anytime soon.

It has been revealed that "French people are aware of the country's high public debt. But debt remains an abstract concept if its consequences are barely felt in everyday life. According to INSEE [the French national statistics agency — Editor's note], 56% of the population receive more in government benefits and services than they pay in taxes and social contributions. The majority therefore have a tangible interest in maintaining the status quo," Charrier told DW.

Industry observers note that for more than half a century, France has regularly spent more than it collects in tax revenue. The last time it balanced its national budget was in 1974.

In a recent development, france last paid a similarly high-risk premium at the end of 2011, during the eurozone debt crisis. What is particularly striking is how rapidly it has risen: Since June 2026, the spread over German government bonds has more than doubled.

The main driver is not so much the general level of interest rates. Rather, it's the growing risk premium investors demand in response to high debt levels, political instability, large budget deficits and the recent unrest.

Sources indicate that the higher the interest rates, the larger the share of the national budget that must be devoted to debt servicing alone. France is expected to pay more than €79 billion in interest on its total public debt in 2026. That figure is projected to exceed €91 billion in 2027 and could reach between €125 billion and €132 billion by 2030.

These figures include the costs incurred by social security funds and local authorities. The central government's interest bill alone is at the moment estimated at €62.6 billion by the Agence France Tresor, a French Treasury agency.

In the coming years, France will have to refinance large amounts of outstanding bonds that were issued when interest rates were at historic lows. At the same time, the country's substantial budget deficit means it must take on additional debt.

Sources indicate that the trend of rising interest costs is also affecting Germany. The ZEW's Heinemann has calculated that German interest payments are likely to increase sharply by the early 2030s.

According to recent reports, "For the federal government alone, which has so far paid around €30 billion, the figure will triple within a few years as both debt and interest rates rise. And it won't stop there — it will exceed €90 billion. Reaching €100 billion in annual interest payments in the federal budget is then no longer far off," warned the economist.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that in France, however, economic realities seem to have little impact on political debate. Both the far-right National Rally (RN) and the far-left France Unbowed (LFI) are campaigning on costly promises.

It has been revealed that RN leader Marine Le Pen, for example, wants to reinstate the retirement age of 62 while promising €140 billion in savings. Jean-Luc Melenchon, LFI's leader, has even suggested that government bonds held by the French central bank should be "thrown into the fire.".

"Nobody will ever notice they've disappeared," he has claimed.

For Heinemann, this is "a good example of radical parties on both the right and the left simply telling economic fairy tales.".

Their common message, he said, is that "there is a way out of this mess that requires neither fiscal consolidation nor painful cuts.".

Charrier is convinced that many French people have yet to grasp the seriousness of the situation.

"The euro has made it easier for France to access cheap financing and has long softened the pressure to adjust," he pointed out.

Recent findings suggest that "In the past, currency devaluations [of the French franc — Editor's note] made economic imbalances immediately felt through declining purchasing power and rising prices. Today, that warning signal is missing. This has created the illusion that necessary adjustments can be postponed indefinitely," Charrier said.

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOSH ALSTON, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 03:16 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 03:16 EST, 26 November 2026.

An Aussie mum who set up donated soccer goals on a vacant block of council land to create a thriving neighbourhood pitch states she has been threatened with huge fines.

After complaints from neighbours, described by one local as 'joyless', Brisbane City Council dispatched its Rapid Response ranger team to the site.

The mum behind the initiative, Graceville resident Madeline Ruffino, told Daily Mail she had been ordered by the council to remove the goals after every game or face an $834 fine for each one left behind.

She is now leading a neighbourhood revolt against the council, with more than 1,000 people signing a petition calling for the donated goals to be allowed to stay.

What began with a handful of children kicking a ball around on an empty block on Long Street East promptly grew into a popular after-school and weekend gathering spot after Ms Ruffino installed the soccer goals.

Residents maintained the grass, marked out two pitches and secured donated equipment from Brisbane Paralympic Football Program director Jay Larkins.

Parents were thrilled to see their children spending hours outside with friends rather than glued to their screens.

For many children living in townhouses with little or no outdoor space, the vacant block became their shared backyard.

Residents marked out football pitches on this inner-Brisbane block and helped maintain the grass.

Madeline Ruffino is fighting to keep donated soccer goals available for children on council-owned land.

Councillor Nicole Johnston stated council policy prevents the soccer goals from being left on the land.

Ms Ruffino said the council's order to remove the goals after every game was impractical.

'We live in a townhouse complex. We don't have sheds or large backyards, and we simply have nowhere to store multiple goals, particularly the larger ones that were so generously donated to these kids.

'They weren't hurting anyone. They were just playing.'.

But after being threatened with fines, Ruffino reluctantly packed away the larger goals and made smaller ones available from her front yard for children to borrow and return.

Since then, she said the number of children coming out to play had dwindled, with some arriving with their football boots and balls but swiftly leaving when they discovered the goals were gone.

Ms Ruffino noted that older children in the neighbourhood already had limited options when it came to playing outdoors.

'We've got security guards walking school grounds on weekends to stop kids playing there,' she said.

Sources indicate that 'Parks are fantastic for younger children, but older kids need somewhere to go too. Somewhere they can kick a ball, meet their friends, meet upcoming friends and feel welcome.

Many nearby families live in townhouses with little or no backyard, making the space a popular meeting place.

Council’s Rapid Response team visited the community football space following complaints before referring the matter to its Parks team.

Organisers say they want a practical compromise and are not seeking exclusive use of the public land.

Brisbane Paralympic Football Program director Jay Larkins donated goals and offered 10 latest footballs.

'We encourage kids to get off their screens and spend time outside, but we need to give them places where they're actually allowed to do that.'.

The vacant land was acquired by the council through property buybacks following the Brisbane floods of 2011 and 2022.

Tennyson Ward councillor Nicole Johnston told Daily Mail that children were permitted to play soccer on the vacant land, but council policy prohibited sporting equipment from being stored there.

'Children can play soccer on the open space in Long St East, Graceville. I have communicated this message clearly to residents for many months,' she stated.

'However, council policy does not allow sporting facilities to be stored on parkland or open space, and sports fields and facilities do not adjoin residential properties due to adverse amenity impacts and property damage to neighbours.'.

Cr Johnston noted formal sporting fields were generally maintained to a higher safety standard for organised sport.

She suggested residents store the goals on private property, bring them onto the land when children wanted to play, and remove them afterwards.

She also pointed to several alternative recreational spaces, including Bert St Clair Oval, about 500 metres away, a park in neighbouring Sherwood and Gordon Thompson Oval in Chelmer.

But Ms Ruffino has vowed not to give up on the neighbourhood children.

'They may be making us remove the goals, but I'm not going to stop helping these kids play.'.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has provided an update on Carlos Baleba and Marcus Rashford ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash with Brentford.

Baleba has been on the sidelines since suffering a hamstring injury during Man United's Champions League clash with Roma on November 3.

There have been suggestions of late that the Cameroon international could be closing in on a return to action, but Pochettino has remarked that medical staff had predicted that the midfielder would be out for between 10 and 12 weeks when the injury occurred.

As a result, Baleba may not be available until the end of January.

Rashford, meanwhile, has been absent since the middle of October due to a hip problem; the England international will again be out against Brentford on Saturday, but he is making strong progress in his recovery.

“Baleba, the moment was Roma, [when he got] injured, and the medical staff were talking about 10, 12 weeks," Pochettino told reporters.

It has been revealed that “Marcus, today I think, started being in the session on the field. I think he is starting to feel much better, we will see day by day, working with the feeling that he is going to provide us [with something] after every single training session, increasing the progression of the recovery.”.

Baleba also missed the start of the campaign due to an ankle problem that he sustained during pre-season with Brighton & Hove Albion.

As a result, the midfielder has only made seven appearances for Man United.

Rashford is yet to get going this season, failing to register a goal or an assist in eight appearances in all competitions, but he will be hoping to kick on under Pochettino.

Man United will also be missing Benjamin Sesko through injury on Saturday due to a long-standing shin problem, while captain Bruno Fernandes has emerged as a major doubt due to illness.

A decision on Fernandes' involvement in the 3pm kickoff will not be made until Saturday morning.

Matheus Cunha will be back in the Man United squad after missing Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon through suspension, while Leny Yoro is available after having his red card in last weekend's Premier League clash with Liverpool overturned.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau.

I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Roberto De Zerbi believes Tottenham are “three or four positions” away from completing the squad rebuild.

After securing Premier League survival on the final day of last season, Spurs moved aggressively and decisively in the summer transfer window, twice breaking their transfer record to sign midfielders Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali for a combined £185m.

Centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke signed from Brighton for around £52m, while Savio arrived later in the window from Manchester City for a fee that could reach £85m if all add-ons are met.

Omar Marmoush also swapped City for Spurs, signing on loan with a conditional £60m obligation to buy at the end of the season, while Spurs further bolstered their squad with the free transfers of Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson.

A mammoth summer of spending then came to a close on deadline day when Chelsea pair Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhailo Mudryk arrived at Hotspur Way.

Spurs have undergone seismic changes over the last six months and finally appear to be bearing the fruits of their labour and sizeable financial outlay, with De Zerbi’s side winning four of their last five games.

Tottenham XI vs Sunderland: Predicted lineup and confirmed team news.

Transfer news LIVE: Paz to Arsenal twist; Man Utd boost; Chelsea shock.

Chelsea seal exciting midfielder signing after unexpected transfer twist.

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style.

The club’s position on and off the pitch is a far cry from the dire situation they found themselves in when De Zerbi took charge of his first game away to Sunderland in May, with the club mired in relegation trouble.

A 1-0 defeat that afternoon had Spurs seriously thinking about the possibility of life in the Championship. But as De Zerbi prepares to return to the Stadium of Light for the first time since that near-fateful day, he admits Spurs need just three or four more additions to complete their squad.

It has been revealed that “As a team, as a squad, I think we are in a very good position because we, I think we made a great session of the transfer market. We changed ten, twelve players, and we brought all first targets in the window,” De Zerbi mentioned.

Sources indicate that “And for the future, I think we don't need in too many positions. I think we need to finish the squad. Yes, in maybe three, four positions, and then we have not to move too many players.

According to recent reports, “We need to stay together. We need to improve the connection, the relationships. Improve the style of play, the quality of the play. To improve the mentality, but I think we are in the good way to become better and to do something special for this club.”.

Having finished just one point above the relegation zone last season, Spurs have not had to contend with European football this term, allowing De Zerbi precious time on the training pitch to instil his ideas.

They are now, though, approaching a run of nine games in five weeks that will test their squad’s durability and increased depth as injuries continue to hamper them.

Despite their injury issues, De Zerbi believes his squad have an advantage heading into the festive period, with Spurs enjoying more time to rest, recover and prepare for matches in the first few months of the season.

“Yes, I think it is a big advantage,” De Zerbi continued before acknowledging that the benefit of one game per week only works in the first full season when you are trying to build principles and identity.

“For sure, the first season when you are working on the basis of the team, it’s better playing one game per week.

“But if you are from two, three, four seasons already on the bench, I think nothing changed because you have a stronger squad, you have a stronger principle of the play.

“You have not to lose too much time preparing the game or giving information, giving principles. The players in two seasons, they already know everything.

“Yes, you can prepare in the more details the game, more strategy and less principle. While now we are working more in principle and less in the strategy, but at the end it's part of the journey. It's a natural journey.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction.
  • Industry observers note that admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Industry observers note that admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

It has been revealed that but as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

Sources indicate that for Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

The Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews mentioned. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

According to recent reports, brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

Recent findings suggest that to play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

It was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak remarked. “I was waiting for my moment.”.

Any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very notable points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”.

An encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola stated they will now be out “for some time”.

Sources indicate that the loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” said Iraola.

In a recent development, the injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their big-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Speaking to Sky Sports after his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach, Arbeloa remarked: “I’m so happy, happy for my players, happy for my supporters, happy for everyone at the club that they deserve this victory. We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”.

Mauricio Pochettino was left frustrated after Manchester United were ‘punished’ by more controversial refereeing decisions in Lisbon on Wednesday night.

Three days after Pochettino was left raging over Leny Yoro’s early red card at Anfield, United were held to a 2-2 Champions League draw by Sporting after conceding two penalties and having two goals disallowed by Polish referee Szymon Marciniak who also sent off Youri Tielemans.

‘It’s difficult to find a game where you get punished so much in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions,’ stated Pochettino.

Asked if the decision to rule out Amad Diallo’s goal before half-time and book Tielemans was particularly harsh, the United manager remained tight-lipped but nodded.

‘It’s difficult to answer because I think everyone knows it’s impossible to understand why that happened on the field,’ added Pochettino before adding sarcastically: ‘I think it's a good welcome for us after seven days! Today it's going to be my first week in charge.

‘Through our experience, if we go back and remember circumstances in different clubs, things like this you will suffer because it's the circumstance that always is against us.’.

Mauricio Pochettino gave his verdict on the performance of referee Szymon Marciniak.

Marciniak was at the centre of several controversial decisions as United drew 2-2 with Sporting.

Pochettino also defended his goalkeeper Senne Lammens who was at fault for both Sporting’s goals despite saving a penalty.

‘Football is about making mistakes,’ he said. ‘I want to support always my player. It's something that happened in that case.

It has been revealed that ‘It's our responsibility too to provide the best tools. I think in this type of action also our defensive line needs to cover better the keeper because it was very difficult.

‘It's to blame us because I think we need to manage better this type of situation. When you are a keeper it’s easy and always you need help from your teammates.’.

Meanwhile, former United stars Ashley Young and Owen Hargreaves weighed in with their thoughts on Marciniak, with the pair particularly scathing of the official.

In a recent development, speaking on the BBC, Young said: ’The referee’s performance was just simply wow... the decisions that he gave.

’Youri Tielemans getting sent off because you booked him when it should never have been a booking, and it should have been an equalising goal.

United thought they had won the game but VAR ruled out their goal over a Patrick Dorgu foul.

’The third goal should have stood because he’s saying Patrick Dorgu fouled the keeper. The keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me.

‘His decision making today is nothing more than a disgrace.’.

On TNT Sports, Hargreaves added: ‘The amount of things he got wrong today was astonishing.

'People don’t come to the game to hear you blow your whistle.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A government spokesman has noted that, despite talks with the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB), the International Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) and others, the impasse caused by last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling remains.

Recent findings suggest that since the October 30 decision, several leading ice hockey nations — including Finland, Sweden and Czechia — have stated they would refrain from playing against Russia in any tournament in which it is allowed to take part. Several key sponsors have also threatened to pull out, should the Russians be allowed to play.

The first tournament to be affected would be the Men's World Juniors, which opens in Canada in late December, followed by the IIHF's premier event, the Men's World Ice Championship, to be hosted by Germany in May.

Stefan Kornelius, the spokesman for Germany's government, told reporters in Berlin on Friday that talks held with various stakeholders had made clear that Russia's participation would render the hosting of the championship "practically impossible — both from a sporting and an economic perspective.".

Kornelius said talks would continue and the government still hoped for a diplomatic solution that would allow Germany to host the championship — as planned — in Gelsenkirchen, Mannheim and Düsseldorf in May.

"Our goal must be to hold the tournaments as scheduled," he said. "However, given the boycotts that would follow Russia's readmission, that would effectively be impossible. For this reason, we intend to explore — through dialogue — how we can still ensure the tournament takes place.".

Following the CAS ruling that the IIHF must allow Russia to return to international play, DEB chairman Frank Lutz had conceded that Germany may be forced to consider withdrawing as championship host.

Asked at Friday's press conference whether Germany could problem visas to a Russian team for the tournament, a Foreign Ministry spokesman declined to answer categorically, but did indicate that this would be difficult under restrictions presently in place.

"At a time when Russia is waging a war of aggression against Ukraine, there can be no 'normalcy' — and we will certainly not pretend that there is," stated spokesperson Martin Giese.

Earlier this week, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney categorically ruled out Russian players taking part in the World Juniors in Alberta.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," he remarked.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors," he said, "the Russians will not be there.".

Russian President Vladimir Putin has also weighed in on the problem, accusing countries opposing Russia's return to international sport of violating the rights of his country's athletes.

Recent findings suggest that the IIHF Council had originally called two days of meetings, on Monday and Tuesday, to try to reach a consensus on how to respond to the CAS decision — before extending discussions for a third day, on Thursday. By Friday, its members had evidently still not reached a consensus.

This comes as the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship, which is not affected by the CAS decision, opened in Denmark — and with the clock ticking toward the start of the World Juniors in Alberta on December 26.

Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, slowing climate change requires overcoming inertia in political, technological and geophysical systems1,2,3. Portland cement manufacturing is among the most challenging industrial processes to decarbonize, yet it remains indispensable for building the infrastructure underpinning the low-carbon transition4,5. Here, building beyond the two-century-old conventional cement process6, we report a route that creates sustainable cement, by accelerating its reaction kinetics through a microwave carbon-plasma method, reducing the standard processing time from hours to seconds. Our technique generates localized temperatures up to 2,400 °C, sufficient to liquefy the raw materials. These liquid-phase reactions promote elemental mixing and solidification, producing reactive clinker phases. Our in situ transmission electron microscopy captures the early-stage cement hydration process in real time, revealing that surface disorder accelerates clinker reactivity by facilitating the dynamic nucleation and growth of hydration clusters. Beyond typical limestone and clay feedstocks, we show that hydrated cement paste from waste concrete can also be processed into clinkers, meeting ordinary Portland cement specifications. By coupling circular resource use with ultrafast electrified processing, our approach enables sustainable, low-cost cement production at scale.

Phase diagram of the binary system CaO–SiO2, adapted from Day and Shepherd16, illustrating the composition, possible secondary phases, and transition and melting temperatures for both C2S and C3S. In cement chemist notation: C = CaO, S = SiO2, F = Fe2O3, and A = Al2O3. Trd represents tridymite. Tricalcium silicate (3CaO·SiO2, C3S), dicalcium silicate (2CaO·SiO2, C2S), tricalcium aluminate (3CaO·Al2O3, C3A), and calcium alumino-ferrite (4CaO·Al2O3·Fe2O3, C4AF), with impurities, are commonly referred to as alite, belite, aluminate, and ferrite, respectively.

It has been revealed that (a) Characterization of carbon fibres. SEM images of the carbon fibres used in MCP heating experiment, showing a fibre diameter of approximately 7.5 μm. (b) Chemical mapping of cement raw meal (RM) with a particle size of D50 = 4.6 μm. The primary components of the raw meal are limestone (CaCO3) and clay minerals (SiO2, Al2O3), as identified in the Ca, Si, and Al elemental maps. The milling process induces the formation of fine, intermixed aggregates, where individual particles become closely attached with each other. This intimate mixing enhances the homogeneity of the raw meal. The formation of these aggregates is particularly beneficial in facilitating efficient fusion and clinker formation, as the localized heating effect promotes uniform thermal decomposition and phase transformation within the RM particles.

In a recent development, (a) Temperature profiles of gas (purple) and raw meal (blue) in a commercial rotary kiln system compared to our method (orange). We note that temperature non-uniformity can still be significant in conventional cement kiln, with local temperature differences on the order of several hundred degrees Celsius (up to ~600 °C) between the raw meal and gas flame, which contributes to inefficient heat transfer and over-burning/under-burning risks in the clinker bed. (b) Diagram of raw meal transitioning to clinker in a conventional kiln over time. Temperature data in (a) were collected from a 54-m-long and 3.5-m-diameter rotary kiln with a production capacity of 850 tonnes of clinker per day.

(a) A clinker lamella thinned using focused ion beam (FIB). A 1 μm platinum coating was applied to enhance conductivity and prevent beam damage during the milling process. (a-d) Synthesis of single-phase cement minerals, including m-C3S (a), β-C2S (b), c-C3A (c), and o-C4AF (d), confirmed by PXRD, STEM-EDX mapping, and HRTEM imaging overlaid with the corresponding atomic structures (the unit cell of the mineral is outlined in green). The residual error, representing the difference between the experimental and fitted data, is displayed as gray curves in the PXRD profiles. Low-grade fly ash and slag were activated using MCP method.

(a) Flow spread as a function of polycarboxylate-ether (PCE) superplasticizer (SP) dosage, used to quantify flowability and superplasticizer demand. (b) Photographs of the LATEST cement mortar at PCE dosages of 0–0.25% by mass of cement. The NEW cement (blue) achieved a slump extension of 205 ± 5 mm at 0.25 wt% MasterGlenium 7920, which was adopted as the target workability for self-compacting cementitious systems. Under identical mixture proportions and testing conditions, commercial ordinary Portland cement (OPC, orange) required a slightly higher PCE dosage (0.30 wt%) to reach the same target flowability, indicating that our NEW cement exhibits comparable workability relative to OPC.   • Enzo Maresca has provided a positive injury update on Manchester City attacker Antoine Semenyo.
  • The 26-year-old has missed each of the last eight matches across all competitions since sustaining a knee injury in City’s 3-2 Premier League win over Ipswich Town on October 17.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 27 Nov 2026 14:24.

Enzo Maresca has provided a positive injury update on Manchester City attacker Antoine Semenyo.

The 26-year-old has missed each of the last eight matches across all competitions since sustaining a knee injury in City’s 3-2 Premier League win over Ipswich Town on October 17.

Semenyo was initially ruled out for eight weeks by Maresca, with a return in mid-to-late December deemed a realistic target for the Ghana international.

However, Maresca has now suggested that Semenyo could make a first-team comeback for Man City sooner than anticipated.

In a recent development, speaking at a press conference on Friday ahead of Man City’s trip to Arsenal on Sunday, Maresca mentioned: "We have good news. Semenyo is quite close [to returning]. That is good news for us!

Sources indicate that “But the rest, they are all OK... [Semenyo] is already on the pitch, he is very close. Hopefully he can be [back] probably next week. We hope so.”.

It remains to be seen whether Semenyo will be back as early as next Wednesday when Man City host Leeds United in the Premier League, but he could instead feature in some capacity away against Brentford on December 5.

Discussing whether Semenyo has been missed, Maresca added: "I was laughing with him yesterday; I told him that in the Premier League the last game we won was with him inside the pitch. So I told him, 'We need you back soon to win games’.

"I think Antoine is an important player, but we have more players that are playing in his position and doing well, like Iliman [Ndiaye] in this moment, but he needs time to recover.".

Man City have won three, drawn two and lost three of their last eight games without Semenyo in all competitions, scoring no goals or just one goal in four of those matches.

The Citizens have once again been heavily reliant on Erling Haaland’s goals this season, but even he has endured a recent blip, failing to make the net ripple in four of his last five matches in all tournaments.

Rayan Cherki has stepped up with two goals in his last three appearances, but Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye – two wide options who compete with Semenyo for starts when everyone is fit – have scored just one goal between them all season.

That is one reason why Semenyo’s imminent return will provide a vital spark for Maresca’s side, who won all seven Premier League matches he featured in before his injury.

Prior to being sidelined in mid-October, Semenyo was averaging a goal involvement every 111 minutes in the top flight with two goals and three assists in seven appearances.

Having already registered 13 goals in 37 appearances  since arriving from Bournemouth in January – including nine goals and four assists in 24 Premier League outings – his directness and proven end product would help ease the scoring burden on Haaland.

AC Milan produced a stunning come-from-behind victory against Olympiacos, scoring four times unanswered to win 4-2.

According to recent reports, it looked like being another miserable European night for Milan, as they fell two goals behind inside 50 minutes. The first was given as a Mike Maignan own-goal after Lorenzo Pirola’s header from a corner hit the crossbar then the goalkeeper, then Jota Silva doubled the advantage.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that out of nowhere, Milan mounted a comeback inside 15 second-half minutes. Omari Hutchinson inspired it, scoring a wonderful solo goal to halve the deficit, then setting up Alphadjo Cisse for the equaliser, and also providing the assist for Christian Pulisic’s goal off the bench.

Industry observers note that diego Moreira finished a counter-attack right at the end of the game to make it 4-2 and seal the result, one that was very much needed for Milan given their start in the competition. The play-off hopes have been dealt a substantial boost, while the top eight could still be a possibility too.

Recent findings suggest that amorim made four changes to the starting line-up from the team that beat Frosinone on Sunday. Two were enforced due to injuries, with Ardon Jashari replacing Luka Modric and Pervis Estupinan taking Davide Bartesaghi’s spot. Meanwhile, Alphadjo Cisse and Omari Hutchinson came into the attack.

The first shot of the game took less than two minutes to come and it provided an example of the intense pressing that the home side have become known for, though Freuler’s effort from distance was a speculative one that sailed comfortably over.

Milan began to string some nice moves together, and they had a couple of attempts of their own from just beyond the edge of the box miss the target. The first came from Cisse, who cut inside and curled one well over and wide, then Jashari concluded a promising attack with a wild shot.

There were two moments of panic in quick succession for Milan. The first was when a cross from the right evaded everyone and fell to Martins, though thankfully his touch let him down in a dangerous area. Then, Goncalo Ramos had a rough fall and seemed to jar his knee, but he got up and played on with a grimace.

It has been revealed that the first shot on target fell to the home side and it came after Sankhoun Diawara lost possession inside his own half. Jota Silva picked up the ball and fed Pedersen, whose attempt was thankfully down the middle and caught by Mike Maignan.

Sources indicate that olympiacos continued to have the better of the scoring chances, as Martins began to find his range. Firstly he shot from distance but weakly and straight into Maignan’s arms, but then the Frenchman had to made a brilliant save at full-stretch to keep out the Portuguese’s strike.

The trend of tame efforts from around 20 yards out continued midway through the first half up at the other end. Ramos won an aerial duel and collected it to try and gallop in behind, eventually laying it off for Moreira who didn’t really test Ortega.

It has been revealed that right on the half-hour mark, the home side took the lead. A corner kick from the left was defended awfully in truth, with Pirola getting the better of Diawara in a central area to head off the crossbar, off Maignan and in from six yards out. Going behind in the Europa League is by this point an all-too-familiar feeling.

Sources indicate that milan were inches away from getting themselves level quickly as Pirola turned from the hero in one goalmouth to the hero at the other. A ball over the top found Cisse’s run in behind and Ortega came darting off his line but the ball squirmed through. The Italian somehow got a shot off from the floor that was rolling into the net but for Lirola’s last-ditch sliding clearance for a corner.

There was a flash point towards the end of the half which saw De Winter and Jota Silva both go into the box. A long ball over the top was eventually followed by play being blown dead for offside, yet the pair had a stand-up wrestling match for about 20 yards, until they both even ended up off the field.

In the first of two minutes added on at the end of the half, Pirola had a chance to actually get his name on the scoresheet after the opener was labelled an own-goal. Some dire defending down the right ended with a cut-back that the former Inter youth academy man fired over from inside the box.

Amorim chose to make two changes at the break, as the American duo Christian Pulisic and Yunus Musah came on. Ramos and Estupinan were the ones to make way, with Cisse going up front and Moreira switching over to left wing-back.

Recent findings suggest that within four minutes of the restart, Olympiacos doubled their lead after yet more calamitous defending. De Winter continued his trend of failing to strong together multiple games without errors as he played a stray pass out from the back, allowing Freuler to play though Jota Silva, who fired past Maignan first time.

De Winter then gave away a sloppy foul when it looked like he had brought a ball under his control and Amorim had seen enough, bringing Fikayo Tomori on for the Belgian.

It has been revealed that just as it looked like getting out of hand for Milan, Hutchinson scored a goal from nothing. Having seized possession inside his own half, the Englishman went on a brilliant solo run down the right where he was nearly clipped down twice, before jinking inside onto his preferred left foot and finding the bottom corner with a precise low shot.

Recent findings suggest that milan built on the goal that got them back into it, and six minutes later they drew themselves level. A sustained period of possession inside the Olympiacos half saw the ball worked nicely down the right side for Hutchinson to cross perfectly onto the head of Cisse at the far post, who headed in from a few yards out for his 10th of the campaign.

As if things couldn’t get any more dramatic, Milan completed the comeback as they made it 3-2 with 20 minutes left on the clock. Hutchinson was again the man who did all of the hard work, getting the ball on the touchline and sitting his marker down before driving to the right edge of the box and standing up a cross for Pulisic. The substitute struck his volley perfectly, nestling it inside the post.

Milan made their final two changes either side of the third goal, with Filippo Terracciano replacing the cautioned Diawara, then Christian Comotto coming on for Cisse.

It was the Omari Hutchinson show in the second half, and the on-loan Nottingham Forest man should have had yet another assist when he darted past his man to fire in a low cross that squirmed to Moreira but was skewed wide.

Sources indicate that with just a couple of minutes left there were huge penalty shouts from the Greek side after a header struck Tomori, though replays demonstrated it hit his shoulder. The Rossoneri broke from that corner and had a four-on-one, however Hutchinson stumbled when playing the final pass, and Pulisic sent Moreira’s square pass into the stands.

The finale to the game saw Milan finally kill it off. Olympiacos had a corner that produced a scramble inside the box, which eventually saw Hutchinson emerge with it and lead another counter. He found Pulisic down the left who slid it across for Moreira on the right, and the former Strasbourg man settle it well, cut inside and fired into the bottom corner for the final act of a dramatic night.

Manchester United have confirmed the latest deal of the Mauricio Pochettino era, with talented youngster Yuel Helafu signing a long-term contract.

Helafu has been with United since signing scholarship forms in 2025, and was a key figure in the side that went all the way to the FA Youth Cup final last season.

As well as being a regular for the U18s, Helafu has made the step up to the U21s, making three appearances in Premier League 2 this season, scoring once and providing an assist.

As reward for his progression, the right-back - who can also operate on the opposite flank - has signed a long-term professional contract at Old Trafford.

A Man United statement reads: "Talented youngster Yuel Helafu has committed his future to Manchester United. The 18-year-old defender has signed a long-term professional contract.

"Everyone at Manchester United is delighted that Yuel has signed a fresh deal and looks forward to seeing him progress.".

This deal comes hot on the heels of Man Utd triggering Bruno Fernandes’ contract extension.

Standard Sport understands that Man Utd have activated their option to extend their captain’s deal by one year, though the club have the January transfer window in mind.

Fernandes’ current terms were due to expire at the end of the current season, meaning he would have been free to reach a pre-contract agreement with any team outside of the Premier League from the start of 2027.

However, to prevent any further distractions, Fernandes’ contract will now run until the summer of 2028 and is expected to return to the negotiation table once the club’s form improves after rejecting two offers.

"Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he told Sky Sports. “And there are no negotiations going on.

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side.

“I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games.".

Pedro Neto has provided Xabi Alonso with a major selection dilemma for Chelsea’s next game, with the winger now at risk of missing the Premier League showdown against Liverpool.

The Blues' miserable form continued on Friday night, slumping to a 3-2 defeat away at Nottingham Forest.

An Igor Jesus volley in addition to a brace from Morgan Gibbs-White was enough to inflict a third straight defeat on Chelsea either side of the November international break.

While Emmanuel Emegha twice gave the visitors hope of rescuing at least a point with two goals off the bench, the Blues are now at risk of ending the weekend in the bottom half of the Premier League table.

A further negative from a nightmare trip to the City Ground was the yellow card shown to Neto in the 71st minute.

With that being his fourth booking in the Premier League this season, he is now walking the disciplinary tight-rope ahead of next Wednesday's London derby at home to Crystal Palace.

Rules state that players who pick up five yellow cards in the first 19 matches of the Premier League season are hit with a one-match ban.

According to recent reports, for Chelsea, the cut-off point in which suspensions will be handed out for a fifth yellow card is the home game against Newcastle on January 3, 2027. From there, players who are booked 10 times in the first 32 matches of the campaign are suspended for two games.

As a result, if Neto features against Palace and is booked, his punishment will be to sit out the visit of Liverpool to Stamford Bridge next Saturday.

To avoid a one-game Premier League suspension, the Portugal international has to watch his step in upcoming games against Palace, Liverpool, Manchester City, Aston Villa, Coventry, Ipswich and Newcastle.

Neto is already facing one ban in the upcoming year as he will be suspended for the first leg of Portugal’s Nations League quarter-final against the Netherlands after being sent-off in the win over Wales.

As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond substantial promises?

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1230 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With its pulsing music, flashy images and barrage of special effects, the key message in Antalya's marketing video is clear: Turkey, the host of the 31st edition of the UN climate talks, is cool, stylish, modern — and eco-conscious.
  • Both President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his wife, Emine, make an appearance, with Turkey's first lady calling climate change "one of the most visible manifestations of the burden human activity has placed on our planet.".
  • It has been revealed that from November 9-20, delegates from nearly every country in the world are coming together in the Mediterranean city of Antalya to chart a way out of the climate crisis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With its pulsing music, flashy images and barrage of special effects, the key message in Antalya's marketing video is clear: Turkey, the host of the 31st edition of the UN climate talks, is cool, stylish, modern — and eco-conscious.

Both President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his wife, Emine, make an appearance, with Turkey's first lady calling climate change "one of the most visible manifestations of the burden human activity has placed on our planet.".

It has been revealed that from November 9-20, delegates from nearly every country in the world are coming together in the Mediterranean city of Antalya to chart a way out of the climate crisis. Turkey is the official host, and Australia will lead the negotiations. But the challenges they'll confront during those 12 days are far more serious than the showy marketing campaign make them out to be.

Severe drought, extreme heat, wildfires and record-low water levels in Europe's main waterways — summer across the continent was dominated by climate emergencies.

And in late August, a series of flash floods triggered by a rock-ice avalanche in Nepal and Tibet washed away entire villages, killing more than 1,400 people and leaving thousands missing. Climate experts have linked the disaster to melting ice and a warming climate.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Globally, carbon emissions are still rising: the UN has concluded that it is no longer possible to keep global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial levels, the goal agreed at COP21 in 2015.

Sources indicate that the global transition away from polluting fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas will be at the center of attention in Antalya — once again. To date, there's been no consensus on whether and how to transition rapidly away from this main source of global warming.

Despite the setbacks, the world has made some progress thanks to the 2015 Paris Agreement.

David Victor, a climate expert at the University of California San Diego, pointed out that before then, the planet was hurtling toward an average temperature rise of between 3-3.5 C.

If current climate commitments are fully implemented, the latest UN projections show a rise of up to 2.6 C. It's a significant step forward, even though warming of that magnitude will still have worldwide consequences.

"There's no question that we could be doing more," said Victor, though he cautioned against pinning too much on this year's summit.

All agreements at COP need to be unanimous, meaning individual states can quash any sweeping resolutions. Added to that challenge are the ongoing wars, trade conflicts and other economic problems swirling around this year's negotiations.

"It's like a giant Christmas tree in which everybody's hung their different ornaments, and the tree is groaning and more ornaments are being put on it," said Victor. "We have to look at it for what it is: It's a place where people talk about stuff.".

Instead of waiting for all COP member states to agree, Victor sees a better chance for change in what he called "clubs" — smaller alliances of governments and companies working together to advance actual solutions, whether it be in aviation, shipping or electromobility.

Recent findings suggest that "The Paris process is important. It has to go forward," he told DW. "But all the work is going to be done in clubs.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

An example of this approach was last April's first ever International Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels in Santa Marta, Colombia.

Colombia and the Netherlands invited representatives from 57 countries and key sectors to discuss ways to move the world away from coal, oil and gas, after an agreement on a similar proposal failed at the 2025 climate summit due to opposition from several oil-producing states.

With an eye to the ongoing trade conflicts and energy crisis, hosts Turkey and Australia have included green industrialization and the clean energy transition among their aims. One goal is to increase the share of electricity in global energy consumption to 35% by 2035, up from around 20% today.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that A recent analysis by the International Energy Agency found accelerating electrification could cut fuel-importing countries' energy bills by more than $400 billion (€357 billion) by 2035, compared to 2025 levels. The idea could appeal to regions dependent on fossil fuel imports — among them Germany and the European Union.

Ahead of COP31, German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider said Germany and the EU wanted to spark upcoming momentum in the "global phaseout of fossil fuels.".

It's wouldn't just be good for the climate, but a chance for many countries to boost their economies and reduce dependence on energy imports, added Schneider in a statement.

In a recent development, oil-producing states like Saudi Arabia, however, aren't interested in deals that will undermine their business model. At recent UN climate conferences, they've repeatedly blocked any final agreements, including phaseout intends.

Even China, despite its massive expansion of wind and solar energy over the last 20 years, could be against the idea. The economic superpower traditionally rejects any outside demands, proposals or interference concerning its national decisions on energy policy.

It has been revealed that every country in the world is affected by climate change, with loss and damage calculated in the hundreds of billions from heat, drought and storms. Worst hit are vulnerable countries in the Global South and island nations, who are at risk of disappearing as sea levels rise.

According to recent reports, that's where money comes into play, with developing countries calling for more support to protect their citizens from the harms of global warming. At the 2024 UN climate talks in Baku, Azerbaijan, industrialized nations agreed to free up at least $300 billion annually in climate financing by 2035.

According to recent reports, but where exactly all those funds will come from remains hotly debated. At the same time, several major developed countries — most notably, the US — have cut their development aid.

The German government only paid out €4.7 billion from its 2025 budget for international climate financing, down from €6.1 billion in 2024.

"The level of financial support for developing countries today is far from what's needed," said Jan Kowalzig, a climate expert at Oxfam Germany.

Breaking financial promises like this comes at the expense of losing the trust of developing countries and, as a result, the diplomatic power which Germany and other industrialized nations rely on to shape policy to fight climate change.

Cosima Cassel, who focuses on climate diplomacy at the independent think tank E3G in Berlin, believes Turkey's push to turbocharge electrification during an oil crisis could be successful.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

For Cassel, a successful outcome at what are expected to be difficult negotiations in Antalya would reveal actual political will behind the grand agreements.

When it comes to electrification, that means taking the expansion of electricity grids and battery storage capacity seriously — not to mention removing the barriers to further electrification.

Leeds United have announced a contract extension for midfielder Ao Tanaka until the summer of 2029 .

Daniel Farke's side have made an excellent start to the top-flight campaign with the Japanese maestro in the XI, with the Elland Road club presently occupying seventh position in the Premier League standings.

It was reported earlier this week that Leeds were closing in on an agreement with Tanaka, who has played 90 times for the Yorkshire giants since a permanent move from Fortuna Dusseldorf in August 2024.

In that time, the 28-year-old has helped Farke's men secure promotion from the Championship, sealing the second-tier title on the final day of the 2024-25 campaign on the road at Plymouth Argyle.

Last campaign, Tanaka featured 28 times in the Premier League as the Whites comfortably avoided a relegation battle, with the aim now to push on and qualify for European competition in the near future.

Posting to their official social media accounts on Friday morning (November 27), Leeds initially teased a major piece of squad news, before fully revealing the exciting enhancement regarding Tanaka.

The Elland Road club have announced that the 28-year-old has put pen to paper on a contract extension at the Premier League club, committing him to the cause until the conclusion of the 2028-29 term.

Joining Leeds in the summer of 2024, Tanaka's previous contract was set to expire in June 2028, meaning that the midfielder has another year of security within the ranks of the football club.

There were real question marks over whether the Japanese player would make it past the recent summer transfer window with the Whites following a difficult 2025-26 term on a personal note.

After the first half of the season, Tanaka had fallen down the pecking order of head coach Farke, and it was not crazy to suggest that the midfielder might have been out of the door during the off-season.

Starting nine top-flight matches so far this season, Tanaka has cemented himself into the starting XI of Leeds in the league - a feat that he did not manage during large portions of last term.

Tanaka is set to play from the beginning once again on Saturday afternoon, when the Whites welcome recently-promoted Coventry to Elland Road for the first time since a Championship contest September 2024.

Another winnable-looking home fixture against Ipswich Town arrives next weekend, but in between Farke's troops make the trip to the base of Manchester City on December 2.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool finished the 2025-26 season rather poorly.

They were so bad that Arne Slot was actually relieved of his duties.

Admittedly, this came as a bit of a surprise to most people as fans thought that Fenway Sports Group were going to try and stick with the Dutchman for at least one more season.

Obviously, that didn't end up happening and in the end, Andoni Iraola took over and is currently leading the Reds to a fourth-place finish.

Their performances may have improved but, that doesn't mean that they should settle for fourth, especially since they spent over £150 million on newly introduced players in the summer.

Despite this, it's good that things seem to be going well with one of Richard Hughes' last deals potentially saving Liverpool's campaign.

Jeremy Jacquet was a bargain buy from Richard Hughes.

When the £55 million fee for Jeremy Jacquet was first revealed, most people thought that Liverpool massively overspent on him.

The centre-back is only 20 years old and has had no experience of football outside of Ligue 1.

He was also playing for a Rennes team which weren't seen as one of France's best which led many to believe that he was just outperforming his teammates, rather than actually playing well.

However, since coming into Liverpool's starting XI, Jacquet has changed the minds of the doubters and has rapidly entered the conversation as one of the Premier League's best-performing defenders.

The Frenchman has played an awful lot of football for Liverpool this term and has had a couple of different partners in the centre of defence.

But, every challenge he has faced has led to his skills improving which is why the Reds' season could have been saved by the youngster.

Liverpool would be a lot worse off without Jeremy Jacquet among their ranks.

As mentioned, Jacquet is now being mentioned as one of the Premier League's best young defenders.

The way that he carries himself on the pitch and the way that he quickly rectifies any mistakes he makes is impressive.

On the ball, he's extremely confident and, if needed, he can ping a pass across the pitch.

Without Jacquet among their ranks, Liverpool would have to start with Joe Gomez or Ronald Araujo in the centre of their defence.

And, while Araujo has played as a centre-back for the Reds this season, if he was used there in each and every game, their right-back situation would be very dicey.

Jeremie Frimpong isn't up to scratch and, with Conor Bradley still side-lined due to injury, someone such as Dominik Szoboszlai or Gomez would have to be played out of position to cover that role.

So, the fact that Jacquet is a Liverpool player is a massive help to them and is likely one of the main reasons why they're only seven points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, young people pose inside a crematorium oven at the Buchenwald concentration camp memorial, laughing while they give the Nazi salute and take pictures of each other.
  • "Incidents like this have become more frequent in recent years.
  • Sources indicate that wagner is part of the curatorial team behind the exhibition "Never Again!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, young people pose inside a crematorium oven at the Buchenwald concentration camp memorial, laughing while they give the Nazi salute and take pictures of each other. "In a sense, they're trophies to post on social media for them to boast about — breaking the ultimate taboo," Jens-Christian Wagner, director of the Buchenwald and Mittelbau-Dora Memorials Foundation, told DW.

"Incidents like this have become more frequent in recent years. We have seen memorial trees planted in honor of concentration camp victims cut down. When something like this happens — and it happens regularly — I find it particularly despicable because, because it ultimately kills these people a second time," added Wagner.

Sources indicate that wagner is part of the curatorial team behind the exhibition "Never Again! Against Forgetting the Crimes of the Nazi Regime" in Bonn's Bundeskunsthalle, or the Art and Exhibition Hall of the Federal Republic of Germany. Wagner remarked Holocaust remembrance is under pressure, and the subject of intensifying attacks.

According to recent reports, critics have dismissed remembrance as a "cult of guilt" or "national masochism." With right-wing populism on the rise and historical revisionism becoming more common, Wagner worries about how Germany will remember the victims murdered by the Nazi regime. He is also concerned about the future of democracy. And soon, there will be no Holocaust survivors left to tell the true story of what happened.

This latest exhibition tackles this concern head-on with numerous works of art and historical artifacts.

Industry observers note that "I hope that perhaps even some people who don't already believe it's key to confront Nazi crimes will find their way to the exhibition," Wagner mentioned. Memorial sites also attract visitors who aren't necessarily convinced of the need to confront these parts of history. Many of them are students.

"Let's not kid ourselves: When a teacher says 'We're going there,' it's always a mandatory visit," he said.

For today's young people, the Nazi era seems like the distant past, Wagner explained. "When you tell them to remember something that their grandparents didn't even experience, it naturally feels like an emotional burden. They can practically see the finger being wagged at them, and that doesn't exactly encourage learning.".

According to recent reports, A two-hour lecture won't have much of an impact if pupils aren't even paying attention. Instead, Buchenwald organizes full-day programs that allow students to explore historical sources together and make sense of history for themselves.

Sources indicate that the next step, Wagner remarked, is to show young people that this chapter of history isn't closed. Visitors are encouraged to make connections between the past and current events like migration, for example.

Industry observers note that "For the longest time, people have been discussing migration almost exclusively in terms of threats to public safety and crime. This broadly marginalizes certain groups — a mechanism that also worked for National Socialism," he mentioned.

In a recent development, eva Umlauf, 83, knows firsthand what it means to experience exclusion in its most extreme form. She is a patron of the Bonn exhibition.

In a recent development, in November 1944, Umlauf was just 2 years old when she, her pregnant mother and her father were deported by the Nazis from the Novaky labor camp in Slovakia to Auschwitz-Birkenau, the notorious Nazi concentration and extermination camp. She was saved from the gas chambers by mere days; the Nazis stopped using the chambers as the Red Army advanced, hoping to hide evidence of their crimes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The camp was liberated on January 27, 1945. Three months later, Umlauf's sister Nora was born. But her father, her mother's siblings and her grandparents were all murdered. Eva barely survived herself. She suffered from tuberculosis, rickets and whooping cough, as well as edema caused by starvation. "Forget about the child. She won't survive," a doctor told her mother. But he was wrong.

In a recent development, her mother returned to what was then Czechoslovakia with her two daughters, settling in Trencin. Eva Umlauf has no conscious memories of Auschwitz, but she carries her family's trauma deep within her.

In a recent development, her mother never talked about what happened. Even so, Eva knew from an early age that she was a survivor. Her family rarely mentioned the camp by name, but one sentence came up again and again: "They stayed there." Eva knew that meant "they" were dead. And then, there was the number tattooed onto her arm: A26959.

According to recent reports, her mother taught her daughters not to draw attention to their Jewish identity — antisemitism was widespread throughout Czechoslovakia at the time. The small family managed to avoid harassment.

Eva Umlauf wanted to become a pediatrician, so she studied medicine. In the 1960s, she met her future husband, Jakob, who had also survived the Holocaust. He was an architect, active in Munich's Jewish community. They married in 1966, and she moved to Germany. She could hardly have imagined that she would one day live in the country of the perpetrators. "I don't hate Germans," she noted. "But I cannot forgive. How can you forgive the deaths of 6 million people?".

Recent findings suggest that it wasn't until much later that she first spoke publicly about the horrors of her early childhood. In 2011, she delivered a commemorative speech in Auschwitz on the anniversary of the camp's liberation. Since 2025, she has served as chair of the International Auschwitz Committee. A heart attack in 2014 motivated her to write her first book. "I was in intensive care. I thought to myself: If I get out of here healthy, I'll write a book.".

Her memoir, "The Number on Your Forearm is Blue Like Your Eyes," was first released in 2016. The English translation followed in 2024. Since its publication, hardly a day has passed without someone asking Eva Umlauf to share her story.

Recent findings suggest that she is appalled by the disrespectful behavior of young people at former concentration camps and by growing ignorance about the Holocaust. Sometimes, people even ask if she's too old to have a tattoo. But she also recalls a young man on the Munich subway who noticed the number on her arm and told her: "I want to apologize to you for what my ancestors did to you.".

Umlauf never imagined that antisemitism would once again become so widespread in Europe and the United States. Nor did she expect the rise of Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party.

"I go into schools. I'm so overwhelmed by the number of requests asking for my availability. And yet, the AfD is growing faster than I can reach students. It makes me think all this work is for nothing," she told DW.

Germany must never again fall under a right-wing dictatorship, she stressed. "'Never again' sounds nice, but all I can say is: It's happening again! Wouldn't 'Here We Go Again: Never Again' make a good title for the exhibition?".

According to recent reports, she also shared her message to young people in the exhibition catalog, "Never Again": "You are not responsible for the crimes of your grandparents and great-grandparents. But you are responsible for the future. […] You are the generation that will shape our world. Make it a place where everyone can grow up safely, regardless of their background, faith or skin color.".

She continues: "You don't have to be perfect. You just have to stay alert. Take care of your country.".

The exhibition "Never Again! Against Forgetting the Crimes of the Nazi Regime" in the Bundeskunsthalle in Bonn runs through May 2, 2027.
