37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1368 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that when the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, ending East Germany's isolation from the West, the event was celebrated on both sides of the border.
  • Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.
  • To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that when the Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, ending East Germany's isolation from the West, the event was celebrated on both sides of the border. Yet, 37 years later, many people on both sides remain deeply skeptical of each other.

Surveys show that only a minority of respondents report feeling a strong sense of community between those from former East and West Germany, and many continue to perceive significant differences.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

We asked three artists from Germany with different perspectives on the history of the country's division to share their views.

Author Lea Streisand was born in 1979 and experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall firsthand while growing up in East Berlin.

In her books and essays, she has returned to her East German upbringing many times, using literature to process it.

The novel "Hufeland, at the corner of Bötzow" (2019, Ullstein), for example, recounts the period of reunification from a child's perspective.

Industry observers note that "November 9, 1989, was simply incredible," she told DW. She was 10 years old at the time. When her mother bought her winter boots with the 100 Deutsche Marks she received from the West German state — a welcome gift given to all East German citizens — she was so disappointed that she felt like crying. But later, a friend of her parents' let her buy so many sweets at the supermarket that they lasted until Christmas.

Recent findings suggest that "The disappointment really set in afterwards, with what happened over the course of the following year. It was unbelievable how swiftly an entire system was suddenly swept away and a latest one built up, as if to say, 'There you go. You're welcome'," Streisand recalled. "I think it was just too fast for people.".

Industry observers note that the people of East Germany, or the GDR, had brought about the fall of the Berlin Wall themselves through a civil rights movement and numerous demonstrations. For many, however, the goal was not to dissolve the state immediately but to reform it.

According to recent reports, among them was Anke Feuchtenberger, born in 1963 in East Berlin. Her childhood was spent in East Berlin and in the East German region of Western Pomerania, where she now lives again and feels "very much at home.".

In a recent development, today, she teaches at the University of Applied Sciences in Hamburg, meaning she spends time on both sides of the former divide. Feuchtenberger is often described as Germany's most influential comic artist. Her work has also garnered international acclaim.

"Back then, as artists, we tried to bring about a change through posters and flyers — to gain more freedom without immediately abolishing socialism," she explained.

At the time, the fall of the Berlin Wall stirred up mixed feelings in Feuchtenberger: "I soon realized that the creative and revolutionary aspects of our movement were very promptly being smothered by consumerism, and that nationalist tendencies — which had already been noticeable before — were coming to the fore," Feuchtenberger recalled. "That made me afraid.".

Sources indicate that meanwhile, for photographic artist Simon Menner, born in 1978 in Emmendingen, in the West German state of Baden-Württemberg, Berlin was very far away. As Menner put it, he experienced the fall of the Berlin Wall as a child in a "rather abstract" way. Today, Berlin is his home.

It has been revealed that in his experience, the way films and documentaries portrayed East Germany around the time of reunification was very bleak. "But West Germany in the '80s," he remarked, "was also bleak and very staid.".

This uneven portrayal of the two parts of Germany is an matter that deeply concerns Menner — partly because he unwittingly contributed to it in a small way. Among other things, Menner's work explores the topic of surveillance and how it works.

In the archives of East Germany's Ministry for State Security, or Stasi — which are freely accessible today as part of the National Archives — he discovered a massive collection of photographs that both fascinated and horrified him and which he wanted to bring to the attention of a wider public.

Sources indicate that his photo book "Top Secret" (2012, from publisher Hatje Cantz) features a selection of photos that offer a unique insight into the work of the Stasi. Some are eerie, while others are curious or even absurd.

In a recent development, menner also tried to look into the photo archive of West Germany's Federal Intelligence Service. "I spent a year trying to gain access — without success," he mentioned.

In hindsight, he now finds his artistic project problematic because he believes it is too one-sided, focusing exclusively on East Germany's past.

According to recent reports, according to Menner, West Germany's intelligence services in the 1960s were not exactly models of virtue either, and he believes it is "actually high time" to critically examine this part of history as well. In his view, an honest examination of Germany's past as a whole is a prerequisite for genuine reconciliation.

Streisand believes literature can help foster mutual understanding. "Literature opens a window into experiences we haven't had ourselves," she said. "You can immerse yourself in the mind of someone who has had a different life than you have and understand what happened.".

Recent findings suggest that interest in these stories remains strong. In 2023, Feuchtenberger published the nearly 500-page graphic novel "Comrade Cuckoo" (published by Reprodukt), which was the first graphic novel to be nominated for the Leipzig Book Fair Prize in the fiction category.

The story spans a childhood in the fictional East German village of Pritschitanow in the 1960s in the GDR to the post-Reunification era. In it, Feuchtenberger weaves autobiographical memories of her upbringing with fantastical and fictional elements.

The artist said she was surprised "that, so long after the fall of the wall, my stories have sparked such great interest in the West.".

Recent findings suggest that in particular, the fact that the main character, Kerstin, rarely sees her parents because they both work full-time is a topic that often comes up at readings. In the GDR, everyone had the right to work, she mentioned. At the same time, it was a civic duty.

According to recent reports, could the West German interest in this stem from the fact that full-time employment for both parents has long been less common in the West? It's possible, remarked Feuchtenberger.

When looking toward their shared future, the two East German women are more optimistic than Menner, from West Germany.

"In Berlin, I often don't even notice anymore whether I'm in the West or the East," mentioned Menner. "But when it comes to sociopolitical issues, politicians should listen to older and younger people more closely," he added, referring to the recent election successes of far-right Alternative for Germany, or AfD . "Otherwise, things are going to get difficult in the near future.".

"It's very crucial to step outside our own bubble because people all over the world are facing problems. Constantly focusing on this German-German divide that has emerged between the groups doesn't help," noted Feuchtenberger.

Industry observers note that "For me personally, the whole issue of borders has somehow dissolved," she explained. This is due in no small part to the many trips abroad that have taken her to various places around the world.

Moreover, in her hometown near the Polish border, she observes how animals couldn't care less about the border. "They come from the east and the west and do whatever they want," she stated. That's why she also gave "Comrade Cuckoo" the working title "A German Animal in a German Forest," "because I found the absurdity of an animal having a nationality so funny.".

"This East-West thing — our children won't have any interest in it at all," stated Streisand. "Young people don't care where their parents come from. Can I get a job that will support a family? Do I have to go to war? Right now, completely different things are relevant.".

Aston Villa team news: Mixed Alejandro Garnacho update provided by Unai Emery amid squad omissions

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Aston Villa manager Unai Emery has insisted that Chelsea loanee Alejandro Garnacho 'has his respect', despite his recent omissions from the first-team squad.
  • Earlier this week, the winger was excluded from Villa's squad for the Champions League fixture at Galatasaray, despite Emery naming two goalkeepers and not using his permitted amount of players on the substitutes' bench.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 27 Nov 2026 15:14, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 15:24.

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery has insisted that Chelsea loanee Alejandro Garnacho 'has his respect', despite his recent omissions from the first-team squad.

Earlier this week, the winger was excluded from Villa's squad for the Champions League fixture at Galatasaray, despite Emery naming two goalkeepers and not using his permitted amount of players on the substitutes' bench.

That led to Emery seemingly indicating that the 22-year-old is currently out of his aims.

With Garnacho believed to be close to activating an appearance clause that would secure a permanent £43m transfer to Villa Park, his absence is naturally coming under scrutiny.

Liverpool's Harvey Elliott found himself in a similar situation in 2025-26, and Emery is justifiably facing questions over whether history is repeating itself with Garnacho.

Speaking at a press conference ahead of Saturday's Premier League fixture at Ipswich Town, Emery claimed that Garnacho had been "training very well" but was behind players deemed to be playing at a higher standard.

Recent findings suggest that the Spaniard told reporters: "Alejandro Garnacho is training very well. His attitude is fantastic. He was struggling at the beginning of the season because he was not fit. Now he is fit.

"He's training good but as well the team was progressing, now is progressing, and when he is not involved in the squad it is because I have to choose with other players as well.

"He has my respect first as a person and second as a player but he is not involved for this reason. But football can change. It is November, of course there is a transfer window in January, but we are not thinking about the transfer window in January. Me especially.

"We are playing matches so I will need players. Now he's not but he is working well. He is at the level that at the beginning we were expecting. But of course other players as well are working and performing well. The structure we are building was also two months ago when he was not fit enough to be playing with the consistency we need.

"So, keep going, keep moving forward, as a team, himself as a player, and we will see.".

Emery was also asked whether Garnacho could leave Villa at the start of 2027, despite Chelsea not possessing a recall clause, nor Villa having a loan break clause.

He mentioned: "He is part of the squad we have and we have as well a lot of players who are playing well now.

"Also to get the balance in the squad. A lot of decisions we decided at the end of transfer window - we have some players not fit, injured, doubts over when they are coming back.

In a recent development, "In September we were struggling but for now we are 24 players in the squad. In last years I had less players but now we are training 22, 23 players and we have to take out each match, especially for the Premier League.

"I can't speak about how it will be in the next transfer window. The club is running it. I am only focused on each match. But, again, he is much, much better, practicing every day with a very good attitude so for me that is very key, firstly for him, and for us.".

If fit, Garnacho will be available for as many as seven more matches before the winter transfer window.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim believes that the comeback win over Olympiacos is something that could ‘change the future’.

After 50 minutes of the game on the outskirts of Athens, it looked like Milan were heading for a fourth defeat in five Europa League games. Lorenzo Pirola crashed a header in off the bar via Mike Maignan, then Jota Silva scored a second early in the second half.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then, out of almost nowhere, Omari Hutchinson inspired a run of three goals in 15 minutes. Firstly he scored a goal of his own with a brilliant solo run, then he set up Alphadjo Cisse for his 10th goal of the season, then he crossed for a Christian Pulisic volley to make it 3-2.

In a recent development, diego Moreira added a fourth late on to make sure of the points. Amorim spoke to Sky after the final whistle to give his thoughts on what was a rollercoaster night, but one that thankfully ended well. His words are via MilanNews.

Will this second half change the Europa League season?

It has been revealed that “It definitely changes our future. We played well in the second half, but we made a lot of mistakes again and we need to improve. But we got a lot of players back, it was a positive night.”.

It has been revealed that “It’s better to finish games like this, winning obviously. We have a lot of work to do to be a very strong team, but the spirit is there. It’s the start of something.”.

Sources indicate that “I think this is the biggest problem: focusing on the small details like set pieces, goalkeeping, and the plays we need to make. It comes with time and experience.

“The technical aspect is fine, but concentration is the most important thing. It’s tough to play physically every three days, but it’s even tougher to constantly have this pressure of having to win.”.

In a recent development, “I always expect this. He has the potential to do much more. He’s talented, like other players on the team. It’s no surprise, he’s very talented. It’s the mentality that counts.”.

How do you explain the build-up errors?

According to recent reports, “We lost the ball without being pressured, trying to play the ball. We left Jashari alone to set up a team with four of our players behind their midfielders. When we had the ball, we gave it away without pressure.

“Koni sometimes put the ball in areas where there was pressure, but instead he was supposed to carry the ball. He’s responsible for pushing the team forward and guiding us forward. We went to get into their pressing zones.”.

It’s your first comeback win of the season….

“I think it’s a great feeling. If you look at the Benfica match, we had several opportunities. We created more than today. You have to see it to believe it, and today we saw that we came from two goals behind and won 4-2. Our confidence will grow.”.

  • In a recent development, sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

In a recent development, sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage said when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”.

The Frenchman remarked that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

It has been revealed that “I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he said. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

Industry observers note that “Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”.

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

Industry observers note that “The first work to do is on me,” he remarked. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

“It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”.

For all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

“The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage noted. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”.

In a recent development, sage joined Palace after a fine campaign with Lens. He led the club to second place in Ligue 1, just six points off Paris St-Germain, and victory in the Coupe de France. Yet, despite Sage’s reputation when he moved to Selhurst Park, his suitability for the Palace job is increasingly being questioned.

Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Sage could suffer the same fate, with doubts growing that he will still be in charge for Thursday’s trip to Besiktas.

Sources indicate that “It’s not my decision,” Sage said. “I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we are able to do better. And today the work is really vital to do, and I will do it. It’s my job, and I’d like to change this.”.

With only Manchester City and Arsenal above them, Brighton and Hove Albion are entitled to dream of making history. Yet, whatever happens between now and May, one accolade is already surely their own: the goal of the season award.

Sources indicate that diego Gómez’s 56-yard strike will instantly become the stuff of Brighton lore. The Paraguayan’s audacity will be even more cherished for coming against Crystal Palace, who were pummelled 5-0 in the M23 derby.

All Premier League defeats are equal but some are more equal than others. Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Pierre Sage is at grave risk of suffering the same fate. Naturally, Brighton fans revelled in reminding him of this threat as the final whistle approached.Palace were so ragged that their performance felt like a defeat that marks the end of a managerial reign. Even stand-in captain Adam Wharton was guilty of dawdling and losing the ball in possession. Hundreds of away supporters left well before the full-time whistle and those who remained booed all players bar Jefferson Lerma.

According to recent reports, with less venom in attack, especially with Ismaïla Sarr being an unused substitute, Palace’s sole chance lay in counter-attacking. This strategy disintegrated in the fourth minute, when Jaydee Canvot headed Pascal Gross’s free-kick into his own net.

But the hint of self-immolation in Palace’s display should not obscure the swagger of Brighton’s performance. Despite losing Danny Welbeck, last year’s top scorer, Brighton have scored 23 goals already this Premier League campaign, the most in the league. This tally includes one of the most extraordinary goals in Premier League history.

In a recent development, most simply, Gómez’s goal, which put Brighton 2-0 up in the seventh minute, was a triumph of the imagination. Receiving a short pass from Olivier Boscagli just inside his own half, Gómez could have sought to pick out a team-mate. Instead, his scanning of the pitch before receiving the ball had revealed that goalkeeper Walter Benítez was off his line and Brighton’s attacking players were being tightly guarded by defenders. And so, just as he entered the centre circle in the opposition half, Gómez attempted the absurd.

“I’m not training with Diego Gómez shooting from 50 metres in training,” head coach Fabian Hürzeler noted while breaking into a smile. “It’s just about making the players quick in their minds.

It has been revealed that “In these moments it’s about being very precise with his long kick. The perception to recognise the keeper and being quick to go to the action was impressive.”.

The presence of mind to attempt something outlandish was one thing; the execution was quite another. With Benítez vulnerable, Gómez took just one touch with his right foot before taking his shot, not giving the keeper enough time to scramble back to cover his line. As he looked up to confirm the opportunity, the 23-year-old struck the ball over Benítez with such venom that it did not even bounce until it reached the goal.

All that remained was for the Paraguayan international to hurtle towards the corner flag, engulfed by his ecstatic team-mates. For the Brighton fans, soaked by showers at the Amex, rain can never have felt so sweet.

Industry observers note that gómez’s goal will earn comparisons with David Beckham’s lob from the halfway line at Wimbledon. The advancements in pressing and conditioning in the 30 years since, with space ever more congested, makes such a strike even harder today. Not since Wayne Rooney in 2017 has a player scored a Premier League goal from further out than Gómez’s 56 yards.

In a recent development, gómez may well attempt an encore. He shot from even further out at the Stadium of Light a week ago. When October ends, three of the last four Premier League goal-of-the-month winners will be Brighton players. Alongside his meticulous emphasis on set-pieces, Hürzeler empowers flair in open play.

Industry observers note that good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

Brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Manchester United were reportedly snubbed by Leeds United striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin before he signed a contract extension at Elland Road.

Mauricio Pochettino's men are heading towards a full-blown relegation battle in the top flight this season, with the Red Devils sitting 19th in the Premier League table after winning one of their first 11 matches.

At the other end of the standings, Daniel Farke's Leeds are in seventh position and recently declared a contract extension for talisman Calvert-Lewin, who is now committed to the club until the summer of 2029.

Following his 2025 arrival on a free transfer from Everton, the 29-year-old has established himself as one of the best strikers in the Premier League, as well as earning call-ups to England squads under Thomas Tuchel.

Leeds are supposedly in the market for new attacking options during the winter trading point, however, there is no doubting that Calvert-Lewin will remain a first-choice option in the ranks of the Whites.

According to transfer expert Fabrizio Romano via TEAMtalk, Manchester United were keen on bringing Leeds and England star Calvert-Lewin to the Theatre of Dreams during the January transfer window.

However, with the 29-year-old since signing club-record terms at Elland Road, the report claims that the former Everton attacker snubbed the advances of the 20-time English champions.

As well as the out-of-form Red Devils, it is understood that two clubs from Italy were extremely interested in securing the services of Calvert-Lewin during the most recent summer transfer window.

Ultimately, Leeds decided to keep hold of their talent and the player opted to stay put at Elland Road, where Farke's side are looking to push on and secure European qualification this season.

It is believed that Calvert-Lewin has become the highest-paid player in Leeds history by agreeing his upcoming terms, with the Englishman expected to be earning upwards of £110,000 per week.

In the days of Sir Alex Ferguson, plucking one of the Premier League's best strikers from a rival would be relatively simple for Manchester United - see Robin van Persie's 2012 switch from Arsenal as an example.

However, those glory days are long behind the fallen English giants, who are hurtling towards a bottom-three scrap if their form does not seriously improve under upcoming head coach Pochettino.

All things considered, it makes complete sense that Calvert-Lewin snubbed an approach from Man Utd in order to continue building a legacy for Leeds at Elland Road.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ronald Araujo's Liverpool future is still up in the air.

The defender has been top class for the Reds since he joined them in the summer and, although it took him a couple of games to get into Iraola's aims, he's now earned himself a guaranteed place in his starting XI.

Indeed, he is being used as a right-back which isn't his natural position but, he's that good in both positions that it doesn't really matter where he's played.

He helps bring an extra layer of defensive stability to Anfield and he's also helped shore up their back line massively.

This has allowed Jeremy Jacquet the time to adjust to Premier League life and has ensured that he was one of the best defensive transfers made in the summer.

But, since Liverpool's option to buy the midfielder is rather high at €55 million, alternative options are now making their way onto the Reds' shortlist.

Liverpool can sign Mohamed Simakan for €35 million.

Right-back has been a problem area for Liverpool ever since they got rid of Trent Alexander-Arnold last summer.

Jeremie Frimpong was brought in to try and help plug the gap while Conor Bradley was expected to take over as Liverpool's first choice right-back.

But, thanks to the injuries that both players suffered, the Reds' prepares didn't work out exactly as they wanted them to which resulted in Araujo being signed this summer.

As mentioned, the Uruguayan has been in fine form this term but, since he's not an actual Liverpool player, a decision needs to be made on his future.

But, with the way that things seem to be going, Araujo looks likely to return to Barcelona.

This has led to fans asking many questions about who their starting right-back is going to be with Caught Offside now throwing a new defender into the mix.

"Liverpool, Manchester United, Arsenal, Tottenham and Newcastle have all continued scouting Simakan, although no formal offers or advanced negotiations have taken place," they wrote.

"For Liverpool, Simakan’s versatility is particularly attractive.

"With long-term succession planning required in central defence, signing a player capable of operating centrally while also covering right-back would give the squad valuable flexibility.

According to recent reports, "The asking price will be crucial. At €35m-€40m, Simakan would represent a relatively manageable investment compared with some of the €70m-plus defenders right now being linked with both clubs.

"There are still questions about adapting back to European football after his spell in Saudi Arabia, but at 26 he should be entering his peak years.".

Mohamed Simakan can cover all the positions Ronald Araujo does for Liverpool.

Not only is Mohamed Simakan younger than Araujo but, he's also worth a lot less.

€35 million for a 26-year-old in this market is unheard of, especially for a versatile defender such as the Frenchman.

As Caught Offside mention, his last couple of years being spent in Saudi Arabia do pose a bit of a worry but, within a few months of making a return to European football, he should be able to get back to his best.

The main stumbling block between Liverpool and Barcelona for an Araujo deal is the fee that the La Liga outfit want.

So, the fact that Simakan is younger, can play in all the positions that Araujo covers for Liverpool and the fact that he'd be cheaper for them to buy, makes a deal for the Frenchman a no-brainer.

Breaking: Norway's ice hockey team notes Russia replacing it at World Juniors

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (867 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that with just weeks to go until the start of the 2027 World Junior Championship, it remains unclear who will be the 10th, and final, participant.
  • Sources indicate that the move, which has yet to be publicly announced by the IIHF, comes in apparent response to the Court of Arbitration (CAS) ruling in late October, which ordered it to allow Russia to return to international play.
  • The IIHF barred Russia and Belarus from international play shortly after Moscow released its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that with just weeks to go until the start of the 2027 World Junior Championship, it remains unclear who will be the 10th, and final, participant. This comes after the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) had said it had been removed from the tournament so that Russia could take part.

Sources indicate that the move, which has yet to be publicly announced by the IIHF, comes in apparent response to the Court of Arbitration (CAS) ruling in late October, which ordered it to allow Russia to return to international play. The World Juniors is the first tournament affected by the CAS decision.

The IIHF barred Russia and Belarus from international play shortly after Moscow released its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

In a statement issued Saturday, the IIHF said it was "taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships, protect the organization's financial stability and secure the long-term future of international ice hockey.".

According to recent reports, as of Monday, the IIHF website still listed Norway as one of the participants in the World Juniors, which is to be hosted by Edmonton and Red Deer, Alberta, beginning on December 26. But Swiss Ice Hockey has responded to Norway's statement, saying its team would not face Russia at the World Juniors — as would be the case if it replaces Norway in the schedule.

However, it's far from certain that Russia will actually be able to ice a team in the tournament, as just last week, the Canadian prime minister ruled out the possibility.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," said Mark Carney.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there.".

Recent findings suggest that how this circle could be squared is unclear. Carney's pledge, coupled with the stated refusal by Finland, Sweden, Switzerland and others to face Russia in an international tournament, appears to have given the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association (NIHF) hope that its team could still play in the upcoming tournament. Several long-time corporate sponsors have also threatened to pull out if Russia is allowed to compete.

"This makes us hope that the last word has not been noted about our participation in Canada in December," said NIHF General Secretary Petter Salsten.

"The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association is awaiting further information from the IIHF in the coming days.".

Meanwhile, the German Ice Hockey Association (DEB) is still in discussions with the government in Berlin and the IIHF about how to proceed — or not — with hosting the Men's Ice Hockey World Championship in May.

"We intend to host the world championship in Germany next year, and I am very optimistic that we will succeed in doing so," DEB chairman Frank H. Lutz told German broadcaster MagentaSport on Saturday.

While he acknowledged the IIHF's CAS-ordered requirement to include Russia and reiterated the DEB's rejection of the court ruling, he provided no indication as to how this obstacle could be overcome.

Lutz, who stated he would be in Berlin for more consultations this week, had previously said handing back Germany's hosting rights was a possibility — if only as a last resort.

On Friday, government spokesman Stefan Kornelius said Berlin supports the DEB's efforts to find a solution.

Recent findings suggest that "However, given the boycotts that would follow Russia's readmission, that would effectively be impossible. For this reason, we intend to explore, through dialogue, how we can still ensure the tournament takes place.".

Asked at the same press conference whether Germany could problem visas to a Russian team for the tournament, a Foreign Ministry spokesman indicated that this would be difficult under restrictions presently in place.

"At a time when Russia is waging a war of aggression against Ukraine, there can be no 'normalcy' — and we will certainly not pretend that there is," said spokesperson Martin Giese.

However, he did not categorically rule out the possibility.

It has been suggested that government officials could be choosing their words carefully out of concern for Munich's chances as it bids to host the Summer Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) recently lifted its sanctions on Russian athletes and suspension of the Russian National Olympic Committee, opening the door for their return to competition despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.

The thinking goes that the IOC would expect national Olympic committees who are bidding to host an Olympic Games — like the German Olympic Sports Confederation (DOSB) — to follow its lead.

Asked whether the debate over Russia's possible involvement in a hockey tournament could affect Munich's chances, government spokesman Kornelius mentioned he didn't wish to "speculate on implications.".

Still, with the IOC set to decide in the next few weeks whether Munich advances to the next stage of the process, one has to think that the glitch could hardly have come up at a more inopportune time for the DOSB.

Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr at centre of African Player of the Year controversy as agent demands transparency

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (570 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 15:21.
  • Ismaila Sarr's agent has released a fierce criticism of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) after the Crystal Palace winger was left off the final five-man shortlist for the 2026 African Player of the Year award, demanding that the governing body publish the full voting results.
  • Sources indicate that the Senegal international enjoyed a remarkable European campaign with Palace, winning the Conference League and finishing as both the competition's leading goalscorer and its Player of the Season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 15:21.

Ismaila Sarr's agent has released a fierce criticism of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) after the Crystal Palace winger was left off the final five-man shortlist for the 2026 African Player of the Year award, demanding that the governing body publish the full voting results.

Sources indicate that the Senegal international enjoyed a remarkable European campaign with Palace, winning the Conference League and finishing as both the competition's leading goalscorer and its Player of the Season. He also scored four goals at the 2026 World Cup, equalling Roger Milla's African record for goals at a single edition of the tournament.

However, Sarr was overlooked in favour of Sadio Mane, Pape Gueye, Achraf Hakimi, Brahim Diaz and Ismael Saibari when the final shortlist was announced on Wednesday, prompting an angry response from his representative, former Premier League forward Diomansy Kamara.

Kamara, who represented Fulham, Portsmouth and West Bromwich Albion during his playing career in England, took to social media on Wednesday evening to question the credibility of the selection process.

The former Senegal international listed Sarr's achievements before demanding that CAF explain how a player with such a record could fail to make the final five.

"We demand transparency, clear criteria and the publication of the detailed voting results," Kamara wrote, before expressing his frustration with the way African football is governed.

Sarr's contribution to Palace's European success was particularly impressive. The 28-year-old scored nine goals in the Conference League, finding the net in both legs of the semi-final against Shakhtar Donetsk. His strike after just 21 seconds in the first leg also established a newly introduced record for the fastest goal in the competition's history.

Both his European triumph and his World Cup performances fell within CAF's designated assessment period, which ran from January 1 to September 15, 2026.

One possible explanation for Sarr's absence concerns the timing of the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision to restore Senegal's Africa Cup of Nations title.

Voting for the African Player of the Year award closed on November 20, four days before Senegal were officially reinstated as African champions.

Consequently, voters submitted their selections while Morocco were still officially recognised as the tournament winners, despite Senegal having prevailed on the pitch in January's final.

Industry observers note that another possibility is that support for Senegal's three leading candidates was divided. Mane was named the best player at the Africa Cup of Nations, while Gueye scored the winning goal in the final. Both had strong cases, although neither could match Sarr's individual achievements in European club football and at the World Cup.

Industry observers note that CAF has explained that the winners are determined by a voting panel drawn from several areas of African football, including national team coaches and captains, technical experts and journalists. The process is independently monitored by PricewaterhouseCoopers.

There is therefore no evidence that Sarr was deliberately excluded by the governing body. Equally, without a detailed breakdown of the votes, it is impossible to establish whether the timing of the CAS ruling or competition between Senegal's nominees materially affected his candidacy.

Industry observers note that the winner will be unveiled at the CAF Awards ceremony in Lagos on December 2. For Kamara, however, the more pressing concern is establishing how one of the most productive African players in European football failed to make the final shortlist.

Man City owners facing fresh pressure as three Premier League rivals call for forced sale

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (650 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 15:42.
  • The owners of Manchester City are facing renewed scrutiny after senior figures at three Premier League clubs reportedly called for them to be forced to sell the club in the wake of its financial breaches.
  • Industry observers note that an independent commission found City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League, relating to alleged breaches of financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 15:42.

The owners of Manchester City are facing renewed scrutiny after senior figures at three Premier League clubs reportedly called for them to be forced to sell the club in the wake of its financial breaches.

Industry observers note that an independent commission found City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League, relating to alleged breaches of financial regulations between 2009 and 2018. The club denies wrongdoing and has appealed against the verdict, with sanctions yet to be determined.

While much of the debate has centred on potential points deductions, financial penalties and the possible removal of titles, some of City's domestic rivals believe that a change of ownership would be necessary to restore confidence in the competition.

According to recent reports, should Man City's owners be forced to sell up as punishment for breaking financial rules? ? https://t.co/YfIws1lvS6.

According to BBC Sport, senior figures at three Premier League clubs have privately expressed their belief that City's Abu Dhabi owners should be compelled to relinquish control of the club.

One executive, speaking anonymously, suggested that any punishment would be inadequate if the current ownership remained in place, while also questioning the purpose of clubs funding an independent regulator if it was unwilling to intervene in such circumstances.

Recent findings suggest that the independent commission found that City had inflated revenues and concealed losses amounting to approximately £900m through commercial arrangements deemed illegitimate. The findings cover nine seasons, during which City won three Premier League titles.

City strongly dispute those conclusions, arguing that the commission's decision contains fundamental errors of law and fact. Their appeal hearing is expected to take place in December, with a verdict anticipated in the upcoming year.

In a recent development, the latest intervention from rival executives represents a significant development in the wider dispute. Even if City were handed a substantial points deduction or a financial penalty, those measures would not necessarily affect Sheikh Mansour's control of the club.

However, the power to enforce a change of ownership rests with the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), whose responsibilities extend beyond the Premier League's disciplinary framework.

Speaking before a parliamentary committee on Wednesday, IFR chairman David Kogan made it clear that the regulator would not be deterred by the prospect of taking action against one of England's most successful clubs.

"We cannot simply ignore our statutory duties in relation to a club because it happens to be of a certain size," Kogan said.

The Football Governance Act 2025 gives the regulator extensive powers over club ownership. Under Section 34, the IFR can assess whether existing owners continue to satisfy suitability requirements, including standards of honesty, integrity and financial soundness.

Recent findings suggest that should an owner be deemed unsuitable, Section 39 provides a mechanism through which the regulator can require them to relinquish their ownership within a specified period. Section 43 also allows the IFR to concern an ownership removal order and appoint independent trustees to oversee the process where the relevant legal conditions are met.

Industry observers note that such intervention would require a separate assessment of the individuals concerned. An unsuccessful appeal by Manchester City would not, in itself, automatically trigger a sale of the club.

The regulator's independence is particularly significant given Sheikh Mansour's position as vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, alongside the country's extensive economic interests in the United Kingdom.

However, Kogan has insisted that political considerations will have no bearing on the regulator's assessment of the evidence.

For now, the immediate focus remains on City's appeal against the independent commission's findings. Should the verdict be upheld, the club could find themselves facing two separate proceedings: one determining the sporting consequences of the financial breaches and another examining whether the individuals responsible for running the club remain suitable owners and directors.

Published: 03:16 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 06:39 EST, 26 November 2026.

Joshua Kimmich has hammered his own club Bayern Munich for their 'incomprehensible' and 'unacceptable' undermining of Jamal Musiala's ongoing illness battle.

Musiala, the 23-year-old golden boy of German football, has hardly played this season due to seizures brought on by 'neurological dysfunction' and has an £18m-a-year salary until 2030.

Last week, Bayern board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the club could discuss him taking a pay cut, arguing: 'We need to talk to the family, the player, and the agency, because then these sums of money, sorry, with all due respect, are no longer feasible.

‘I cannot imagine that Jamal wants to leave the club or that any other club would buy him under these conditions.'.

There was a huge outcry after Rummenigge's remarks, with the likes of Jude Bellingham, Michael Olise and Rio Ferdinand all backing Musiala.

According to recent reports, and when asked about the situation after Bayern's 2-1 defeat by Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday night, Kimmich said: 'What happened now is something that simply must never happen in this way. I find it completely incomprehensible.

Joshua Kimmich hammered Bayern Munich for their handling of Jamal Musiala's situation.

Musiala came off the bench for Bayern in their 2-1 defeat by Lille on Wednesday night.

'I think this is something that should be discussed behind closed doors, something you can address with Jamal's agent or with Jamal himself. And I think the other side is open to that as well.

Recent findings suggest that 'I believe I've also read that they've met and are supposed to issue a statement. What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated publicly. It must never happen that a player is made to bear the brunt of it.

'Of course, the club always comes first and is bigger than us as players, but it's not bigger than the person. And that's an absolute no-go. It's also not the Bayern way. Especially at this particular time, when I've often emphasised how special this club is.

Sources indicate that 'Even in my own situation, the club was incredibly special. You could really feel that this sense of togetherness was being lived out.'.

Kimmich pointed out that Musiala's health issues are in no way a result of him being unprofessional.

'We mustn't forget that he underwent another operation in the summer and then suffered another injury afterwards,' he continued.

It has been revealed that 'But I see him and spend time with him every day. I see how he works and how hard he works. That's another important aspect of the situation. It's not as though he's having problems because he's unprofessional. Quite the opposite: he's here every day, naturally wants to get the very best out of himself, works extremely hard every day and, I think, genuinely enjoys being part of our team.

'I hope he knows that all of us are 100% behind him, both the team and the club officials.'.

While Kimmich offered his support to Musiala, he admitted he did understand the difficulty the club faces financially with one of their most expensive players unable to start more than one Bundesliga game this season.

Musiala collapsed on the pitch at two consecutive games in August (pictured being helped by team-mates against RB Leipzig).

He continued: 'Generally speaking, you have to look at the situation from different perspectives. I have absolute understanding for the fact that this is not an easy situation for a club either.

Recent findings suggest that 'Of course, I've witnessed Jamal's journey over the past two years. I mean, he carried us at the Euros and was our standout player afterwards. Then he signed a contract extension, was given the number 10 shirt here and with the German national team. Then came the first muscle injury. I can speak from personal experience: when you extend your contract, especially at that age, it's not about sitting back and enjoying the next five years.

'Rather, it's a source of motivation and a responsibility you want to live up to. Then Jamal had the illness and the serious injury. We mustn't forget that over the past year and a half, I don't think he's managed to play four or five games in a row.

In a recent development, 'So it's understandable to some extent that he's not performing at his usual level. And it's also understandable that the club might be concerned because of the illness.'.

The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.

Musiala shocked the sporting world when he collapsed in two matches earlier this season, with Bayern manager Vincent Kompany explaining that the player had suffered from a reaction to a change in his medication.

Honorary president Uli Hoeness was the first to speak out on the potential drop-off in form Musiala might suffer with long-term absences, claiming earlier this month that he 'may never regain the performance level he once had'.

'We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,' Hoeness told German outlet BR24.

Both Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have made comments suggesting consequences should Musiala not return to his level.

Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen then backed up Hoeness's comments and implied that Musiala's contract may need to be 'assessed'.

It has been revealed that 'We're monitoring his level of play. He'll certainly need time to improve further – like any injured player,' Dreesen said in discussion with AZ. 'And then we need to calmly assess the situation and, if necessary, sit down with his family and management.

'Either we'll all be happy together and he'll be the same Jamal he always was – or, if he's a different Jamal along the way, we'll have to discuss it.'.

Sources indicate that 'If we're not consistently at a level that also aligns with the economic realities, then we'll have to talk to each other. Nevertheless, we have a valid contract, and that's the end of it.'.

The 23-year-old is one of Bayern's highest-earners, having signed a deal with the club to extend his time in Bavaria in February 2025.

Adding fuel to the fire days later was former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who told Sky Sports/RTL that he thought it was almost reasonable to discuss a renegotiation should Musiala not return to the level at which he once played.

But the player union Fifpro were forthright in their disagreement with his statements,  releasing a statement claiming that all parties currently sharing their views on Musiala's contract 'should know better'.

'Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession,' the statement read.

'In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.'.

When this statement was shared to social media via journalist Fabrizio Romano, global talents including Jude Bellingham and Musiala's team-mate Michael Olise were among those to like the post.

Criticisms were even more fiery in Germany, with the vice president of Germany's player union Michael Franz accusing the club of harassment.

'What the Bayern Munich officials are doing, and I don't mean Kompany and (Max) Eberl (director of sport), who have behaved impeccably, seems despicable to me,' Franz shared in an interview with Sport1. 'There is even something about it that resembles harassment.'.

'A footballer's level of performance can be discussed publicly, but it is not right to talk about his illness and the salary he receives in such circumstances. We must not forget that Jamal Musiala has done everything in his power to come back.'.

'Money has become more key than the person, and that is unacceptable.'.

Musiala collapsed twice within four days in mid-August, first during Bayern's match against Leipzig – shortly after scoring – and then against Heidenheim.

He then returned to the pitch in September, netting against Bodo/Glimt in Champions League action and Union Berlin shortly before the first international break.

After suffering a hamstring injury, Musiala then spent time away from the side before his return at the end of last week – a match which also saw Harry Kane suffer an ankle injury which will keep him out for over three months.

Musiala came off the bench on Wednesday night against Lille and managed to play the final 15 minutes of the 2-1 defeat.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Virgil van Dijk is now in the final year of his Liverpool contract.

The Dutchman has been one of the Reds' best players since he joined in 2017 and, without him, Liverpool wouldn't have won half as much as they have.

However, by the time the 2027-28 season kicks off, the Dutchman will be 36 years old and will be entering the twilight stages of his career.

Indeed, he did hit his prime a bit later than most players so he could continue playing at the top level for a while.

But, because the Reds can't be sure of this, they're holding back on offering the Dutchman a newly introduced deal for now.

Many different centre-backs have been linked with Liverpool as their next Virgil van Dijk but, there's one stand-out candidate who the Reds have just been handed a massive boost to sign.

Barcelona want to sign Ayden Heaven which could give Liverpool a clear run at Nico Schlotterbeck.

Liverpool, Barcelona and Manchester United have all been fairly intertwined with transfer links recently.

All three teams seem to want the same players in the same positions and, while one of them are bound to end up signing them, they'll drive the price up for each other which doesn't really make much sense.

However, since most of the world's biggest clubs all want to sign the best players, these links are rarely ever going to die down but, fortunately for Liverpool, Barcelona seem to have turned their attention away from Nico Schlotterbeck.

That is, if this latest revision from BBC Sport is to be believed.

"Fulham and Barcelona are among the clubs to have expressed an interest in Heaven, with both having tried to sign him when he decided to leave Arsenal," they wrote.

"The England U20s defender's preference is believed to be a loan move, though he would also entertain permanent offers.

According to recent reports, "At United he has largely been used as a back-up option and, after enjoying a run in the team under former manager Ruben Amorim, he lost his place under Michael Carrick. He returned to the side only after an injury crisis hit the club last season.

"Heaven is also capable of playing at left-back and in midfield, but does not expect to be trusted as a regular starter amid the instability at Old Trafford, with the club 19th in the league.

"He is under contract until 2029 in a deal that includes an option for an extra year.".

Nico Schlotterbeck is who Liverpool need to replace Virgil van Dijk.

One of the best things about Schlotterbeck is the fact that he's left-footed.

The German can also be used as a centre-back or a left-back if needed.

His entire career has been spent in Germany but, most of his experience of competitions such as the Champions League have come with Borussia Dortmund.

Last summer, he signed a latest contract with the German outfit but, there is a release clause in his contract for certain clubs across the globe, including Liverpool.

The exact price of this clause is unknown but, the fact that Liverpool are one of them means that he clearly wants to make the move.

He's also only 26 years old so, even though he has plenty of experience under his belt, there's still room for him to grow.

Here's hoping that Liverpool get this deal over the line, especially now that Barcelona seem to be turning their attention away from him.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Quantum metrology promises measurement precision beyond classical limits by exploiting large-scale quantum states1,2,3,4,5,6,7, yet realizing this advantage faces two fundamental challenges: the deterministic preparation of non-trivial quantum probes8,9 and the efficient extraction of metrological information in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces10,11,12.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quantum metrology promises measurement precision beyond classical limits by exploiting large-scale quantum states1,2,3,4,5,6,7, yet realizing this advantage faces two fundamental challenges: the deterministic preparation of non-trivial quantum probes8,9 and the efficient extraction of metrological information in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces10,11,12. Here, we introduce quantum confocal microscopy in Fock space that addresses these challenges for a Fock-like probe state with a tightly concentrated photon-number distribution. Drawing a direct analogy between classical wave optics and quantum state evolution in a bosonic mode13,14, we construct a confocal lens system with a quantum circuit of \({\mathcal{O}}(1)\) operational depth, realizing a bidirectional transformation between a readily obtainable coherent state and this Fock-like probe state. Using a superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamics platform, we deterministically prepare focused probe states with mean photon numbers up to N = 500, achieving a 21.5 ± 1.1 dB reduction of the photon-number variance relative to a coherent state. Using the focused states for displacement sensing, we achieve a record metrological gain of 19.20 ± 0.20 dB beyond the standard quantum limit. This work establishes quantum confocal microscopy as a compact protocol that makes high-photon-number non-Gaussian Fock-like probes experimentally accessible and measurable, providing a viable route towards quantum-enhanced precision measurement, and is readily extendable to other bosonic platforms and high-dimensional quantum many-body systems.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 27 Nov 2026 16:12.

Merseyside and Manchester clubs headline gameweek 12 of the 2026-27 Premier League campaign, which kicks off on Friday night when struggling Nottingham Forest and struggling Chelsea collide at the City Ground.

Only three matches are on the Saturday menu, but one is especially significant, as Mauricio Pochettino seeks his first win as Manchester United manager at the third attempt when the Red Devils welcome Brentford to Old Trafford.

Leeds United tackle Coventry City at Elland Road in the only other 3pm Saturday kickoff, before Aston Villa try to stop the rot away to newly-promoted Ipswich Town at Portman Road.

Six games then take centre stage on Sunday, starting with the second-ever Premier League Merseyside derby at the Hill Dickinson Stadium between Everton and high-flying Liverpool.

Four fixtures will then be fought at 2.05pm involving the four Europa League and Conference League competitors; Sunderland meet Tottenham Hotspur at the Stadium of Light, Thomas Frank's Crystal Palace host Hull City, Brighton & Hove Albion aim to get their shock title charge back on track at home to Newcastle United, and Bournemouth seek a sensational 11th win on the spin when they travel to Fulham.

Last but by no means least, champions Arsenal and challengers Manchester City - who are separated by two places and six points in the Premier League table - close out the gameweek with an unmissable battle at the Emirates Stadium.

Here, Sports Mole provides a comprehensive Premier League team news list for gameweek 12, highlighting every injured, doubtful and suspended player.

Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study reveals

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (472 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a newly introduced study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.

According to recent reports, emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change. While over the past decade, these emissions have risen by 0.9% per year, they are expected to drop by 0.4% in 2026.

"It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," remarked the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.

"So in a way, a little bit of good news, but for the wrong reasons.".

The study was released while global leaders are meeting in Turkey for the United Nations' COP31 climate conference.

Sources indicate that the study published by international research group the Global Carbon Project found that oil emissions dropped by 1.9% in 2026, while natural gas fell by 0.3%. Coal emissions however continued to rise, by around 0.6%.

"A drop in emissions in ‌one year is not a peak unless it ‌is driven ​by structural change," Peters cautioned.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that A structural change would mean that emissions would slowly rise to a peak and then slowly decline afterward, indicating a long term trend. That's not what happened though, Peters remarked. "What we see this year is [that] oil emissions are going up and then suddenly, bang, down 2%.".

It is the third time in recent years that global carbon pollution has dropped. The previous declines were during the global economic crisis in 2009 and during the COVID pandemic in 2020. In each of those cases, emissions went back up once global economies recovered.

In a recent development, while the geopolitical shocks of the past year have been the driving factors behind the temporary emissions reversal, there has also been a rise in renewable energy contributing to the data. So while solar panels, wind farms and electric vehicles did make a difference, they were just not enough to cut emissions by themselves.

"The long-term answer remains the rapid deployment of clean energy technologies," according to co-author of the study, Pierre Friedlingstein, of the Global Carbon Budget Office at the University.

In a recent development, and even though emissions from fossil fuels dropped slightly, overall global carbon dioxide emissions still went up by about 1%, the study warns. The overall rise is because of land use changes like deforestation and peat fires, which increased too fast to be offset by the slight decrease in fossil fuel burning.

#164761. Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough

Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough

📅 18 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5006 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet.
  • According to recent reports, in the end it also points to another thing.
  • What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

According to recent reports, in the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously noted of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”.

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

It has been revealed that defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

That is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

The hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Sources indicate that ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

We have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick said this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

In a recent development, having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it looked like they had been knocked to the floor for good in the Europa League, AC Milan got up and produced a stunning response in Greece.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin their analysis this morning by writing that Milan highlighted their ‘true Italian colours in Europe at last’ in a ‘magnificent, incredible performance’. It took a while to get going, with two goals from the home side needed as a wake-up call, but it worked.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Sources indicate that ruben Amorim reshaped his side and they produced epic comeback, turning a 0–2 deficit into a 4–2 victory, with the Rossoneri suddenly appearing courageous, aggressive, and dominant. For one night, Omari Hutchinson was the god of Athens, with his Messi-like goal and two assists.

In stoppage time, the tireless Diego Moreira also got on the scoresheet. It’s a massive boost to both energy and morale, putting the team back into the play-off places. There is more work to be done, but it feels like a start.

Also worth examining is the Milan side seen in the first half and the beginning of the second, a period when Joao Silva’s quick goal to make it 2-0 threatened to turn into yet another cursed night.

The Rossoneri were off the pace again, completely at the mercy of Olympiacos’s frenetic pace and 4-2-3-1 formation, which hemmed them into the final thirty metres and stifled any chance of a counter-attack.

It was a case of no Luke Modric, no party. In truth, one counter did materialise, coming down the left flank. Despite being off-balance, the ever-present Cissé managed to get a shot on target from the ground, only for Pirola – an Italian playing in Greece – to clear it off the line.

Milan need to be built around Cissé, but in the first half it was Goncalo Ramos who occupied the centre of the 3-4-2-1, functioning less as a ‘false nine’ and more as a centre-forward who simply wasn’t there, much like the team-mates who should have been supporting him.

In a recent development, milan got off to a poor start. Entrusting the protection of the midfield to the Jashari-Rabiot duo – neither of whom are a true defensive specialist – proved to be a questionable strategy against Freuler and Gustavo Sà.

In truth, the whole side struggled. Hutchinson was ineffective as a right-sided attacking midfielder; Cissé was never brought into play on the opposite flank; and Estupiñán – tasked with a hybrid role as both full-back and wing-back – looked completely flat on the left.

In a recent development, amorim’s tactical experiments backfired, not least because De Winter was far from flawless at the back, while Diawara appeared somewhat naive. At the other end, Pirola looked every bit the Achilles among the Greeks.

He scored the opening goal with a header (officially recorded by UEFA as an own goal, as the ball ricocheted off the crossbar and then Maignan), and later made a crucial intervention to deny Cissé.

Sources indicate that one could have held endless debates over why Milan wins five out of six matches in Italy, yet was on the verge of a fourth defeat in Europe. Arguments about the ‘pace of European competition’ feel a bit reductive: fair enough regarding Benfica, but we are talking about Ferencváros and Olympiacos.

According to recent reports, milan simply needed to restore their balance. Amorim took drastic measures: he brought on Yunus Musah to bolster the midfield and Pulisic to inject energy into the attack, while taking off Estupiñán and Ramos (the latter due to a knock), effectively reshaping the entire side.

In defence, Mario Gila and Koni De Winter remained (though Fikayo Tomori, who soon replaced the latter, performed much better), joined by Sankhoun Diawara. In the middle, Hutchinson and Moreira took the flanks, while the well-balanced duo of Jashari and Musah took control of the centre.

Up front, Rabiot and Pulisic flanked Cissé. When Jota Silva made it 2–0 just four minutes in, it seemed as though there was no effective remedy, but it was merely a matter of regrouping.

Moving away from his hybrid role as an attacking midfielder/central midfielder, Hutchinson transformed into a devastating wide player. In the 11th minute of the second half he won the ball in midfield, embarks on a brilliant slalom run and found the bottom corner.

Industry observers note that from that moment on, the Greek side effectively disappeared from the match. They ran around aimlessly, lacking any tactical cohesion or ideas, while their manager Alguacil faltered with his substitutions.

It has been revealed that the equaliser came from Cissé, who headed home a pinpoint assist from Hutchinson after more good work on the right. It was his tenth goal of the season (four in the Europa League, six in Serie A): when Cissé plays he scores, simple as that.

Recent findings suggest that the 3-2 goal arrived courtesy of Pulisic, who executed a stunning mid-air half-volley, once again set up by the Englishman. Pulisic himself squanders a chance to make it 4-2 on the counter-attack, but Moreira eventually sealed the deal in the closing seconds.

Industry observers note that it can’t be said that ‘we’ve found the real Milan’ even after the comeback, not with a Milan that possesses so many different identities. It’s clear that Ramos needs to reflect, but the urgent need for points suggests it’s time for Cissé and Pulisic.

Recent findings suggest that A defensive-minded player is a must in a two-man midfield. If Hutchison is such a dynamo on the right, then Moreira could perhaps be ‘sacrificed’ on the left. And at the back, maybe Tomori was cast aside a bit too soon.

Half the squad is sidelined with injuries, yet there are more resources available than one might imagine. Six points is not enough: the team need another six from their last three games to make the knockouts. The night in Piraeus, however, is a start.

By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 16:17.

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has insisted that Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior are subject to the same selection criteria as the rest of his squad, warning that any dissatisfaction with being named on the bench is a matter for the players themselves.

The Portuguese manager was questioned about the status of his attacking stars during Friday's press conference ahead of Saturday's La Liga encounter with Alaves at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Industry observers note that madrid's recent improvement has coincided with Bellingham's excellent form and a resurgence from Vinicius, who has faced increased competition for his place following the summer arrival of Yan Diomande. Mourinho, however, believes that the collective spirit he has established since returning to the Spanish capital is helping him manage those individual ambitions.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Mourinho dismissed the suggestion that certain members of his squad enjoy preferential treatment.

"If one day they are on the bench and they don't like it, that's their problem," noted the former Chelsea and Manchester United manager, who stressed that Mbappe, Bellingham and Vinicius were on an equal footing with their teammates.

Industry observers note that mourinho acknowledged that Mbappe has yet to start a match on the bench this season, while Bellingham has only done so once. He explained that the difference in playing time between the pair and other members of the squad was justified by their performances.

Mbappe has registered 19 goals and five assists in 18 appearances across all competitions this season, while Bellingham demonstrated his importance to the team once again in Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.

Madrid were trailing at half time when Mourinho introduced the England international, who subsequently scored a superb goal and provided the assist for Vinicius to complete the scoring.

It has been revealed that such performances help explain why Mourinho has been reluctant to rest either player. The Portuguese nevertheless insisted that the team's objectives take precedence over individual ambitions and expressed satisfaction at how his players have accepted that principle.

The debate surrounding Madrid's attacking options has intensified in recent weeks, with Vinicius returning to form after a difficult start to the campaign and a four-match La Liga suspension.

The Brazilian made an key contribution from the bench in last weekend's 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo before finding the net against PSV, giving Mourinho another selection decision to make ahead of the Alaves fixture.

However, Mourinho rejected the idea that Vinicius and Diomande should be regarded as rivals, explaining that both players share the same objectives and that the Brazilian has retained the support of his teammates throughout his difficult spell.

The Madrid boss also dismissed concerns about the atmosphere within the dressing room, revealing that he has not encountered any significant problems during his first five months back at the club.

His satisfaction with the current squad extends to his aims for the January transfer window, with Mourinho making it clear that he would prefer to finish the season with the players already at his disposal.

"I don't want anyone to leave either; the door is closed," the Portuguese explained after ruling out the need for new signings.

According to recent reports, that stance is particularly noteworthy given the limited opportunities afforded to some of Madrid's younger attacking players. With Rodrygo also working his way back from a long-term injury, competition for places could become even greater during the second half of the campaign.

Mourinho's comments suggest that he would rather manage that competition internally than reduce his attacking options midway through a season in which Madrid are competing for honours on several fronts.

#164755. Industry News: Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1002 w)
